title: North Macedonia’s BESS market begins to develop - Energy Storage
content: North Macedonia has begun constructing battery energy storage systems (BESS) this year, according to analysis from Macedonian solar energy association Solar Macedonia. Professor Dimitar Dimitrov, from Skopje’s Ss. Cyril and Methodius University and Solar Macedonia, told pv magazine some of these projects are standalone battery storage systems, while a significant number involve the integration of battery storage to existing PV plants. “The main objective of adding battery storage to existing PV facilities is to enable energy arbitrage by storing electricity during periods of low market prices and selling it during higher-price periods,” Dimitrov explained. “This can improve the overall economic performance of PV projects, increase their revenues and consequently strengthen the investment case and shorten the payback period.” Statistics from earlier in the year put North Macedonia’s installed solar capacity at above 1 GW. In February, the country’s Ministry of Energy, Mining and Mineral Resources approved 59 solar projects with a combined capacity over 3 GW under its 2026 annual energy construction plan. The construction plan also approved 96 energy storage facilities, including 77 integrated systems linked to new or existing plans and 19 standalone units, with a combined capacity of 2.2 GW/4.9 GWh. Dimitrov said that during the remainder of 2026, the administrative procedures for utility-scale PV and BESS projects that are already in the national plans and have already received grid-connection approval are expected to speed up, allowing these projects to start construction in 2027. “At the same time, C&I PV and BESS projects are expected to continue with development,” Dimitrov continued. “The main driver is the growing interest of C&I consumers in reducing their electricity costs, improving energy security and making better use of the renewable energy they produce by themselves.” Dimitrov also said the introduction of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, which adds additional carbon-related costs to electricity exports to EU countries, is creating additional challenges, even for renewable energy investments. “As a result, electricity producers are mainly dependent on the domestic market and on exports to non-EU countries in the region,” Dimitrov explained. “This is particularly challenging for solar PV projects. Solar generation is highest around noon hours. Consequently, in these hours electricity markets have a significant surplus of supply, leading to lower electricity prices, reducing the revenues of PV plants and making new investments less attractive.” Dimitrov added that drought conditions and low Danube water levels that started towards the end of July have contributed to higher regional electricity prices. “[This has appeared] to be favorable for the economic viability of PV plants even in North Macedonia by increasing revenues from electricity generation,” Dimitrov told pv magazine. Last month, Chinese construction conglomerate PowerChina was selected to implement a 30 MW solar project in North Macedonia for state-owned power utility Elektrani na Severna Makedonija (ESM). The project, awarded through a European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) tender administered in late 2024, is split into two sites, a 10 MW installation at an exhausted coal mine belonging to the Oslomej thermal power plant and a 20 MW array near the Bitola thermal power plant. Earlier this year, pv magazine spoke to Dimitrov about North Macedonia’s gigawatt-sized project pipeline of renewable energy projects during Intersolar in Munich. title: Samsung secures grid clearance for 400 MWh battery in Australia - Energy Storage
content: The Australian renewables and energy storage arm of Samsung has received formal grid connection clearance for the Mangoplah battery energy storage project being developed near Wagga Wagga in New South Wales. The 5.3.4A letter, issued by the Australian Energy Market Operator, confirms that the facility satisfies the technical conditions required for the battery to connect to the National Electricity Market (NEM). The project comprises a 100 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage system being developed on a 10.5-hectare site near the township of Mangoplah, about 30 km south of Wagga Wagga. The facility would connect directly into the 132 kV electricity transmission network that traverses the site. According to Samsung C&T Renewable Energy Australia, the BESS will provide system strength services to the transmission and distribution networks in the area, helping to provide security of supply and safeguard the energy network. “Energy storage technologies can unlock electricity generation growth in areas experiencing network constraints,” the company said in its scoping report. “They will also support on-demand energy needs as the network transitions to more renewable sources of energy.” The 5.3.4 letter comes after the Mangoplah project in was given the all-clear under the federal government’s EPBC Act with the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) determining the development is “not a controlled action.” Samsung has previously indicated that, subject to the necessary approvals, construction of the Mangoplah facility is expected to begin in 2027. Commercial operations will likely start in 2028 or 2029, depending on the approval process. The Mangoplah project is part of Samsung C&T’s growing renewable energy portfolio in Australia. The company is currently working on several other standalone batteries  and solar and battery projects across the country. These include a 200 MW/800 MWh Romani battery project in southwest of NSW and the 80 MW/320 MWh South Coree battery project in the state’s Riverina Murray region. Samsung C&T is also involved with the 1,000 MW Western Giga Energy hydrogen concept proposed for Geraldton in Western Australia. is launching a new Denza Z9 GT model on September 9. The new tri-motor variant is expected to start at around $50,000, filling the gap between the current range-topping Performance and Flagship RWD models.

revealing the new Z9 GT

title: ENGWE’s new E26 3.0 e-bike packs dual motors, full suspension, and half a deer
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 8 2026 - 3:22 am PT
ENGWE has just launched its latest all-terrain electric bike, the E26 3.0, and the company is going big on power this time around. The new model combines dual hub motors, full suspension, and chunky fat tires into a bike that looks designed to handle just about anything you can throw at it.
While ENGWE has plenty of
commuter-focused models
, this new launch appears to be designed for the dirt – and has the power to match it.
The ENGWE E26 3.0 uses a pair of hub motors rated for a combined 2,000W of peak power, with ENGWE claiming up to 160 Nm of torque.
That dual-motor setup gives riders the option of putting down considerably more power than you’d find on a typical commuter-oriented electric bicycle, especially when climbing loose or steep terrain.
I assume there’s some AI at work in this marketing image, or else they’re coming back for the rest of the deer later
The top speed is listed at 28 mph (45 km/h) on throttle and 31 mph (50 km/h) under pedal assist.
Stored power comes from a fairly sizable 48V and 20Ah battery, giving the bike 960Wh of capacity. ENGWE claims up to 100 miles (161 km) of range when using a single motor in the lowest pedal assist setting, or 70 miles (113 km) with both motors active. As usual, those are best-case figures, and riders making liberal use of both motors should expect significantly less range. Either way you slice it though, that’s still a pretty big battery.
It’s worth pointing out that the E26 3.0’s dual-motor power level and top speeds on both throttle and pedal assist put it outside the typical Class 1/2/3 e-bike framework used across much of the US. Riders should check their local and state regulations to determine where a bike with this level of performance can legally be ridden.
That distinction may be somewhat less important for the type of riding ENGWE appears to be targeting here. The E26 3.0 is clearly positioned as an all-terrain machine, and on private property or other areas without e-bike classification restrictions, its street-legal classification isn’t necessarily as critical as it would be for a bike primarily designed for commuting. Public trails are another matter, of course, particularly those that specifically restrict access to Class 1, 2, or 3 e-bikes.
The rest of the bike is similarly geared toward all-terrain riding. There are 26 x 4-inch puncture-resistant fat tires, a 120mm travel front suspension fork, and 80mm of adjustable rear air suspension. Hydraulic disc brakes with large 203mm rotors provide the stopping power.
There’s also a 3.5-inch full-color display, integrated LED lighting, rear rack, and a claimed payload capacity of 400 lb (181 kg). At 85.9 lb (39 kg), though, this definitely isn’t the kind of e-bike you’re going to enjoy carrying up a flight of stairs. Even getting it into the back of a truck is going to either be a partner job or a concerted effort with some focused bracing.
The ENGWE E26 3.0 is
launching at $1,799
, discounted from a listed $2,399 MSRP. At that price, you’re getting an impressive amount of hardware: dual motors, nearly 1 kWh of battery, full suspension, hydraulic brakes, fat tires, and a fender package.
It’s certainly not a lightweight or subtle e-bike, but that’s not really the point. ENGWE appears to have built the E26 3.0 for riders who would rather have too much motor than not enough – and for
, they’re getting quite a lot of it. Just remember to ride it where you’re permitted!

title: Plug-in Hybrids emit 6x more pollution than claimed, and they're getting dirtier
content:
A new study shows that the gap between real-world pollution from plug-in hybrids and official government estimates is getting wider – and worse, plug-in hybrids themselves are getting dirtier.
And the car lobby is trying to hide it, and make it harder to regulate the pollution coming out of these vehicles.
The evolution of transportation takes many forms, and we here at Electrek like to cover most of them. It leads to all sorts of weird acronyms – BEV, PHEV, EREV, FCEV, HEV and so on.
Here, we’re talking about the PHEVs. Plug-in hybrid vehicles.
PHEVs are cars that have a significantly sized battery which can be filled up by plugging in, unlike conventional hybrids, which get all their energy from gasoline and merely recapture some of it during braking. Some have bigger batteries than others, but most of them can run on pure battery mode at least for some reasonable number of miles.
Plug-in hybrids are often thought of as a “transitional” technology between fully fossil-powered vehicles and fully electrically-powered ones, because you can use either as a fuel source. More flexibility means you can use whatever fuel source is more convenient for your current application.
It seems like a “best of both worlds” situation at first look… but there are downsides. PHEVs are more mechanically complex, and often one or both of the powertrains will be cobbled together as an afterthought, leading to a compromised vehicle overall.
And then, there’s the pollution, which turns out to be far higher in the real world than anyone wants to admit.
We’ve covered many, many studies showing that PHEVs are dirtier than expected, and now Transport & Environment (T&E) is out with a new update showing that not only is the gap between real-world and laboratory emissions growing for EU PHEVs, but PHEVs are getting dirtier over time, rather than cleaner.
PHEVs are now 6x dirtier than testing indicates
The analysis is an update of T&E’s previous work, showing a trend of PHEV emissions testing estimates getting less and less realistic over time.
The new update uses data from 220,000 PHEVs in Europe. Europe has mandated fuel use monitoring on vehicles, called the “On Board Fuel Consumption Monitoring” (OBFCM) system. This allows for much better real-world data, which can then be compared against laboratory data to see how cars use fuel in the real world, rather than tests (which, as we have learned, can be gamed).
T&E analyzed this data and found that PHEV emissions rose from 138 gCO2/km in 2023 to 145 gCO2/km in 2024, an increase of 5% in a year. Needless to say, this is going in the wrong direction.
In fact, 145 gCO2/km is only 14% less than the average for fossil-fueled vehicles, meaning in the real world, PHEVs are only barely cleaner.
Not only is this going in the wrong direction, but government testing indicated over the same period that PHEVs should have gotten cleaner. But in the real world, they didn’t. So what’s going on here?
It’s about “utility factors”
Since PHEVs have two powertrains with vastly different pollution profiles (one of which produces no tailpipe pollution, and one which is responsible for the hurricanes and wildfires ravaging the planet and millions of deaths per year), any testing has to estimate how often you’re going to use each of those powertrains.
So government includes a “utility factor” calculation for how often it thinks battery power will be used. And those utility factors are way, way off.
It turns out that people just don’t plug PHEVs in. (Although, that said, even when running on electric mode, PHEVs use 3x more gas than claimed)
This happens for various reasons, and the amount that it happens differs from territory to territory and from car to car. But in every study we’ve seen, whether in EU (where OBFCM data is available, and thus these studies are more common) or in the USA, the common fact is that tests always underestimate the pollution that PHEVs put out. On the better-designed PHEVs, if you do plug them in all the time, they can be much cleaner than a gas car… but people just don’t do it.
Car lobby wants to keep numbers wrong to keep selling you engines
With all these studies showing PHEVs to be dirtier than we thought, it would make sense for government to act and fix the estimates (and for automakers to make PHEVs that are more worth plugging in, as some of the above-linked studies have suggested).
Updating testing is precisely the plan – as the gap between testing and real-world emissions has been rising, the EU has planned to update “utility factors” to better reflect the reality of how people use their vehicles.
But the problem with that is that if Europe finally more realistically accounts for the real-world pollution coming out of these vehicles, auto manufacturers wouldn’t be able to get as much unearned “extra credit” for selling polluting gas-powered cars with a small battery and plug attached. This would be a threat to their greenwashing, and they can’t have it.
So automakers have consistently lobbied the EU to weaken updates to utility factors, which would allow their vehicles to continue polluting, but allow them to continue patting themselves on the back for greening their fleet when they have done no such thing.
Test numbers don’t matter, the real harm done is what matters
To be clear: pollution matters in the real world because of the health problems it causes for everyone, and because of its contribution to climate change. Neither of those damages care about what the gamed testing numbers say. If you breathe pollution, you breathe it either way, even if the automakers lie to you and tell you that the air was clean.
We’ve been through something similar before – Dieselgate. In that instance, VW (and, uh, basically everyone else) lied to the tests while polluting more in the real world. This is part of why we have OBFCM in the first place – so we don’t have to rely on the tests, and we can know what’s going on in the real world. And here we are, just a decade later, falling to the same lies.
Top comment by Spencer Hodges
The technical reason is two fold. First, yes people don't actually plug them in as expected. But this just turns them into a conventional hybrid. And hybrids pollute more than expected largely because of the catalytic converter not maintaining operational temperatures. At its operational temp of hundreds of degrees Celsius, it can be >90% efficient in conversion of NOx, HC and CO. But during the warm up period, the catalyst barely does anything. And in hybrids, it's possible for the catalyst to never reach operational temperatures. It's a real problem.
Further, as pointed out by Lucien Mathieu from T&E, these sorts of delays harm the European auto industry.
“Plug-in hybrids are one of the auto industry’s greatest greenwashing stunts – marketed as a green solution, yet delivering a heavy environmental toll in practice. They are also a major rip-off for consumers, who end up paying far more for fuel than expected. Carmakers are demanding that the EU turn a blind eye so it can delay investing in fully electric cars. Utility factors were designed to make official emission match with real-world; they are evidence-based policy making. If Europe wants to keep a chance to compete with China in the global EV race, it must resist any attempt to weaken the utility factors.”
Automakers have used this PHEV “extra credit” to delay deploying pure EV cars – they’ll add a small battery to an ICE car, get bonus points for doing very little, and continue on without updating their cars to what the state of the art of the industry can actually provide. Meanwhile, Chinese automakers are rapidly deploying new EVs, and those are gaining share in Europe and across the glove rapidly, displacing European-made cars. If Europe wants to keep up, it needs to stop deluding itself and start confronting reality.
Can we please learn a lesson for once, and stop trusting the automakers when we know they’re lying?

title: Polestar confirms Formula 2030 concept previewing next Polestar 2 and 7
content:
Polestar
Polestar 2
Fred Lambert
| Sep 8 2026 - 5:42 am PT
The Polestar Formula 2030 concept car. Source: Polestar
Polestar has confirmed a new concept car, the Formula 2030, and it’s the clearest look yet at where the Swedish EV brand’s design is headed.
The concept previews styling that will show up on the next Polestar 2, due in 2027, and the Polestar 7 compact SUV coming in 2028. It’s also the design centerpiece of a broader strategy the company is pitching to investors around one goal: getting to profit.
A bold evolution, not a redesign
The Formula 2030 is the first full design statement from Philipp Romers, who
took over as Polestar’s head of design
in 2024 after arriving from Audi and replacing Maximilian Missoni.
Romers isn’t tearing up the playbook. “It was obvious we needed a bold evolution not revolution of what came before,” he said, pointing to the “Dual Blade” headlights that stay front and center on the concept so it “remains recognizably a Polestar.”
The Formula 2030 previews the design of the next Polestar 2 and Polestar 7. Source: Polestar
You can see it in the images. The front end keeps the split-blade light signature Polestar has run since the Polestar 2, and the profile is the same low, long-roof fastback shape the brand has leaned on. This is a refinement of a look that’s already on the road, not a reinvention.
That’s a reasonable call. Polestar’s design has always been one of its stronger cards, and the company doesn’t have the money right now to gamble on a radical reset.
Tied to the “Formula 2030” strategy
Polestar didn’t reveal the concept at a motor show. It showed it behind closed doors to investors, retailers, and a group of VIP customers at “The Cube,” its Gothenburg headquarters, as part of a “Formula 2030 strategy event.”
Polestar showed the concept at a strategy event at its Gothenburg HQ. Source: Polestar
The concept is being sold internally as proof the product pipeline is on track, and it’s landing at a moment when Polestar badly needs that story to hold up. The company says the strategy is meant “to continue business growth and drive to profitability.”
The showcar gets its public debut later this year, riding along with the media launch of the Polestar 4 SUV.
The numbers behind the pitch
Polestar is coming off a record first half on volume and a still-ugly bottom line. It delivered 30,423 vehicles in H1 2026, its best-ever first half, but posted a net loss of $842 million on revenue of $1.36 billion, which was down 4% year over year. Gross margin sat at -8%.
The losses are narrowing, which is the point Polestar wants investors focused on. The H1 net loss shrank 29% from a year earlier, and the company has been cutting the gap for several quarters. But it’s still losing money on every car at the gross level, and it recently trimmed its full-year delivery guidance.
There’s also a hole in the map. Polestar effectively lost the US market after it was
barred from selling there under the federal Chinese-connected-vehicle rule
, which hits cars with Chinese software and manufacturing ties. That’s a big chunk of premium-EV demand the brand now can’t touch, and it makes Europe the center of the whole plan.
The next Polestar 2 and the Polestar 7 are the two products meant to carry that plan. Polestar has said the
7 will replace the 2 as its entry point
and target Europe’s largest EV segment, and it’s part of a wave of
four new models the company is pushing out over three years
Electrek’s Take
A design concept is the cheapest, safest thing a struggling automaker can put out, and I don’t mean that as an insult. Polestar can’t afford a splashy new factory reveal or a moonshot product right now, so showing off a sharp evolution of a design language people already like is their move to play.
The substance is still the next Polestar 2 and the Polestar 7. Those are the cars that decide whether “Formula 2030” is a real turnaround or a nice slide deck.
The trend line is going the right way. Losses are shrinking, H1 volume was a record, and the product cadence is genuinely aggressive for a company this size. But “drive to profitability” has been the plan for years, and the goalpost keeps moving.
The good news is that Geely doesn’t appear to be giving up on Polestar.

title: Tesla Cybercab has a hidden virtual joystick to drive it manually
content:
Tesla Cybercab
Fred Lambert
| Sep 8 2026 - 7:48 am PT
A Tesla Cybercab rider found something in the robotaxi: a manual driving mode. When he got in, the touchscreen was showing a virtual joystick to drive the car by hand.
Tesla built the Cybercab with no steering wheel and no pedals. But it apparently still has a way to drive it manually, and you do it by dragging a finger across a screen.
Matthew Skrzypczak posted a video on X on September 7 showing his Cybercab in an unusual state.
“When I got in the vehicle, the display was in a different configuration with a virtual joystick for manual driving,” he wrote, adding that he had “a feeling I wasn’t supposed to see this” and then tried to drive the car with it anyway.
#cybercab
situation! When I got in the vehicle, the display was in a different configuration with a virtual joystick for manual driving! I have a feeling I wasn’t supposed to see this… but I try to manually drive the vehicle anyway! 😂
@wholemars
@DirtyTesLa
@DavidMoss
The clip shows the Cybercab’s single touchscreen split in two. The left side is a driving interface built around an on-screen joystick, with a prompt to “Close cabin doors” and buttons for opening the doors and calling support. The right side shows a live surround-camera view of the car parked in what looks like a parking lot – though the side cameras appear to be frozen on a frame from a previous location at a Supercharger.
What it shows is the workaround Tesla built for a car with no physical controls. A Cybercab still has to be moved by a person sometimes, whether that’s repositioning it in a depot or nudging it out of a tight spot, and with no wheel and no pedals, an on-screen joystick is how you do it. Tesla has never shown this mode publicly.
A robotaxi with “almost” no controls
Tesla launched the Cybercab in Austin on September 3, and that same day
NHTSA opened an audit
into how it certified a vehicle with no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors. The agency wants to know whether Tesla was right to decide that certain federal safety standards simply don’t apply to a driverless car. That probe covers roughly 1,000 vehicles.
The pitch has always been that the Cybercab doesn’t need manual controls because it drives itself. Yet here’s manual control, buried in a menu.
And Tesla has already left the door open to more. Back in October, chair Robin Denholm
said the car could get real controls
if it had to: “If we have to have a steering wheel, it can have a steering wheel and pedals.”
We have seen many Cybercab prototypes equipped with a steering wheel and pedals during the test phase.
Electrek’s Take
A touchscreen joystick is fine for creeping a car across a parking lot at walking speed, but those controls honestly look awful to use. It’s not a serious answer to the question regulators are actually asking, which is what happens when a driverless car needs a human and there’s no real way for one to take over.
Tesla removed the wheel and pedals to make a point, that full autonomy is here and manual controls are obsolete. And yet, it has yet to scale its robotaxi service, which has been in operation for more than year with Model Ys, which use the same autonomous hardware and software as the Cybercab, which is ultimately just a different form factor.

title: Toyota is recalling about 10,000 C-HR EVs
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 8 2026 - 8:25 am PT
issued a recall involving around 10,000 electric C-HR vehicles. The recall stems from a potential loss of power while driving.
What to know about the Toyota C-HR EV recall
The all-electric C-HR is one of three electric SUVs Toyota now sells in North America, alongside the updated bZ and bZ Woodland.
It went on sale earlier this year, starting at about $37,000, as a smaller, sportier alternative to
, Toyota’s first electric SUV.
While the new C-HR EV is off to a promising start, the electric crossover is already facing its first recall.
Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR vehicles in North America. While details are still limited at this point, Toyota said about 10,000 C-HR models are involved in the recall.
The issue stems from a software glitch with the regenerative braking system. Under certain conditions, when the battery is fully charged or has a high charge level, the regenerative braking system can overcharge it.
Toyota C-HR EV (Source: Toyota)
When this happens, the electric drive system can shut down, causing the vehicle to lose power while driving.
Owners of affected vehicles can take them to a Toyota dealership, where technicians will update the battery ECU (electronic control unit) software.
2026 Toyota C-HR EV XSE interior (Source: Toyota)
Toyota will notify owners in early November 2026. The recall has not yet been released on the
website, so details are still limited. We should learn more soon. Check back for the latest updates.
In the meantime, owners can contact Toyota’s Brand Engagement Center at 1-800-331-4331. To see whether your vehicle is involved, visit
or, when it becomes available, nhtsa.gov/recalls and enter your VIN or license plate number.
Only the 2026 C-HR model year is affected. The
2027 Toyota C-HR
is also on sale now.

近日，宁德时代在产业链上下游同步展开动作，一方面与泰金新能、深圳惠科等企业达成战略合作，重构锂电铜箔供应链；另一方面通过旗下B2B平台“宁德时代商城”开启全球开放月促销，加速渗透中小储能集成商市场。
上游：联合装备与材料商重构铜箔供应链
在装备端，宁德时代与泰金新能建立统一统筹、统一标准、统一集中采购管理机制。泰金新能为新扩建项目提供标准化、规模化集中交付，推动装备端系统性降本与技术迭代升级。
在供应端，宁德时代将与深圳惠科等2家合作方在未来3年共同新建40万吨产能。各方遵循“成本加成、合理利润、风险共担”的全新定价原则，确立新建产能长期供货量与合理加工费锁定机制。宁德时代通过预付款与账期优化给予资金赋能。
下游：B2B直销模式降低中小集成商采购门槛
针对传统中小储能系统集成商面临的经销商多层转手、成本高昂及品质参差等痛点，宁德时代于今年6月推出“宁德时代商城”B2B直销平台，并于9月3日至30日举办全球开放月促销活动。
活动期间，314Ah储能电芯价格为0.395元/Wh起，280Ah（1P）储能电芯价格为0.465元/Wh起。
目前，该商城已开放电芯、电箱、集装箱三类产品的展示与销售。其中，314Ah和280Ah（1P）储能电芯处于在售状态，587Ah储能专用电芯已上架但暂处于待售状态。
在电箱产品方面，商城目前展示280Ah储能电箱和314Ah储能电箱长款，额定电量分别为46.59kWh和104.49kWh，对应1P52S和1P104S配置。
集装箱产品则包括EnerD和EnerD+两款储能集装箱，额定容量分别为4.472MWh和5.015MWh。其中，EnerD重量约41.5吨，EnerD+重量约38.5吨，两款产品均已通过相关国标认证。
通过线上直销方式，宁德时代将储能电芯及系统产品的采购环节进一步线上化，并将起订量降低至3箱，为中小型储能系统集成商提供直接采购渠道。

title: 总投资超110亿！7大储能锂电项目加速推进
content:
9月以来，储能及锂电产业链多项项目密集落地，涉及全固态电池、储能电芯、储能系统、正极材料及隔膜等环节，部分项目进入开工、投产或量产阶段。
为恒智能30亿元储能系统项目落地宜宾
9月3日，为恒智能与宜宾市叙州区正式签署投资协议，总投资约30亿元的14GWh数智化储能系统生产基地正式落地。
项目计划分两期建设，一期预计2027年投产，全部达产后将形成年产14GWh工商业储能系统产能，主要生产液冷储能柜、光储充一体化系统等产品。
元禾能源济宁高新区工厂项目开工
9月3日，元禾能源济宁高新区工厂项目正式开工。项目将建设研发中心、PACK生产线及总装生产线，并配套建设屋顶光伏、园区储能电站、充电站及智慧运营中心。
项目将通过光伏、储能及能源管理等设施，构建“源网荷储”一体化能源体系，打造零碳园区示范项目。
盟固利拟投建3万吨正极材料项目
9月3日，盟固利公告称，公司向特定对象发行股票申请获中国证监会同意注册批复。此次拟募资不超过8.66亿元，其中7.36亿元用于投建年产3万吨锂离子电池正极材料项目一期，1.3亿元用于补充流动资金。
项目一期拟建设2条正极材料生产线，新增年产能1.5万吨，包括1万吨/年的NCA材料产线和0.5万吨/年的高电压钴酸锂产线。项目整体规划年产能3万吨，一期建成后将新增1.5万吨正极材料产能。
佛塑科技投资71.58亿元建设两大隔膜项目
9月3日，佛塑科技公告称，拟通过全资子公司河北金力新能源科技有限公司，在广东韶关、河北武安投资建设两大绿色高端隔膜项目，合计总投资约71.58亿元。同时，公司拟定增募资不超过40亿元，用于项目建设及补充流动资金。
其中，韶关基地拟建设年产40亿平方米绿色高端湿法隔膜项目，总投资约33.47亿元，计划建设8条湿法隔膜基膜生产线；武安基地拟建设年产40亿平方米绿色高端涂覆隔膜项目，总投资约38.11亿元，计划建设8条湿法隔膜基膜生产线及44台涂布机。
两大项目建成后，将新增合计80亿平方米/年的隔膜产能，进一步扩大公司在动力及储能电池隔膜领域的产能布局。
华宜清创-普华新材启动全固态电芯项目
9月1日，华宜清创、普华新材发布硅碳负极及全固态电芯产品，并启动全固态电芯项目。
此次发布的“启辰”系列全固态电池采用硫化锂正极、硅碳负极及固-固界面工程技术，能量密度突破400Wh/kg。
此外，现场还落地多项战略合作。一是华宜清创分别与兰溪致德新能源、洛阳联创锂能完成多孔碳材料战略合作签约，与国轩高科达成硅碳负极领域深度合作，同时携手深圳清研电子、浙江峰泽新材料达成多维战略合作。二是广州融捷能源、四川新能源汽车创新中心、华宜清创等共同启动全固态电芯项目。
因湃电池587Ah储能电芯正式量产
近日，因湃电池“大方无隅”系列587Ah储能电芯正式量产下线。该产品于今年3月首次亮相，此次实现量产，意味着因湃完成从产品研发到规模制造的落地。
据介绍，587Ah电芯推出干坤版混合固液储能电芯和浩瀚版液态储能电芯两款产品。其中，干坤版面向高安全储能场景，浩瀚版主要适用于新能源大基地、电网侧调峰等大规模储能场景。
产能方面，因湃已建成6.5GWh储能大电芯专属产线并进入稳定运行阶段。目前公司已建成产能18GWh，总规划产能超过60GWh，产品覆盖动力电池和储能电池领域。
辉能科技第三代全固态电池进入量产
9月2日，辉能科技宣布第三代Gen 3.5锂陶瓷电池已在台湾吉瓦级工厂进入量产，标志着其全固态电池技术由研发及中试阶段进入规模化生产阶段。
据介绍，辉能科技第三代吉瓦级平台已于2024年投运，此次Gen 3.5产品进入量产后，将进一步推动全固态电池的商业化应用。
目前，辉能科技已累计出货超过240万颗电芯，并持续推进下一代Gen 4电池研发。公司表示，下一代Gen 4电池将采用全无机超流体电解质体系，沿用现有Logithium™电芯架构与制造工艺，预计仅需改造约10%的现有吉瓦级产线即可生产，目标应用覆盖AI数据中心、电动汽车、海事及航空航天领域。

title: 比亚迪、恩捷股份等4企推进储能锂电项目建设
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，锂电及储能产业链多个项目取得新进展，涉及电解液、储能设备、锂电隔膜等环节。
其中，新宙邦美国电解液生产基地正式动工，比亚迪12万吨电解液项目加快建设，高特电子储能智造基地投产，恩捷股份重庆基地7米超宽幅在线涂布产线同步落地。
新宙邦美国电解液生产基地正式动工
近日，美国新宙邦在美国俄亥俄州劳伦斯县艾恩顿举行锂电池电解液生产基地动工仪式，项目正式进入建设阶段。
据介绍，该项目是新宙邦在北美落地的首个规模化电池化学品生产基地，主要面向北美动力电池、储能及消费电子市场，建成后将进一步提升公司在北美地区的本地化生产和供应能力。
高特电子储能智造基地正式投产
9月4日，高特电子智造基地投产仪式在杭州市余杭区举行，标志着公司储能领域产能建设取得新进展。
据介绍，该智能智造基地以建设“黑灯工厂”为目标，目前产线约70%生产流程实现自动化，全面满产后可实现日产超1万套BMS及配套设备，将进一步提升储能产品规模化生产能力。
比亚迪12万吨电解液项目预计11月试生产
据“枝江发布”消息，近日，位于湖北宜昌枝江市姚家港化工园的比亚迪新能源产业项目建设有序推进。目前，项目1、2号主体厂房正在进行钢结构吊装，1、2号库房钢结构主体已完成，罐区正在进行基础回填，项目预计11月试生产、12月正式投产。
该项目由比亚迪集团弗迪电池有限公司投资建设，计划总投资3.72亿元，占地约80亩，主要建设年产12万吨电解液及新能源材料产线。
恩捷股份重庆基地7米超宽幅涂布产线投产
近日，恩捷股份首条7米超宽幅在线涂布产线在重庆基地一次性调试成功并顺利投产。至此，重庆基地12条生产线全面实现在线涂布能力全覆盖，正式迈入全流程在线涂布智能化量产新阶段。
据介绍，7米超宽幅在线涂布产线对设备适配、工艺匹配及产品质控等要求较高，此次产线顺利投产，将推动重庆基地隔膜生产效率及高端产能进一步提升。

title: 润阳0.763GW高效N型BC电池技改项目获备案
content:
9月4日，云南润阳世纪光伏科技有限公司申报的“年产0.763GW高效N型BC电池生产线智能化升级改造项目”正式通过企业投资项目备案。
据悉，该升级改造项目坐落于云南省曲靖市曲靖经济技术开发区，项目性质为改建，总投资额为3671.9万元。按照规划，项目拟于2026年12月正式开工建设，预计建设周期为两年，计划于2028年12月建成投产。
项目将依托现有厂房实施智能化升级，通过设备移拆、利旧改造、新增关键工艺设备及厂务配套改造，搭建BC高效电池产线。
此前，润阳在云南曲靖布局13GW N型高效太阳能电池绿色智慧工厂，此次技改仅涉及763MW产能，规模相对有限。
对于润阳而言，此次项目值得关注的或许是现有N型产线能否以相对较低的投入完成BC路线升级。如果改造后的产线能够实现稳定量产，并在效率、良率和成本等方面达到预期，后续或具备进一步扩大BC产能的基础。

title: 理想汽车拟26.5亿增资欣旺达动力
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月4日，欣旺达发布公告，宣布其子公司欣旺达动力拟进行增资扩股，引入北京理想汽车有限公司作为C++轮投资方。
根据公告，欣旺达同意理想汽车出资26.5亿元，向欣旺达动力增资，认购欣旺达动力13.99519878亿元新增注册资本，对应本次增资完成后欣旺达动力8.79%的股份。
增资完成后，欣旺达动力的注册资本将由145.15292050亿元增至159.14811928亿元人民币，欣旺达惠州新能源有限公司持有欣旺达动力的股权比例将由26.38%变更为24.06%。目前上市公司对欣旺达动力仍具备控制权，子公司继续纳入上市公司合并报表范围。
截至本公告披露日，上述C++轮投资方与欣旺达动力、实际控制人、欣旺达惠州新能源有限公司拟签署《欣旺达动力科技股份有限公司增资协议》。
根据公告资料显示，理想汽车与原有股东重庆车之辕创业投资有限公司同属Leading Ideal HK Limited旗下，交易完成后，理想体系合计持有欣旺达动力11.17%股权。
欣旺达动力全部权益价值评估值为250.007672亿元，本轮参考欣旺达动力C轮投前估值250亿元及C轮、C+轮增资情况，并经各方协商一致，欣旺达动力本次增资扩股前，股权全部权益价值确定为274.848亿元。
公告披露，本次增资旨在深化欣旺达动力与理想汽车的战略合作，发挥双方在技术研发、产能配套、市场拓展方面的协同优势，巩固动力电池业务竞争地位。同时充实欣旺达动力资本金，降低资产负债率，支撑动力电池业务发展需求。
本次交易不构成重大资产重组，相关各方拟签署增资协议，交易尚待协议约定的交割先决条件完成后实施。
财务数据显示，欣旺达动力2025年实现营业收入200.93亿元，净利润亏损31.69亿元。2026年上半年，欣旺达动力营收155.29亿元，净利润亏损3.24亿元，企业仍处于战略投入阶段，尚未实现盈利。
在此之前，欣旺达动力已于2026年5月完成C轮16.8亿元融资、7月完成C+轮8.05亿元融资，叠加本次C++轮26.5亿元增资，年内多轮产业资本入局。

title: 阳光电源、阿特斯储能纪要：AIDC配储成新焦点
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，阳光电源、阿特斯发布8月投资者关系活动记录，两家光储龙头上半年均面临行业需求波动、原材料及地缘政策等考验，储能业务、AIDC配套业务成重点关注方向。
阳光电源：营收规模回落，AIDC业务进入技术验证阶段
8月28日，阳光电源披露，2026年上半年公司实现营业收入309亿元，同比下降29%，归母净利润52.6亿元，同比下滑32%。
收入下滑主要来自国内与中东市场收缩，其中，国内受光伏装机下行、战略性放弃亏损项目影响，国内收入由去年同期181亿元降至82亿元，降幅55%。中东市场受去年沙特大项目高基数影响，收入从57亿元回落至11亿元，下降91%。
尽管营收规模下行，但阳光电源盈利水平环比改善，二季度毛利率抬升至38%，净利润率提升至19%，上半年整体毛利率35.9%，同比提升1.5个百分点。毛利率提升主要源于业务结构优化，低毛利新能源投资开发业务占比下降，欧洲等高收益市场占比提升。碳酸锂涨价、储能行业竞争加剧、人民币升值则对储能板块毛利率形成拖累。
业务端，逆变器上半年发货66GW，同比减少10GW，下滑主要来自国内市场，海外出货与市场增速匹配，逆变器收入108亿元，依托海外收入占比提升、品牌溢价，业务盈利能力改善。
储能业务上半年发货25GWh，同比增长28%，实现收入154亿元，电力储能收入下滑拖累整体储能营收，中东收入同比减少52亿元。阳光电源发布全场景储能变流平台、新一代“1+X”模块化PCS，拿下阿联酋7.5GWh电力储能大单。
对于市场展望，阳光电源表示逆变器毛利率整体保持稳定。储能毛利率受区域确收结构、碳酸锂价格、储能时长多重变量影响，一季度储能毛利率32%、二季度35%环比上行，三四季度需要逐季度跟踪变量变化。
AIDC业务方面，阳光电源已经推出EnerNeo系列固态变压器SST并供货，数台SST设备预计四季度投运，有望落地800V直流供电算力场景。当前，AIDC配储在手订单约2GWh，跟进项目十余GWh。
SST订单预计四季度逐步落地，2027年小批量交付，2028年大规模交付，35kV SST预计2027年上半年完成研发。此外，阳光电源与海外AI头部企业保持沟通，看好AIDC赛道增长潜力，认为该业务具备爆发式增长基础。
海外市场方面，阿特斯表示，长期来看，美国业务将适度收缩、控制风险，暂不考虑美国本地建厂，转向发力其他海外市场，探索零部件、服务层面海外合作。
欧洲储能市场，上半年实际表现超预期，欧盟2030年200GW储能目标支撑需求，负电价、峰谷价差、容量市场拉动行业，预计2027年欧洲储能增速维持50%以上。
阿特斯：海外大储高速放量，AIDC配储尚处规模化前期
8月30日，阿特斯披露半年度投资者交流情况，2026上半年实现营业收入127.84亿元，归母净利润3.00亿元。
业绩承压来自多方面，主要包括行业整体环境承压、储能上游材料涨价叠加价格下行、光伏业务主动收缩带来固定成本摊销抬升、美国业务重组整合带来阶段性扰动。
储能已经成为阿特斯核心增长支柱，上半年大型储能系统出货6.1GWh，同比增幅超103.3%，储能系统收入56.59亿元，占总收入比重约44%。截至报告期末，累计大型储能交付规模超23GWh，是海外头部储能系统集成商。
针对储能毛利率下滑，阿特斯解释主要受电芯原材料涨价、市场竞争带来产品价格下行，叠加美国业务调整影响。公司判断后续上游成本有望得到控制，对储能板块利润形成支撑。
市场层面，储能整体需求依旧处于快速上行通道，欧美高价市场订单是阿特斯主要来源，工商业储能受电价波动拉动需求提升，不同区域、细分板块价格表现分化。
对于AIDC配储赛道，阿特斯认为市场前景积极，但行业整体处于规模化突破前期。表后大规模储能可复用现有常规产品，机架侧毫秒级响应储能还需要专项开发，相关商业模式正在和客户推进落地。美国网侧储能今年装机增速较快，AIDC配套储能未来有望逐步走向标配。

title: Kawasaki completes 30 MW hydrogen gas turbine installation at RWE’s Emsland plant | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
The system is located in the hydrogen park at the Emsland power plant in Lingen, Lower Saxony, and uses Kawasaki’s 30 MW-class L30A gas turbine. Kawasaki manufactured the gas turbine at its Akashi Works, while group company Kawasaki Gas Turbine Europe GmbH (KGE) incorporated it into the generating unit and installed the equipment.
Following commissioning of the gas turbine and generating unit, Kawasaki and RWE plan to begin a power generation demonstration using 100% hydrogen fuel. According to Kawasaki, the project will be the first hydrogen-only power generation demonstration in Europe using a 30 MW-class gas turbine.
The demonstration will use CO₂-free hydrogen produced through water electrolysis using green electricity supplied by RWE-owned wind power facilities. The project will also test flexible power generation by mixing natural gas as a supplementary fuel and varying the hydrogen co-firing ratio between 0% and 100% to match hydrogen availability and market requirements.

title: Power to Hydrogen and Repsol complete AEM electrolyzer pilot
content:
The pilot was conducted through Repsol’s All4Zero industrial innovation hub and evaluated P2H2’s commercial-scale AEM stack across more than 1,250 hours of parametric and durability testing, including operation under simulated variable load profiles. The test protocol included repeated cycling between 40% and 100% load and operation across pressures from 2 to 30 bar.
The stack recorded irreversible degradation of approximately 2 mV/kHr over the testing period, with average cell voltage described as virtually unchanged between the start and end of the test. Based on these results, P2H2 projects system lifetimes exceeding 50,000 hours. Hydrogen purity reached up to 99.9% at 30 bar operating pressure. The system also resumed testing without consequence following an unplanned facility power outage.
Using the US Department of Energy’s H2A-Lite analysis framework with Repsol-specific inputs, P2H2 projects a levelized cost of hydrogen of approximately €3.86/kg, representing around a 16% reduction versus incumbent electrolyzer technologies. Under optimized renewable energy scenarios with hybrid power purchase agreements, the company said costs could reach approximately €2.82/kg.
“This pilot proves what we’ve long believed: that AEM electrolysis can deliver PEM-like performance at a fundamentally lower cost structure,” said Dr. Paul Matter, Founder and CEO of Power to Hydrogen. “With Repsol’s rigorous testing framework and real-world operating conditions, we’ve demonstrated the durability and efficiency that the market has been waiting to see from AEM. This is commercial-scale hardware, stress-tested under the conditions that matter to industrial buyers.”
Berta Moreno, Senior Scientist at Repsol, said: “Through our All4Zero accelerator, Repsol is committed to identifying and validating the technologies that will be essential to decarbonising industrial operations at scale. Power to Hydrogen’s results demonstrate meaningful progress toward the performance thresholds required for large-scale renewable hydrogen deployment.”
The companies are exploring a larger-scale demonstration at the 500 kW to megawatt level. P2H2 has stated it is actively deploying systems at this scale, including ongoing projects at the Port of Antwerp-Bruges, Belgium, and with SINTEF in Norway. Repsol has set a target of 600–800 MW of renewable hydrogen capacity by 2030.

title: 2027 Chevrolet Bolt 70-MPH Range Test: Here’s How Far America’s Cheapest EV Goes
content:
The new Bolt starts at less than $30,000 and promises over 250 miles of range on a full charge.
Photo by:
State Of Charge
6:32am ET
InsideEVs contributor Tom Moloughney range-tested the 2027 Chevrolet Bolt.
America’s cheapest new EV promises 262 miles on a full charge on the combined cycle.
The electric hatchback was driven at a constant 70 mph, and it did better than expected.
Despite looking similar, the
new Chevrolet Bolt
is significantly better than its predecessor. It packs more range, faster charging, a lot more tech inside, and a starting price of less than $30,000.
This makes it
the cheapest new EV in the United States
right now, but that won’t matter much if it can’t deliver a solid range in the real world. Thankfully, it can, as InsideEVs contributor and
State of Charge
YouTube host Tom Moloughney found out during his well-known 70 miles per hour highway range test.
On paper, the 2027 Bolt is rated for 262 miles on a full charge on the combined cycle. Meanwhile, the EPA highway range rating is 232 miles, and I’ll get right to the point: GM’s entry-level EV topped that result in the real world, even though the EPA highway procedure doesn’t even exceed 60 mph.
The tester was a base Bolt LT with 17-inch wheels and the same 65-kilowatt-hour lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery pack that’s available on all the trims. The tires were set to the manufacturer’s recommended pressure, the ambient temperature was between 71°F and 80°F, and the climate control system was set to the most efficient mode.
As always, the 70 mph run was done on the New Jersey Turnpike, where Tom does the vast majority of his highway range tests because it doesn’t have a lot of traffic early in the morning and there are lots of charging stations to choose from.
Gallery: 2027 Chevrolet Bolt: Review
The 2027 Chevrolet Bolt drove 243 miles on a full charge and still had an estimated 1% and 2 miles of remaining range, according to the car’s instrument cluster. That’s 11 miles more than the EPA highway score and 19 miles less than the EPA combined figure. All in all, a solid result, with Tom reckoning he could probably squeeze a couple of more miles out of the battery, but he preferred to keep it safe, as the Bolt had already limited the power output. The average energy efficiency was 3.6 miles/kilowatt-hour, and the total energy used was 66 kWh, just a smidge over the stated usable capacity of 65 kWh.
At this point, It’s worth noting that speed has a big impact on the 2027 Bolt’s range. Earlier this year, the YouTube channel EV Motoring did a 75 mph range test with a similar car, and
the result was noticeably worse
. The weather was similar, but the 5 mph difference resulted in an average efficiency of 2.8 mi/kWh and a real-world range of just 197 miles.
If it wasn’t clear until now that speed kills EV range, these numbers should keep things in order.
Still, with a starting price of under $30,000, a more than decent real-world range, and perfectly usable charging speeds, the new Bolt should make for a great commuter. Too bad General Motors won’t keep it around for too long.

title: Dacia’s Answer To Cheap Chinese EVs Used To Be One. Now It’s European
content:
Built in Slovenia, the all-new Dacia Spring gets a roomier body and up to 155 miles of range, starting at €17,900 in Italy.
Photo by:
1:24am ET
The all-new Dacia Spring moves production from China to Slovenia, starting at €17,900 in Italy.
It shares its platform with the Renault Twingo and offers up to 155 miles of WLTP range from a 27.5-kWh LFP battery.
A larger body brings more space, while optional 50-kW DC charging takes the battery from 15–80% in 28 minutes.
Can Europe build affordable electric cars without handing the business to China? The original answer from European budget brand Dacia came with an ironic twist:
Its affordable Spring EV
was built in China. The completely redesigned second generation changes that, moving production to Slovenia while keeping its price low.
In Italy, it starts at €17,900, and even the better-equipped Journey trim doesn’t exceed €20,000. That’s about the same as the outgoing China-made model, and you get an all-new European-made car with better specs.
This isn’t another facelift.
The Spring
has had several, and none could hide the fact that it was still related to the Renault Kwid, a cheap combustion car for the Indian market. The new Spring shares its platform with
the new Renault Twingo E-Tech
, but it wants to look chiseled and serious, not cute and cheerful like the French car.
Gallery: Dacia Spring (2027) Debuts in Paris
The Spring’s specifications look very familiar alongside the Renault’s. Both have a single front-mounted motor producing roughly 80 horsepower and 175 Nm (129 pound-feet), and they both draw from a 27.5-kilowatt-hour battery. Dacia confirms the pack’s LFP chemistry and says the state capacity is the usable number. The Spring manages up to 250 kilometers (155 miles) on the WLTP cycle, slightly behind the Twingo’s 263 kilometers (163 miles).
That’s if you can match the claimed consumption figure of 4.9 miles/kWh (12.7 kWh/100 km).
It accelerates from a standstill to 100 km/h (62 mph) in 12.1 seconds and tops out at 130 km/h (81 mph). That's pretty slow, but Dacia says existing Spring owners average just 34 kilometers (21 miles) per day; you mostly see these cars in town, and 75% of charging takes place at home. This car is built around those routines.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Using a 7-kW home wallbox, the Spring’s standard 6.6-kW onboard charger takes 2 hours and 55 minutes to charge the battery from 15% to 80%. The optional 11-kW charger cuts that to 1 hour and 55 minutes when connected to a sufficiently powerful three-phase wallbox.
the previous model
, a DC fast charger isn't standard. It's bundled with the more powerful AC charger, and even though it only charges at up to 50 kW, which is pretty modest, it can bring the battery from 15-80% in 28 minutes.
The base Expression trim gets manual air conditioning, rear parking sensors, a seven-inch digital instrument display and a smartphone-based multimedia system—it has no central screen. Journey adds a 10.1-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a reversing camera, and keyless entry.
More On This
Measuring 3.85 meters (151.5 inches), the new Spring is 15 centimeters (5.9 inches) longer than the outgoing model. It’s also 18 cm (7 in) wider than before, which makes it look much more planted on the road and a lot less like a tall and narrow kei car.
Dacia says it developed the new Spring in less than two years. Sharing its underpinnings with the Twingo helps keep costs and development time down, giving it a credible shot at competing with Chinese rivals on value. European production could help win over buyers, too, especially since choosing it doesn’t mean paying a hefty premium.

title: Plug-In Hybrids Have An Emissions Problem. Carmakers Want To Delay The Fix
content:
The EU says PHEVs emit six times more CO2 than official claims on average, yet automakers are fine with it.
Photo by:
Andrei Nedelea
6:34am ET
EU data shows PHEVs emitted six times their official CO2 ratings on average, with the gap widening each year.
On average, their tailpipe CO2 emissions were just 14% below those of conventional gas and diesel cars.
Automakers want to scrap a 2027 rule change that would bring official PHEV emissions ratings closer to reality.
Plug-in hybrids look great on paper. If charged regularly, they will achieve and even exceed their manufacturer-claimed efficiency and emissions numbers. It’s all about keeping the combustion engine off and driving on electricity. The problem is that many people still treat them like regular hybrids,
don’t charge them
, and end up producing much higher emissions than advertised.
Their emissions problem is a familiar story
. Last September, European data showed they produced roughly five times their official CO2 emissions. Now the gap is even bigger, just as manufacturers push back against efforts to make the numbers more honest.
According to a new Transport & Environment (
) analysis of newly released European Union data, PHEVs registered in 2024 averaged 145 grams of CO2 per kilometer, against an official 24 g/km. The findings come from onboard fuel monitors in 220,000 vehicles, reflecting how those cars were actually driven rather than how they performed in a standardized lab test.
Photo by: Transport & Environment (T&E)
For 2023 registrations, those figures were 138 and 28 g/km. Actual emissions rose about 5% while official ratings fell roughly 15%. T&E says the discrepancy has widened annually since monitoring began in 2021.
The data also shows that PHEVs’ real-world emissions were only 14% below those of regular combustion cars’ 169 g/km, down from a 17% advantage the previous year. It’s important to note that these are average tailpipe figures, not lifecycle comparisons.
Official tests use an estimate called the “utility factor” to account for how much a PHEV spends running on electricity. The more electric driving they assume, the lower the car’s CO2 rating. But if owners rely on the combustion engine more than expected, actual emissions will be considerably higher.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The assumption is that if a car spends more time using its battery, it lowers its rated CO2 output. The EU began tightening that assumption starting in 2025, but it’s doing it in stages, with a new correction expected in 2027. Manufacturers know this change is coming and are pushing back because it would make their PHEVs look less green on paper and therefore less appealing to buyers.
It also helps determine if automakers meet their fleet CO2 targets. An earlier report estimated that
passing off PHEVs as having lower emissions
helped automakers avoid billions of euros in fines. It also highlighted the fact that drivers reported fuel efficiency numbers far higher than the advertised figures.
Powertrain supplier Horse, which opposes the change in how PHEV emissions are calculated, posted a paper in early March called “How tighter PHEV utility factor requirements will harm the auto industry.” Its concern is basically that more realistic CO2 ratings would make PHEVs a tougher sell.
also analyzed a paper published by ACEA (the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association), in which the association wants the next utility factor correction canceled.
More On This
There’s a lot at stake here because PHEVs continue to grow in popularity across the EU.
says they accounted for nearly 10% of all new passenger vehicle registrations across the bloc in the first half of 2026.
T&E argues that weakening the rules would delay EV investment and hurt Europe’s ability to compete with China. It wants lawmakers to reject the industry’s demands; a Council debate is expected October 12, followed by a parliamentary vote in November.
More accurate emissions estimates won’t make PHEVs burn less fuel. But they would make it harder for carmakers to take credit for cutting emissions that only disappear on paper and are far higher for most drivers. After years of warnings about PHEV emissions, that seems a bit overdue.

title: Polestar’s New Concept Hints At What’s Coming To Its Next Two EVs
content:
The Formula 2030 design study evolves Polestar’s familiar design language and previews features coming to the next Polestar 2 and 7.
Photo by:
Polestar
5:22am ET
Formula 2030 previews Polestar’s evolving design language, retaining familiar cues like its Dual Blade headlights.
Its design cues will appear on the next Polestar 2, due in 2027, and the forthcoming Polestar 7.
Polestar faces heavy losses and a U.S. sales ban covering model-year 2027 and newer vehicles.
Polestar design is changing, but it’s a classic case of evolution rather than revolution. The manufacturer teased the Formula 2030 concept to showcase its new design direction, but despite the name, its influence will appear much sooner, starting with
the new Polestar 2
debuting early next year.
It will also influence the look of the new Polestar 2’s crossover cousin,
the Polestar 7
, which arrives in 2028. They won’t look exactly like the concept, but it gives us a good idea where the brand is headed next.
The brand’s design boss Philipp Römers says Polestar didn’t want to stray too far from its established visual identity. Familiar touches like the Dual Blade headlights will stay, alongside updated styling, a fresh interior and a focus on more sustainable materials.
More Polestar Stories
The Formula 2030 concept appears to be a low-slung sedan with a more planted stance than any previous Polestar. Its front design accentuates the vehicle’s width, making it look even more aggressive than
the Polestar 5
, which is currently the brand’s sportiest offering and its halo model. Looks like Polestar wasn’t kidding when announcing it had
set its sights on BMW M and Mercedes-AMG
For now, all we get is a dark teaser showing the front fascia of the upcoming concept; no side or rear views. It will be fully revealed later this year during the media drive for the recently revealed Polestar 4 SUV, a more practical wagon-like variant of the 4 fastback already on sale.
Polestar needs the new 2 to land with buyers and build on its predecessor’s popularity in an increasingly crowded EV market. It will be a sedan, like the car it replaces, with big shoes to fill as a successor to the company’s best-selling model with over 190,000 units sold, according to the manufacturer.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
However, in a market increasingly dominated by high-riding crossovers, the Polestar 7 could end up being the bigger seller.
Even though it started 2026 with
its best first quarter ever
, the company's shares dropped nearly 30% after it announced its first-half 2026 results. Vehicle sales were up 0.4% year over year, but revenue fell 4.4%, and it posted a net H1 loss of $842 million, even after reducing operational losses by 43%. This led it to cut its full-year growth outlook from low double digits to low- to mid-single digits.
lost access to the American market
. Polestar says U.S. authorities denied it authorization to sell model-year 2027 and newer vehicles under the Connected Vehicle Rule. It can still sell earlier model-year inventory, but once that is depleted, it expects to stop new-car sales in the country.

title: Sold Out: Volkswagen’s Cheap ID. Polo EV Now Has Months-Long Wait Times
content:
Sold Out: Volkswagen’s Cheap ID. Polo EV Now Has Months-Long Wait Times
Its cousins, the Skoda Epiq and Cupra Raval, have also seen massive interest from customers.
- The Volkswagen Group’s small and affordable new EVs are facing huge demand.
- Volkswagen ID. Polo, Skoda Epiq, and Cupra Raval orders are facing months-long wait times.
- Tens of thousands of orders have already been placed for the entry-level EVs.
Volkswagen is having a rough time right now, but at least its new and affordable electric cars are doing just fine in Europe. The recently introduced Electric Urban Car Family, represented by the subcompact Volkswagen ID. Polo, Skoda Epiq, and Cupra Raval, is seeing huge success, with tens of thousands of cars ordered already and waiting lists that go on for months.
The ID. Polo, which went on sale in April, is now sold out, with over 30,000 orders on the books and a ten-month waiting list, according to a major Volkswagen dealer group quoted by Automotive News. The electric crossover version of the automaker’s iconic nameplate, dubbed ID. Cross, is also seeing robust demand, even though the first units are expected to land in dealerships in November.
Volkswagen ID. Polo (2026)
The technically similar Skoda Epiq has been an even bigger hit. With over 35,000 orders since the books opened in July, the Czech automaker’s smallest EV is now sold out for several months, with delivery dates as late as June 2027 for new orders. The same goes for the Cupra Raval, which is the sportiest of the four, at least until the hot Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI arrives later down the road.
Skoda Epiq (2026)
The entry-level versions of the electric hatchbacks start from around €25,000 ($29,000) in Germany, including VAT. That’s more than their combustion-powered alternatives, but it still goes to show that a reasonably priced EV with decent range and charging performance will go a long way, especially when a gallon of gas is now selling for nearly $9 in the region.
The strong demand has prompted all three automakers to warn customers that waiting times could be longer for certain configurations, but that’s a good problem to have. That said, Volkswagen and Cupra are working to increase the output at the factory in Martorell, Spain, where the ID. Polo and Raval are being assembled. Skoda, which builds the Epiq in Pamplona, is also looking for ways to boost production and cut delivery times.
All models deliver at least 200 miles of WLTP range on a full charge, and vehicle-to-load functionality is available across the board, which means owners can export energy from their cars’ high-voltage batteries to power appliances, tools, or camping equipment without having to carry external batteries or devices.

title: This 381 Wh/kg Solid-State Battery Packs More Energy and Charges in Just 8 Minutes
content:
A Mercedes-Backed Company Just Put Solid-State Batteries Into Mass Production
Taiwan’s ProLogium seems to have cracked the code, with the first mass-produced solid-state cells promising impressive energy density.
- ProLogium claims it has started mass-producing all-solid-state battery cells.
- The Taiwanese company, backed by Mercedes-Benz, is rolling out the first large-format pouch cells at its gigawatt-capable facility in Taoyuan.
- ProLogium’s latest Lithium Ceramic Battery promises 5-to-80% charging times in under 10 minutes.
All-solid-state battery cells, which promise longer driving ranges, faster charging times, and increased safety, are now being mass-produced. That’s what Taiwan’s ProLogium, which has seen investments from Mercedes-Benz and other big industry names, claims.
And yes, Finland’s Donut Lab made some bombastic claims at the beginning of the year, but so far we haven’t seen concrete evidence that the startup has fulfilled its promise of selling solid-state batteries to the masses.
ProLogium, meanwhile, has some big names backing up its claims. Its Generation 3.5 large-format 185.4 ampere-hour Lithium Ceramic Battery (LCB) cell, which is now rolling off the Taoke assembly line at its facility in Taoyuan, Taiwan, has been tested by Germany’s TÜV, showing a gravimetric energy density of 381 watt-hours/kilogram and a volumetric energy density of 903 watt-hours/liter.
ProLogium Lithium-Ceramic Battery Cell Lineup
That’s roughly 30% better than the mainstream nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) cells powering most electric cars on the road in the United States today, which usually top out at around 300 Wh/kg at the cell level. Meanwhile, the more cost-effective lithium-iron-phosphate cells, which are increasingly finding their way into EVs around the world, have a gravimetric energy density between 150 and 200 Wh/kg.
When Donut published the first specs of its promised solid-state battery cell, it said that it delivered 400 Wh/kg.
Separately, UL Solutions, which tests and certifies the safety of EV chargers, batteries, cables, and much more, tested ProLogium’s large-format cell under China’s new GB/T 43568-2026 methodology, which was introduced in July to better differentiate between all-solid-state cells and units that still use some form of liquid electrolyte.
As part of the test, the cell was kept in a vacuum for six hours at a constant temperature of 248°F (120°), and the recorded weight loss was less than 0.05%, which is well below the 0.5% maximum threshold that allows companies to label their products as all-solid-state batteries.
ProLogium’s Gen 3.5 cell uses a composite solid electrolyte and a ceramic separator with a proprietary edge-frame structure that helps isolate potential burrs while providing sealing and insulation.
The company says its previous Gen 3 cell can fast-charge from 5% to 80% state of charge in eight and a half minutes, and that it won’t catch fire if shot with a bullet, at temperatures as high as 338°F (170°F), and when overcharged at twice the rated voltage.
The initial production capacity of the facility that’s making the first Gen 3.5 large-format pouch cells is 0.5 gigawatt-hours. That’s roughly 6,000 EV battery packs, each with 80 kWh of capacity, so not a lot compared to traditional lithium-ion EV battery plants, but ProLogium has big expansion plans. The Taiwan facility is set to double production by 2030, and a second production facility in Dunkirk, France, is designed for an initial annual output of 4 GWh, with a maximum capacity of 44 GWh. The French factory is expected to go online in 2028, with production ramping up through 2030.
Then, there’s the Gen 4 battery cell, which is right around the corner, according to ProLogium. With a fully inorganic superfluidized electrolyte system, the next-gen battery promises even faster charging times and better low-temperature performance. And better yet, factories that build Gen 3.5 cells will need to upgrade just 10% of their line equipment to start assembling Gen 4 cells, which means costs stay down.

title: Watch Tesla FSD Navigate Denmark's Tightest, Toughest Street
content:
Narrow cobbled streets, cyclists and cafe crowds make driving an impressive test of FSD’s capability, as well as its occupants’ nerves.
Photo by:
robot*irl/YouTube
9:45am ET
Tesla FSD navigates narrow, crowded streets in Aarhus, where pedestrians and cyclists leave little room for cars.
The drive shows impressive judgment in tight spaces, despite occasional hesitation and overly cautious speeds.
Its only two mistakes were minor: failing to indicate around an obstacle and stopping too far from a traffic light.
Some streets make you question whether you should be driving down them, even when the signs clearly say that you can. This
Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) demonstration
in Aarhus, Denmark, features plenty of those, with pedestrians, bicycles, and cafe customers making already tight streets feel even narrower.
The roughly 21-minute video uploaded by
robot*irl
follows an FSD drive into increasingly tight parts of the city center. As the occupants explain, cars are guests in these streets, so it’s perfectly okay for people to be walking in the middle of the road; getting through requires a lot of patience, as well as accurate steering.
Seeing a car go down a narrow, cobbled lane without any human intervention is pretty impressive. Sure, it hesitates a couple of times and takes it a bit slower than a human would, but the driver never touched the controls once throughout the video. FSD handled an oncoming car, strollers parked on the side of the road, and people who walked straight into the Tesla’s path.
The car always waited for cyclists before turning or moving over into the oncoming lane, it inched past obstacles with remarkable precision, and even waited for a dog that crossed its path. At one particularly awkward encounter, an oncoming car and a stroller complicate an already narrow passage. The Tesla adjusts its position and works through the squeeze with ease in a situation that may have made some actual human drivers uneasy.
Later, it negotiates another narrow gap beside roadworks. Even the local who provided the Tesla for the test and is sitting in the passenger’s seat admitted that he hadn’t previously taken FSD through some of these streets. That doesn’t mean Tesla didn’t train FSD on similar situations, but it adds to the sense that this was an exploratory drive and an unusual situation for the car to react to.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The only two mistakes were pretty minor: it moved over with one wheel into the oncoming lane to avoid an obstacle and didn’t indicate, and in one instance it stopped a bit too far from the traffic lights. The fact that nothing more major than this happened on such a tricky drive is pretty impressive.
Watching FSD negotiate these packed narrow streets certainly inspires confidence. It still needs a human supervisor, though, and getting through a crowded Danish street is a different achievement from convincing regulators that occupants can take their eyes off the road. The timeline for eyes-off operation in Europe remains unclear, but it will likely be longer than in the United States.
More On This
Meanwhile,
Tesla’s Cybercab has started carrying passengers
in Texas, and early onboard videos all seem to show impressively uneventful and relaxing journeys. With no steering wheel or pedals, this is driverless operation: passengers can look away because supervising the car isn’t their job.
Making that experience seem ordinary is a meaningful achievement, even if a limited rollout in a geofenced area in Austin doesn’t establish readiness for every European street, even if it can do the Danish cafe crawl very well already.

title: “傻瓜式”剪片：Adobe Premiere 更新 AI 功能，时间线上能直接生成音视频素材
content:
IT之家 9 月 8 日消息，Adobe 今天（8 日）宣布重新设计专业视频剪辑软件 Premiere 中的 AI 交互方式，新的“生成式媒体”工具支持直接在项目时间线中生成视频、音效、音乐和声景，无需中断当前工作流程。所使用的生成模型并非全都是新产品，这次更新的重点是大幅简化调用方式。
以往缺少补充镜头或音频素材时，编辑人员往往需要在浏览器或外部应用之间来回切换。更新后，只需选中视频或音频轨道上的空白区域，即可根据项目上下文生成可完全编辑的片段。
此外，时间线还可以直接调用多种底层模型，提供了 Adobe Firefly、谷歌 Veo、Runway、Luma 和可灵，便于用户根据项目风格选择合适的模型。
Premiere 还将增加一批处于测试阶段的 AI 音频工具，可分离同时说话的不同人物、在人声出现时自动压低音乐音量，并单独调整对白和环境声。
据IT之家了解，Adobe 还将把 AI 助手引入特效编辑软件 After Effects，目前同样处于测试阶段。编辑人员可以直接使用自然语言指令整理项目、解决技术问题或创建效果，无需自行编写表达式。

title: 《奇异人生》开发商 Dont Nod 陷财务危机：计划裁员 90 人，可能撑不过明年 1 月
content:
IT之家 9 月 8 日消息，据游戏媒体 VGC 今天报道，法国游戏工作室 Dont Nod Entertainment 表示，公司可能需要裁员最多 90 人，并警告称公司可能面临关闭局面。
IT之家从原报道获悉，Dont Nod 工作室成立于 2008 年，以《奇异人生》系列游戏而闻名。该公司在 2026 年上半年报告中表示，董事会已批准新商业模式，可能导致最多 90 人被裁员。
该公司在声明中表示：“尽管我们已经采取了业绩改善计划，实施一系列削减成本行动，但上述努力不足以恢复长期竞争力。我们正在重新考虑法国业务，将运营重点集中于单一作品，同时整合启动新项目所需的专业能力。”
此外，Dont Nod 今年 4 月推出了新作《Aphelion》，但该作的销量不足以帮助公司摆脱困境。审计机构曾于 6 月警告称，该公司可能会在今年内耗尽资金。
Dont Nod 此前曾于 2020 年向腾讯出售少数股权，但腾讯如今没有计划向公司注资。此次财务报告也谈到了这一问题。公司表示，如果无法尽快获得新的融资，他们可能无法撑过明年 1 月 31 日。

title: 任天堂《塞尔达传说》40 周年纪念版 Switch 2 掌机官宣，10 月 29 日发售
content:
IT之家 9 月 8 日消息，今天（8 日）晚间的《塞尔达传说》40 周年任天堂直面会上，任天堂正式公布了《塞尔达传说》主题的 Switch 2 限定版主机及 Switch 2 Pro 手柄。
据IT之家了解，这两款产品均为纪念《塞尔达传说》诞生 40 周年而推出，10 月 29 日发售。Pro 手柄另有附带展示支架的特别版本，仅在任天堂商店销售。
任天堂推出《塞尔达传说》主题游戏机已有多年历史。过去 20 多年里，旗下几乎每款掌机都有相应版本。2004 年，任天堂推出金色 Game Boy Advance SP，上盖饰有三角力量图案，随附《塞尔达传说：缩小帽》游戏。
此后，任天堂又于 2006 年推出《塞尔达传说：幻影沙漏》金色 DS Lite，2011 年推出系列 25 周年纪念版黑色 3DS，随后陆续推出《塞尔达传说：众神的三角力量 2》主题的金黑配色 3DS XL，机身带有三角力量图案，以及《塞尔达传说：姆吉拉的假面 3D》主题的金色 New Nintendo 3DS XL。
家用主机方面，任天堂曾推出《塞尔达传说：风之杖 HD》限定版 Wii U 套装，内含主题 GamePad 和游戏。此外，任天堂还为《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》推出过配备白色主题底座的特别版 Switch OLED，并于 2024 年推出金色 Switch Lite。

title: 捷豹路虎将通过自愿离职方式裁减近 10% 员工，目标省下 17 亿英镑
content:
IT之家 9 月 8 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间 9 月 7 日，英国豪华汽车制造商捷豹路虎宣布，未来两年将通过自愿离职方式裁减近 10% 的员工。在中国车企竞争、关税等压力加剧之际，汽车行业面临的经营环境愈发严峻。
捷豹路虎隶属于印度塔塔汽车，在英格兰设有 17 处运营地点。公司计划裁减约 4000 个岗位，目标是节省 17 亿英镑（IT之家注：现汇率约合 154.67 亿元人民币），并将盈亏平衡点降至 30 万辆左右。
捷豹路虎在全球拥有约 4.3 万名员工，其中 3.4 万人在英国，公司没有透露此次裁员将涉及哪些地区。CEO 巴柏德坦言：“汽车行业面临重大挑战，技术变革、激烈竞争和持续的地缘政治不确定性交织在一起。”
与此同时，捷豹路虎仍在应对 2025 年网络攻击造成的影响。那次攻击导致捷豹路虎长时间停产，并扰乱了供应商的运营。
捷豹路虎表示，未来 12 个月将推出 5 款新产品，未来 5 年还将继续投入 150 亿至 180 亿英镑（现汇率约合 1,364.76 亿至 1,637.71 亿元人民币），用于电动化、数字技术、先进制造和改善客户体验。
尽管如此，捷豹路虎认为，要增强业务韧性，仍必须削减开支并精简组织结构。此次自愿离职计划主要面向 2.6 万名受薪员工和管理人员。
当天，英国商务大臣乔纳森 · 雷诺兹还与巴柏德通话，并计划本周晚些时候与捷豹路虎及工会会面。
英国首相安迪 · 伯纳姆的发言人表示：“我们理解，对受影响员工、他们的家人以及更广泛的社区来说，这将是一段充满不确定性、令人担忧的时期。我们也知道，当前市场环境给全球汽车行业带来了挑战。”
当地市长理查德 · 帕克宣布提供 50 万英镑（现汇率约合 454.9 万元人民币）资金，帮助选择自愿离职的员工。

title: 消息称 WhatsApp 将支持第三方 AI 智能体，顺应时代潮流
content:
感谢IT之家网友 花开上林 的线索投递！
IT之家 9 月 8 日消息，据科技媒体 WABetaInfo 上周（9 月 4 日）报道，WhatsApp 即将支持第三方 AI 智能体。
IT之家从原报道获悉，当 OpenClaw 等人工智能助手出现时，许多用户尝试将这些 AI 智能体当作机器人连接到 WhatsApp，但很多情况下都会导致封号。
对比之下，Telegram 选择拥抱时代趋势，后续逐渐成为用户与 AI 智能体聊天的主要平台之一。这些智能体既可以运行在用户家中的电脑，也可以在云端运行。
如今，WhatsApp 正在开发第三方 AI 智能体原生支持，允许用户将这些 Agent 接入到 WhatsApp 聊天框内。根据流传出的截图，WhatsApp 将使用 API key 与第三方 Agent 连接。
此外，用户只能在私聊对话中与智能体交流，不能将其添加到群聊或者社区，也无法访问用户的其他对话、联系人或文件。WhatsApp 还会提醒用户，AI 的回复可能会出错。

title: 谷歌 DeepMind 推出 AlphaGenome Atlas，覆盖人类基因组全部 90 亿种单核苷酸变异预测
content:
IT之家 9 月 8 日消息，谷歌今日推出 AlphaGenome Atlas，这一平台包含了人类基因组中 90 亿种单核苷酸变异（所有可能的单字母 DNA 改变）的功能预测，是目前涵盖基因突变对分子生物学影响最全面的目录，学术界可通过免费门户网站免费使用。
DNA 是生命的语言，掌握其密码能够改变人类理解生物学和治疗疾病的能力，但解读基因变异对分子层面的影响长期存在瓶颈：人类基因组有约 90 亿种可能的单字母突变，在实验室逐一测试几乎不可能。
根据介绍，谷歌 DeepMind 此前已经推出 AI 模型 AlphaGenome，可以预测基因变异对生物过程的影响，可用于分析特定变异并在研究中得到广泛应用，此次通过大规模预先计算 AlphaGenome 的预测结果，构建出覆盖全基因组变异的全景资源库，就像地图集汇总地理信息一样，绘制出全基因组 DNA 变异的分子效应图谱。
为帮助科学家快速找到影响最大的遗传改变，谷歌同时发布了 AlphaGenome Variant Impact（AVI）评分，该评分结合了 AlphaGenome 和 AlphaMissense（IT之家注：谷歌用于预测改变蛋白质的 DNA 变异影响的模型）两者的预测优势，将两个模型的预测结果浓缩为单个数值，研究人员可以快速对变异进行排序，同时解读其分子效应。
AlphaGenome Atlas 是一个规模达 1 PB 的数据集，比 AlphaFold 数据库大 30 倍以上。该平台提供多个互相联动的资源：
- 分子效应预测：每个变异包含数千个分子效应预测，涵盖基因调控的多个重要方面，覆盖数百种人类和小鼠细胞类型与组织。
- AVI 评分：描述每个遗传变异影响的单一数值。
- AVI 特征归因：每个 AVI 评分都关联到驱动其结果的特定生物学特征，比如 AlphaGenome 预测的基因调控方面，或是 AlphaMissense 的蛋白质影响评分。
- DNA 序列基序：包含超过 2500 个重复性 DNA 序列（基因组的“词汇”）及其位置的完整合集。
AVI 评分同时适用于编码区（占基因组 2%，负责编码蛋白质）和非编码区（占基因组 98%，负责协调基因活性，容纳绝大多数性状相关变异），帮助研究人员根据潜在影响快速对变异进行评分和排序。测试显示，AVI 评分在多种变异致病性和罕见疾病基准测试中都展现出一流性能。
目前外部合作研究团队已经借助 AlphaGenome Atlas 取得多项实际成果：在罕见病研究中，博德研究所团队借助 AVI 评分筛选变异，发现了此前被忽略的、与癫痫性脑病密切相关的 DNM1 基因变异，实验验证确认了该预测结果；埃克塞特大学研究人员对英国生物样本库超过 54000 名参与者的全基因组数据进行分析，通过 AlphaGenome Atlas 发现了多 22% 的非编码基因关联，精准定位了调控关键蛋白质水平的特定变异。
AlphaGenome Atlas 今起通过门户网站、AlphaGenome API 向学术研究开放，也可作为技能在 Google Antigravity 使用，非商业研究可免费获取，后续还将在谷歌云开放商业使用权限。

title: 赛睿推出高端 Aeon Pro 无线手柄：搭载可更换电池与 OLED 屏幕，售价 259.99 美元
content:
9 月 8 日消息，对于许多游戏玩家来说，SteelSeries（赛睿）早已是一个耳熟能详的品牌，但在游戏手柄领域却并没有太强的存在感。与其先通过价格相对亲民的主机和 PC 手柄慢慢建立口碑，赛睿这次选择直接进入高端市场，推出售价 259.99 美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,749 元人民币）
的 Aeon Pro 无线手柄，支持 Xbox 和 PC，并于今日开始发货。
作为目前市场上价格最高的游戏手柄之一，Aeon Pro 究竟有什么其他产品没有的功能？答案是有一些，但并不算特别多。
用户最先注意到的，可能是手柄上的一块小型 OLED 屏幕，可以引导用户在 Xbox、PC 和蓝牙连接模式之间切换，同时也可以直接在手柄上调整大部分设置，包括针对不同游戏类型提供的预设方案。
用户还可以直接通过手柄重新映射按键，以及调整震动灵敏度。不过，一些更复杂的功能，例如调整摇杆死区和创建配置文件，仍然需要通过 PC 端的 SteelSeries GG 应用完成。
在游戏手柄上加入屏幕并不是一个全新的概念，但 Aeon Pro 的这块屏幕至少比较容易使用。
这款手柄最吸引人的功能，也是最实用的一项，是它采用了可更换电池系统。
Aeon Pro 随机附带两块电池，每块电池的续航时间约为 12 小时。备用电池可以放在随附的无线基站中充电。值得一提的是，这款电池实际上与赛睿高端 Arctis Nova Pro、Omni 和 Elite 耳机使用的是同一种电池。
无线基站配备两个 USB-C 接口，其中一个用于连接 Xbox，另一个用于连接 PC。基站可以自动切换连接来源，用户也可以直接通过手柄手动切换。
与其他专业级游戏手柄相比，Aeon Pro 在硬件方面并没有带来太多令人意外的设计。其配备霍尔效应摇杆和扳机，大部分输入按键采用机械开关，而不是传统的薄膜结构。因此，与标准 Xbox 手柄等产品相比，它能够提供更加清晰的按键触感和声音反馈。
手柄还提供两档扳机键行程限制。用户可以选择更短的扳机行程，将原本连续的模拟输入转换为更接近鼠标点击的触感。
手柄背面配备了四个背键拨片，这些拨片无法拆卸。赛睿表示，这是因为模块化设计的拨片通常容易出现松动和晃动的问题。因此，无论用户是否使用，这四个拨片都会一直保留在手柄上。
与其他按键一样，这些背键可以直接通过手柄进行映射，也可以通过 PC 端的 GG 软件进行设置。
不过，以 259.99 美元
（现汇率约合 1,749 元人民币）
的售价来看，Aeon Pro 理应附带一个拉链收纳包，但实际上并没有提供。
对于正在寻找替代产品的玩家来说，Valve 售价 99 美元
（现汇率约合 666.1 元人民币）
的 Steam Controller 是一款可定制程度更高的 PC 游戏手柄。
索尼 DualSense Edge 则比 Aeon Pro 便宜 60 美元
（现汇率约合 403.7 元人民币）
，同时也拥有不错的 PC 兼容性。
即使是在 Xbox 平台上，市场上也并不缺少价格更低、功能却同样强大的产品。
例如，8BitDo 推出的 Ultimate 3E 售价 149.99 美元
（现汇率约合 1,009 元人民币）
，虽然同样不算便宜，但它拥有 Aeon Pro 的许多核心功能，同时还提供模块化按键组件和额外的方向键模块。
不过，对于一家此前在游戏手柄领域几乎没有什么影响力的公司来说，Aeon Pro 的出现至少让赛睿获得了参与高端手柄竞争的资格。
接下来，或许可以期待赛睿继续推出适用于 PlayStation 和 Switch 平台的版本。
赛睿长期以来一直是许多玩家熟悉的游戏外设品牌，但游戏手柄并不是其传统强项。这次没有选择通过低价产品慢慢进入市场，而是直接凭借售价 259.99 美元
（现汇率约合 1,749 元人民币）
的 Aeon Pro 无线手柄挑战高端市场。至于这款产品能否凭借可更换电池、OLED 屏幕以及专业级硬件配置真正站稳脚跟，还有待市场进一步验证。

title: 高通与亚马逊达成合作，共同打造 AI 定制芯片与 1.6T 光互联解决方案
content:
IT之家 9 月 8 日消息，高通技术公司今日宣布与亚马逊达成一项跨多代产品的合作，双方将共同为大规模 AI 数据中心提供可规模化部署的定制芯片，并围绕 AI 推理展开合作。此外，两家公司还将共同开发最高支持 1.6T 速率的光互连解决方案，以及面向未来的下一代相关技术。
随着 AI 工作负载呈指数级增长，计算、存储、网络、内存带宽以及高能效基础设施的需求正以前所未有的速度提升。此次合作将结合亚马逊全面、安全且具有成本性能优势的 AI 基础设施，以及高通技术在低功耗处理、芯片设计和系统级集成领域的技术优势。
高通技术和亚马逊还将共同开发高性能光互连解决方案，以满足 AI 基础设施不断扩大的规模和带宽需求。双方的合作将利用高通的 SerDes 高速串行器 / 解串器技术和光学 DSP 技术。
作为扩大合作的一部分，高通技术计划进一步加大对 AWS AI 基础设施的使用，包括 Amazon Bedrock，并将其应用于电子设计自动化（EDA）工作负载，以缩短芯片设计周期。
高通公司总裁兼 CEO 克里斯蒂亚诺 · 阿蒙表示：“随着 AI 需求不断加速增长，数据中心基础设施需要在计算和互连两个方面同时取得进步，以实现更高性能和更高效率。高通很高兴与 AWS 围绕定制芯片和连接解决方案展开合作，将我们在先进处理和高能效计算领域数十年的技术积累应用其中，提供突破性的性能，并推动下一代 AI 基础设施的发展。”
AWS 副总裁 Prasad Kalyanaraman 表示：“与高通技术的这项合作建立在双方长期合作的坚实基础之上，也体现了我们共同推动技术边界的承诺。通过在定制芯片和先进连接技术领域开展合作，我们将为客户提供性能更强、效率更高、成本效益更出色的基础设施。”
此外，SEC 文件显示，高通公司和其子公司高通技术公司及其部分关联公司与亚马逊数据服务公司及其部分关联公司达成一项战略合作。高通已向亚马逊的关联公司签发一份认股权证，赋予权证持有人以每股 161.26 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,085 元人民币）的行权价，购买合计最多 25,000,000 股公司普通股（以下简称“权证股份”）的权利。
该权证允许以无现金方式行使，有效期至 2036 年 9 月 3 日。相关付款总额最高可达 600 亿美元（现汇率约合 4,037.06 亿元人民币），其中基于初始采购承诺，3,750,000 股已于权证签发时归属。
截至IT之家发稿，高通盘前股价涨超 8%。

title: Digitale Sicherheit zwischen Risiken, Recht und Regulierung: DigiSem 2026 am Weizenbaum-Institut
content:
Digitale Sicherheit zwischen Risiken, Recht und Regulierung: DigiSem 2026 am Weizenbaum-Institut
DigiSem 2026: Vier Institute für Digitalisierungsforschung (NifD) bringen Nachwuchswissenschaftler:innen zur digitalen Sicherheit in Berlin zusammen.
Wie lassen sich digitale Technologien sicher gestalten, ohne dabei individuelle Rechte und gesellschaftliche Selbstbestimmung einzuschränken? Mit dieser Frage beschäftigt sich das Digitalisation Research Seminar (DigiSem) 2026, das vom 21. bis 22. September am Weizenbaum-Institut in Berlin stattfindet. Gemeinsam laden das Bayerische Forschungsinstitut für Digitale Transformation (bidt), das Center for Advanced Internet Studies (CAIS), das Leibniz-Institut für Medienforschung | Hans-Bredow-Institut (HBI) und das Weizenbaum-Institut (WI) Doktorand:innen und Postdocs dazu ein, ihre Forschung zu digitaler Sicherheit vorzustellen und interdisziplinär zu diskutieren.
Im Mittelpunkt steht digitale Sicherheit als menschenzentriertes und interdisziplinäres Forschungsfeld. Dabei geht es um die Frage, welche Risiken digitale Technologien für Menschen und Gesellschaft mit sich bringen und wie sich diese Risiken begrenzen lassen. Dazu gehören etwa Diskriminierung und Verzerrungen durch digitale Systeme, Des- und Falschinformationen oder Situationen, in denen Nutzer:innen nur eingeschränkt nachvollziehen oder beeinflussen können, wie digitale Technologien eingesetzt werden. Auch die Frage, wie digitale Systeme so gestaltet und reguliert werden können, dass sie insbesondere vulnerable Gruppen – etwa Kinder – besser schützen, ist Teil des Seminars.
Ziel des zweitägigen Seminars ist es, den Austausch und die Vernetzung von Nachwuchswissenschaftler:innen über Fachgrenzen hinweg zu fördern. Im Mittelpunkt stehen konstruktives Feedback zu Forschungsarbeiten und der Austausch über gemeinsame Fragestellungen. Die Diskussionen sollen dazu beitragen, digitale Systeme sicherer, verantwortungsvoller und gesellschaftlich nachhaltiger zu gestalten.
Zwei Keynotes zu KI und Cyber-Resilienz
Einen Impuls setzt Prof. Dr. Lena Kästner, Professorin für Philosophie, Informatik und Künstliche Intelligenz an der Universität Bayreuth und Principal Investigator im bidt-Projekt FoGG. In ihrer Keynote „AI and the Safety Paradox: Convenience, Control, or Compromise?“ widmet sie sich dem Spannungsverhältnis zwischen Komfort, Kontrolle und Sicherheit beim Einsatz künstlicher Intelligenz.
Die zweite Keynote hält Dr. Jens Karschau, Referent im Bereich digitaler Verbraucherschutz beim Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI). Unter dem Titel „Cyber-Resilience: Bridging Consumer Protection, Smart Hardware, and the AI Frontier“ spricht er über die Sicherheit digitaler Ökosysteme für Verbraucher:innen, deren systemische Risiken und die wachsende Bedeutung Künstlicher Intelligenz.
DigiSem 2026 – Digitalisation Research Seminar
Wann: 21.–22. September 2026
Uhrzeit: 21.09.: ab 13 Uhr; 22.09: 09:00-14:30 Uhr.

Über das Netzwerk der Institute für Digitalisierungsforschung (NIfD)
Das Netzwerk der Institute für Digitalisierungsforschung (NIfD) vereint seit 2021 führende Einrichtungen in Deutschland, die die gesellschaftlichen, politischen und technologischen Folgen der digitalen Transformation interdisziplinär erforschen. Die Mitglieder des Netzwerks sind das Alexander von Humboldt Institut für Internet und Gesellschaft (HIIG), das Bayerische Forschungsinstitut für Digitale Transformation (bidt), das Center for Advanced Internet Studies (CAIS), das Leibniz-Institut für Medienforschung│Hans-Bredow-Institut (HBI), das Weizenbaum-Institut und das Zentrum verantwortungsbewusste Digitalisierung (ZEVEDI). Das Netzwerk stärkt seine Kooperation, Wissensaustausch und gemeinsame Initiativen, um die Digitalisierungsforschung in Deutschland sichtbar und wirksam zu machen.

title: Japan-Aufenthalt stärkt Forschungskooperationen
content:
Japan-Aufenthalt stärkt Forschungskooperationen
Professor Carsten Röcker hat bei einem mehrwöchigen Forschungsaufenthalt in Japan bestehende Kooperationen mit mehreren Hochschulen vertieft und neue Anknüpfungspunkte für gemeinsame Forschung identifiziert. Stationen waren die Yokohama City University, die Keio University in Tokio und das Toyota Technological Institute in Nagoya. Im Mittelpunkt standen Themen aus der Mensch-Technik-Interaktion, dem Service Design und der technologiegestützten Inklusion. Der Aufenthalt knüpft an langjährige Partnerschaften an und soll die gemeinsame Forschung weiter stärken.
Internationale Zusammenarbeit in der Mensch-Technik-Interaktion weiter ausgebaut
Professor Carsten Röcker hat bei einem mehrwöchigen Forschungsaufenthalt in Japan bestehende Kooperationen mit mehreren Hochschulen vertieft und neue Anknüpfungspunkte für gemeinsame Forschung identifiziert. Stationen waren die Yokohama City University, die Keio University in Tokio und das Toyota Technological Institute in Nagoya. Im Mittelpunkt standen Themen aus der Mensch-Technik-Interaktion, dem Service Design und der technologiegestützten Inklusion.
Professor Carsten Röcker vertritt an der TH OWL das Fachgebiet Mensch-Technik-Interaktion. Seine aktuellen Forschungsschwerpunkte liegen in den Bereichen inklusive Mensch-Technik-Interaktion, industrielle Assistenzsysteme und Technologieakzeptanz.
Vom Gastwissenschaftler zum langjährigen Forschungspartner
Eine der Kooperationen verbindet das inIT bereits seit mehreren Jahren mit Dr. Yutaro Nemoto. 2020 war Dr. Yutaro Nemoto für fünf Monate als Gastwissenschaftler am inIT tätig. Gemeinsame Interessen am Internet der Dinge, an menschenzentrierter Gestaltung und an der Entwicklung nutzerfreundlicher digitaler Technologien bildeten den Ausgangspunkt für gemeinsame Projekte und Publikationen. Heute ist Dr. Yutaro Nemoto Associate Professor an der Graduate School of International Management der Yokohama City University.
Im Forschungsprojekt SAIL – Sustainable Life-Cycle of Intelligent Socio-Technical Systems wurde die Zusammenarbeit weiter intensiviert. Dazu gehörten unter anderem die gemeinsame Organisation eines internationalen Workshops mit Beteiligung von SAIL-Promovierenden sowie mehrere wissenschaftliche Publikationen.
„Der besondere Wert internationaler Kooperationen zeigt sich dort, wo aus kontinuierlichem Austausch neue Forschung entsteht. In Japan konnten wir bestehende Themen vertiefen, unterschiedliche Ansätze miteinander verbinden und zugleich neue Anknüpfungspunkte für gemeinsame Forschung identifizieren“, sagt Professor Carsten Röcker.
Neue Impulse aus Robotik, Service Design und Inklusion
An der Graduate School of Media Design der Keio University tauschte sich Professor Carsten Röcker mit mehreren Forschenden zu aktuellen Ansätzen der Mensch-Technik-Interaktion aus. Dazu gehörte der Austausch mit Guillaume Gourmelen, Project Assistant Professor an der Keio University. Seine Forschung beschäftigt sich unter anderem mit Mensch-Roboter-Interaktion, Haptik und der Fernsteuerung technischer Systeme. Vor Ort testete Professor Carsten Röcker zudem einen Prototyp eines haptischen AR-Stuhls, der veranschaulicht, wie sich haptische Interaktion mit Augmented Reality verbinden lässt.
Mit Chihiro Sato, Associate Professor an der Keio University, standen unter anderem Service Design sowie die Verbindung physischer und digitaler Räume im Mittelpunkt. Professor Carsten Röcker nahm außerdem an einem Co-Design-Workshop mit älteren Menschen außerhalb Tokios teil, bei dem digitale Unterstützungstechnologien gemeinsam diskutiert und weiterentwickelt wurden.
Weitere Einblicke bot eine Feldstudie mit einem fliegenden Roboter zur Unterstützung sozialer Interaktion. Daraus ergeben sich Anknüpfungspunkte zur Forschung am inIT, insbesondere zur nutzerzentrierten Gestaltung und Evaluation neuer Assistenz- und Interaktionstechnologien.
Langjährige Kooperation mit dem Toyota Technological Institute
Eine weitere Station war das Intelligent Information Media Laboratory des Toyota Technological Institute in Nagoya. Dort traf Professor Carsten Röcker Professor Norimichi Ukita, mit dessen Forschungsgruppe das inIT bereits seit vielen Jahren zusammenarbeitet. Die Forschung des Labors beschäftigt sich unter anderem mit intelligenter Bildverarbeitung sowie der Analyse und Vorhersage menschlicher und robotischer Bewegungen.
Im Mittelpunkt des Besuchs standen aktuelle Forschungsthemen und die nächsten Schritte der gemeinsamen Arbeit. Für September ist ein einmonatiger Gegenbesuch eines Mitarbeiters aus der Forschungsgruppe von Professor Norimichi Ukita am inIT geplant. Dabei sollen bestehende Forschungsansätze gemeinsam weiterentwickelt und neue Kooperationsmöglichkeiten erschlossen werden.

Introducing our 35 Innovators Under 35 list for 2026
What will the next generation of science and technology look like? Our latest Innovators Under 35 list offers a glimpse.
Every year, we recognize 35 people from around the world who are doing groundbreaking scientific work and building clever technical fixes for sticky problems. By finding the top young innovators globally and learning what they’re focused on, we aim to give readers a sense of the advances to expect in the years to come.

Welcome to the spiderverse, a world measured through webs
Counting the creatures around us is critical for conservation, but it’s often a laborious, costly process that still leaves gaps. Environmental DNA, or eDNA, offers a promising alternative by analyzing genetic material shed by living things.
Recently, spiderwebs have emerged as an eDNA goldmine, as they trap material from their arachnid creators, their prey, and bio-detritus like saliva and pollen from nearby plants and animals. Studies found no passive tool matched spiderwebs’ ability to ID vertebrates.
