title: Strong advance of large-scale solar-storage projects across Mexico over the past month - Energy Storage
content: Mexico’s utility-scale solar pipeline is showing renewed activity, with a succession of projects entering environmental assessment or receiving conditional approval from the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (Semarnat). Projects identified by pv magazine Mexico since early August total more than 3 GW of planned PV capacity, with battery storage increasingly incorporated into new developments. The exact MW / MWh splits are not always published by Mexican authorities in environmental assessments or conditional approvals, but at least 800 MWh is disclosed, including La Morita III’s 270 MWh. Battery storage is a defining feature of this new project pipeline: most of the proposed plants include a BESS, and several specify three-hour storage configurations. Taken together, the nearly 20 projects identified by pv magazine Mexico over the past month represent more than 3 GW of planned solar capacity, stretching across 10 Mexican states and including projects ranging from around 42 MW to more than 370 MW, with several developments exceeding 200 MW. Trapiche Solar – Veracruz The 130 MWac Trapiche Solar project has entered environmental assessment in Soledad de Doblado, Veracruz. The development covers around 583.9 hectares and is designed to supply electricity to Mexico’s national power system. Its infrastructure includes a battery energy storage system, although the environmental documentation does not specify its power or energy capacity. The project will use a 34.5 kV collection system and a step-up substation to raise voltage to 115 kV, while its transmission line will undergo a separate environmental procedure. Espuela Solar – Guanajuato Espuela Solar , developed by Espuela New Energy in Dolores Hidalgo, Guanajuato, has also entered the environmental assessment process. The plant will have 130.3 MW of capacity and 110.295 MWac, based on 178,500 Trina Solar 730 W modules and 368 Huawei 330 kVA inverters. A battery storage facility is included in the design, although its MW and MWh ratings have not been disclosed. The project also incorporates 17 transformer stations and a substation raising voltage from 34.5 kV to 115 kV Delicias Solar – Guanajuato Semarnat has conditionally approved Delicias Solar, a combined solar, battery storage and green hydrogen development planned for San Luis de la Paz, Guanajuato. The PV facility will have a maximum net capacity of 42 MWac and use 120,792 crystalline-silicon modules, with estimated annual electricity production of around 200 GWh. The project also includes 35 MW of electrolysis capacity and is expected to produce approximately 3,205 tonnes of green hydrogen annually. A battery system forms part of the development, adding storage to the solar-to-hydrogen configuration. Cazadero Solar – Campeche The Mexican authorities have conditionally approved the 200 MW Cazadero Solar project in Escárcega, Campeche. The plant will comprise 635,622 bifacial PV modules and will be coupled with a battery energy storage system. Semarnat’s environmental resolution considers the development viable subject to several conditions, including securing authorization for changes in land use on forested areas. The approval provides three years for construction and establishes a 35-year operating period. Chabacanes Solar – Veracruz Semarnat has granted conditional environmental approval to Chabacanes Solar , a project developed by Solarig Development México in Ozuluama de Mascareñas, Veracruz. The facility will have 75.1 MW of PV capacity and 50 MW of nominal AC capacity. It will be paired with a 6 MW/12 MWh battery energy storage system capable of two hours of discharge. The environmental authorization allows five years for site preparation and construction, followed by 30 years of operation and maintenance. Rancho Empacadora I – Tamaulipas Greendat Capital has submitted the Rancho Empacadora solar project for environmental assessment in Altamira, Tamaulipas. The planned facility will have 300 MW of installed solar capacity, making it one of the largest projects in the latest group of filings. Its design comprises a PV field, inverters, transformer stations, a step-up substation, control facilities, a high-voltage transmission line and a battery energy storage system. The documents made public by the environmental authorities do not state the MW or MWh capacity of the BESS. La Morita I – Nuevo León Greendat Capital is also behind La Morita I , a 100.2 MW solar project proposed in the municipality of China, Nuevo León. The facility has entered Semarnat’s environmental impact assessment process and will occupy approximately 223 hectares within a much larger project area. Its planned infrastructure includes PV modules, inverters, transformer stations, a step-up substation, a high-voltage line and battery storage. The environmental filing confirms the BESS but does not disclose its power, energy capacity or discharge duration. La Morita II – Nuevo León The neighboring La Morita II project, promoted by Tusae Energy II, is also undergoing environmental assessment in China, Nuevo León. The project will have 227.847 MW of capacity and use 312,120 modules rated at 730 W, together with 667 inverters. Its design includes 23 transformer stations as well as a battery storage system, substations, internal roads and control infrastructure. As with La Morita I, the available environmental documents do not specify the MW or MWh capacity of the battery system. La Morita III – Nuevo León La Morita III , planned in China, Nuevo León, has entered Semarnat’s environmental impact assessment process. The project will have 373.416 MW of PV capacity and 300 MW of nominal capacity, using 511,530 modules rated at 730 Wp and 1,000 300 kW inverters. It will be coupled with a 90 MW/270 MWh battery energy storage system designed for three hours of discharge, equivalent to 30% of the plant’s nominal power. A 34/400 kV step-up substation and an approximately 2.5 km, 400 kV transmission line will connect the facility to CFE’s Presa Grande substation, while the planned operating life is 25 years. Santos – Nuevo León Greendat Capital’s Santos solar-plus-storage project has been submitted for environmental assessment in Anáhuac, Nuevo León. The facility will have 126.078 MW capacity and around 100 MW of nominal output. It will be paired with a 30 MW/90 MWh BESS designed to provide three hours of storage. The project site is located approximately 20 km northwest of the municipal center of Anáhuac and adds to a growing concentration of solar-plus-storage proposals in Nuevo León. San Agustín – Zacatecas Transformaes Creación Sostenible has submitted the San Agustín Solar Park for environmental assessment in Zacatecas. The project combines 64.47 MWp of PV capacity with 48.88 MWh of battery storage and will occupy a 121.34-hectare site. Around 70.6 hectares will be occupied by the photovoltaic field, while the BESS will use approximately 0.46 hectares. The developer estimates total investment in the project at $72.88 million. Lagartija – State of Mexico Developer Genux has been awarded the Lagartija PV project in the State of Mexico through Mexico’s 2026 binding planning process. Lagartija and the accompanying Ocelote project will together provide 201 MW of solar capacity and will both incorporate battery energy storage systems. Genux has not disclosed an individual capacity split between the two projects or the power and energy ratings of their batteries. Combined investment in the developments is expected to reach approximately $165 million, with estimated annual generation of around 490 GWh. Ocelote – State of Mexico Ocelote is the second State of Mexico project awarded to Genux under the same 2026 planning process. Together with Lagartija, it forms a 201 MW solar portfolio that will include battery storage, although the developer has yet to disclose the individual PV capacity assigned to each site or detailed BESS specifications. Genux expects the pair to produce approximately 490 GWh of electricity annually, which it says is equivalent to the consumption of more than 150,000 Mexican households. The two projects represent an estimated combined investment of about $165 million. Barajas Solar – Coahuila Barajas Solar , promoted by Armería New Energy in Frontera, Coahuila, has entered Semarnat’s environmental assessment procedure. The development will have 130.3 MW of PV capacity, 110.4 MWac and a net capacity of 100.2 MW at the point of interconnection. Its 178,472 bifacial modules will be complemented by a 34.5 MW/103.5 MWh battery storage system, providing three hours of energy storage. The developer estimates investment at MXN 2.38 billion ($130 million). El Gorrión – Coahuila El Gorrión , a solar-plus-storage project promoted by Tusae Energy I, has entered environmental assessment in Saltillo, Coahuila. The facility will have 125.88 MW of DC capacity, 100.2 MW of installed AC capacity and nominal output limited to 100 MW, using 172,440 modules rated at 730 W. The environmental filing declares a lithium-ion BESS rated at 30 MW/90 MWh for three hours of storage, although the detailed equipment breakdown adds up to 25 MW, a discrepancy that remains to be clarified. The project will occupy 226.47 hectares and connect to existing CFE infrastructure through a 34/115 kV step-up substation and an approximately 1 km, 115 kV transmission line. title: BYD cuts Denza Z9 GT EV prices with the new e3 Premium trim, starting at about $50,000
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 9 2026 - 7:13 am PT
launched the new Denza Z9 GT e3 Premium, a lower-priced version of its top-selling electric luxury GT, starting at about $50,000.
BYD launches lower-priced Denza Z9 GT e3 Premium
We knew it was coming. Li Hui, Denza’s general manager,
confirmed earlier this week
that a new “lightweight” variant of the tri-motor EV would go on sale on September 9.
Denza launched the new Denza Z9 GT e3 Flash Charge Premium Edition on Wednesday, as a more affordable option to the range-topping e3 Performance model.
Like the Performance version, the new Premium trim is based on BYD’s e3 platform. The setup uses three electric motors: one 230 kW (308 hp) motor up front and two 310 kW (415 hp) motors in the rear, delivering a combined 770 kW (1,032 hp) and 1,210 Nm (892 lb-ft) of torque.
Denza said the tri-motor setup enables it to accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h (0 to 62 mph) in just 2.8 seconds.
While the Performance version still beats it by 0.1 seconds (2.7 seconds 0 to100 km/h), the new e3 Premium is about $6,000 (40,000 yuan) cheaper.
The new Denza Z9 GT e3 Premium starts at 329,800 yuan in China, or about $49,000, compared to the Performance version, which starts at 369,800 yuan ($55,000).
Denza Z9 GT prices by trim in China (Source: Denza)
Powered by a 122.5 kWh BYD Blade Battery 2.0, the new Premium trim offers a CLTC range of up to 860 km (534 miles), beating the Performance with up to 820 km (509 miles).
It also has BYD’s Flash Charging technology, which lets it charge from 10% to 70% in 5 minutes. A full charge (10% to 97%) takes just 9 minutes.
To offer it at a lower price, the new Premium trim does have a few equipment changes from the Performance variant. For one, it trades the carbon-ceramic brake discs for cast-iron discs and uses different wheels.
BYD Denza Z9 GT interior (Source: BYD)
The new Denza Z9 GT e3 Premium is the same size as the other trims, measuring 5,195 mm in length, 1,990 mm in width, and 1,480 mm in height, with a 3,125 mm wheelbase.
Like the other version, the new model comes standard with premium features, including its God’s Eye 5.0 driving assistance technology and DiSus-A dual-chamber air suspension system.
According to Li, the new Z9 GT has been China’s top-selling luxury GT for several consecutive months after it went on sale earlier this year.
Denza Z9 GT (Source: Denza)
BYD also sells the
Denza Z9 GT in Europe
, starting at €115,000 ($134,500) in Germany, and in the UK, where it’s available starting at £95,000 for the plug-in hybrid (PHEV) and £105,000 for the fully electric version.
Whether or not BYD will launch the new Denza Z9 GT EV Premium model overseas has yet to be confirmed.
In Europe and the UK, BYD’s luxury electric GT has a WLTP driving range of up to 599 km (372 miles).

title: Data confirms Autopilot/FSD was active in crash that killed a mother, passerby saved her baby
content:
Tesla Autopilot
Tesla Full self-Driving
Fred Lambert
| Sep 9 2026 - 7:12 am PT
A 2021 Tesla Model Y left an Alabama highway, hit two trees, and caught fire, killing its driver, 29-year-old Kayleigh Page. Her 7-month-old daughter was pulled from the burning car by a stranger who saw it happen.
Troopers reported it as a single-vehicle wreck. What they didn’t say, and likely didn’t know, is that Tesla’s own data shows the car’s driver-assist system was engaged. This is part of an
ongoing Electrek investigation
matching reported crashes to Tesla’s redacted NHTSA data.
What happened on Highway 157
Around 7:40 p.m. on Sunday, December 7, 2025, a 2021 Tesla Model Y Long Range was heading along Alabama Highway 157 near the Cullman County line, about a mile north of Battleground in Morgan County. The car left the roadway, struck two trees, and caught fire, according to the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency.
The driver,
Kayleigh Page, 29
, of Waterloo, was pronounced dead at the scene. Her infant daughter, a passenger, was hurt but survived, and a passerby who witnessed the crash rescued the baby from the vehicle, Morgan County Sheriff Ron Puckett said. The child was hospitalized in stable condition.
State troopers worked it as a routine fatal wreck. No report mentioned Autopilot, “Full Self-Driving,” or any driver-assist system. To the public, it was a car that ran off the road.
What Tesla told the federal government
Under a NHTSA Standing General Order, automakers must report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact. Tesla filed one on this crash.
In it, Tesla identifies the car as a 2021 Model Y and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as
“Verified Engaged”
— meaning it confirmed through its own telematics that the system was active. It logs a pre-crash speed of
and records a fatality. It says it holds the
event-data recorder and telematics
Then it redacts the three fields that would explain the crash: the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating area. All blacked out as “confidential business information,” the
same redactions Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports
. It even left the “crash with” and roadway fields marked “unknown,” so its own filing doesn’t say the car hit trees.
A road departure, the most common Tesla driver-assist crash
This is the failure mode that shows up more than any other. Electrek’s analysis of the full NHTSA dataset found that of the Tesla driver-assist crashes where the pre-crash movement is disclosed,
the single largest category is the car leaving its lane or the road,
well ahead of rear-ends or turns. A Tesla drifting off a highway and into the trees is not an outlier in this data. It’s the pattern.
We can’t say whether this was basic Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving,” because Tesla redacted the software version. On a rural two-lane highway at 55 mph, either could have been engaged. Basic Autopilot holds a lane and a speed on roads like this, and FSD does too. Both have documented failures where the car wandered out of its lane. The field that would tell us which system was steering is the one Tesla blacked out.
Why we keep doing this
Tesla is, more aggressively than ever, encouraging owners to treat a Level 2 driver-assistance system as if it drives itself. It sells the software as “Full Self-Driving,” Elon Musk keeps promising unsupervised autonomy is months away, and the branding invites drivers to trust the car.
Around the time of the crash, Musk even suggested that Tesla drivers could look at their phones when using FSD.
But it is still Level 2. The human is driving and responsible at all times, and Tesla’s own actions confirm it: consumer FSD still requires supervision, and its robotaxi service is a small, closely monitored fleet. That gap between the marketing and the machine breeds the complacency that gets people killed.
The redaction makes it worse. At the moment Tesla is telling owners to trust the car, it’s hiding the records that would show how the system behaves when things go wrong. What’s confirmed here is narrow and real: a driver-assist system was engaged when this car left the road and a young mother died. Everything that would explain how, Tesla sealed.
How we matched it:
the NHTSA record is unredacted on location (Vinemont/Morgan County), state, vehicle (2021 Model Y), the fatality, and the month. Tesla logs the incident time as 02:09 UTC, which converts to about 8:09 p.m. local, inside the window troopers reported, who put the crash between roughly 7:40 and 8:46 p.m. It’s the only fatal Tesla crash in that area that month. It’s the same crash. Electrek has reached out to the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency for the crash report and the vehicle data, and asked whether investigators received Tesla’s raw telemetry or only Tesla’s own interpretation of it.

title: RGNT’s 85 MPH retro electric motorcycle just got a scrambler makeover
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Sep 9 2026 - 2:42 am PT
Swedish electric motorcycle maker RGNT has expanded its lineup with a new scrambler version of its retro-inspired electric motorcycle, adding a bit more off-road attitude without messing too much with the formula underneath.
The new RGNT Street Scrambler joins the existing
Street Classic
, a model we’ve been covering since it was first unveiled
over six years ago
. The two share essentially the same electric drivetrain and battery options, but the new Scrambler model gets several changes aimed at riders who occasionally want to leave the pavement behind.
The most obvious differences are the Scrambler’s 18-inch front wheel, up from the Classic’s 17-incher, along with chunkier 18 x 2.5-inch on/off-road rubber up front. The rear remains a fat 17 x 3-inch tire. The Scrambler also gets a raised and wider handlebar, while the ride height increases by 20mm. Ground clearance rises from 230mm to 260mm, and seat height increases from 810mm to 830mm.
Those aren’t exactly Dakar Rally modifications, but they should make the bike considerably happier on gravel roads and light trails while maintaining the classic motorcycle proportions that make RGNT’s bikes stand out.
Underneath, things are familiar. Both versions use RGNT’s 46 kW direct-drive rear hub motor producing a claimed 540 Nm of peak torque. Top speed is 135 km/h (84 mph), while 0-100 km/h (0-62 mph) takes 3.9 seconds.
The standard 8.3 kWh battery is rated for 139 km (86 miles) of range, while an optional 10.1 kWh long-range pack stretches that figure to 170 km (106 miles). Despite its fairly accessible appearance, the battery is fixed rather than removable.
Charging is handled through a Type 2 connector common across Europe, with the standard 1.8 kW onboard charger providing a full charge in 4 hours and 35 minutes.
An optional 6 kW charger cuts that to 1 hour and 25 minutes, or around 50 minutes for a 20-80% charge. The company refers to it as nearly a “full tank” in the time it takes for a coffee stop, but that’s some mighty slow sipping. As far as motorcycle recharges go though, under an hour for most of a charge is still fairly impressive, especially for AC charging. This won’t be a touring bike any time soon, but for commuters and occasional trail riders, the recharge time is decently quick with that faster charger upgrade.
An on-board 6 kW charger offers a mostly-filled battery in under an hour – for an extra €1,895
Other modern touches hide behind the decidedly old-school styling, including ABS, traction control, regenerative braking, keyless starting, full LED lighting, and a 3-inch circular display supporting Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
RGNT has been pursuing this combination of vintage motorcycle design and modern electric drivetrain technology for several years now. Founded in Sweden, the company builds its motorcycles in Gothenburg, leaning heavily into a handcrafted, small-production approach rather than trying to compete with mass-market motorcycle manufacturers on volume. Earlier this year, the company announced that it had over 600 motorcycles on European streets.
That handcrafted approach isn’t cheap, but the bikes also aren’t offensively expensive, either. The Street Classic
starts at €8,995
, while the new Street Scrambler starts at €9,495. Buyers can reserve a build with a €100 deposit, with options including the larger battery, faster charger, heated grips, luggage rack, windscreen, and side bag system.
For an extra €500 over the Classic, the Scrambler seems like an interesting way to add some dirt-road capability without losing the handsome retro styling that is arguably RGNT’s biggest calling card.
The bikes are currently only available in Europe, but RGNT has announced that it expects to enter the US market in 2027 with prices starting at US $9,995, meaning there could be RGNT Street Scramblers cruising around US streets sooner rather than later.

title: 中创新航合肥研究院签约落地，将开展锂电池及相关产品的研发与实验测试业务
content:
9月8日下午，长丰县政府与中创新航在合肥市政务中心签署合作协议，中创新航合肥研究院正式落地。该项目建设内容包括中试线、研发实验室、实验测试中心，将开展锂电池及相关产品的研发与实验测试业务。
中创新航董事长刘静瑜表示，合肥研究院将建成体系完备的综合性研发平台，未来将引进超2000名研发人才，构建起“技术研发-中试验证-产品测试”的全链条创新闭环，并深化与合肥本地高校院所、龙头企业的协同创新，推动更多关键核心技术在合肥原创突破、落地转化。
据了解，中创新航是全球领先的新能源科技企业。2021年，中创新航合肥基地落地开工，目前一期、二期已建成投产，三期即将投产，四期正加快建设。合肥基地全部达产后，将成为中创新航全国最大生产基地，可带动就业近万人。

content:
集邦光储观察获悉，卫蓝新能源近期披露多项业务进展，包括储能项目落地、与大型国企签约合作、Pre-IPO上市筹备等动态。
10.44MWh工商业储能项目完成并网
9月8日，卫蓝新能源披露，广东惠州伟志电子10.44MWh储能电站项目实现并网投运。
该项目由惠州市曜晖综合智慧能源有限公司开发建设，面向惠州伟志电子工商业用电场景。项目分工上，卫蓝新能源供应储能电芯，国瑞协创承担储能系统集成与设备交付，为卫蓝新能源在华南工商业储能领域的落地项目。
该项目采用无追索权项目融资模式。融资、抵押以及追索范围仅限定于项目公司自身资产、设备、收益与权益，不涉及开发商、股东及母公司表内资产。如若项目无法偿付融资，出资方不对项目主体以外主体进行追偿，依靠项目资产与运营收益形成独立融资闭环，为工商业储能领域市场化融资提供实践样本。

IPO辅导已完成备案
资本市场层面，卫蓝新能源资本化工作持续推进。卫蓝新能源成立至今完成9轮融资，2025年9月完成D+轮融资，投资方包含工银资本、国开金融以及多地能源、产业投资基金。
2026年，卫蓝新能源启动Pre-IPO轮融资，计划募资规模约20亿元，对应投前估值200亿元。卫蓝在2025年12月完成创业板IPO辅导备案，目标登陆A股创业板。从后续发展规划来看，卫蓝新能源还将联合产业链上下游合作伙伴，加快工商业储能、电网侧储能、新能源配储等多场景储能方案的规模化落地。

中科海钠签署10GWh钠电长期供货协议
9月2日，中科海钠与韩国VOLTA株式会社正式签署战略合作协议，双方将在此前15MWh储能项目合作基础上，进一步推进5年10GWh钠离子电池长期供货协议。
根据协议，中科海钠将向VOLTA供应钠离子电芯，产品将覆盖大储、工商储及户储等应用场景。VOLTA负责系统集成及韩国本土市场推广，韩国光云大学参与技术验证、研发及测试。

title: 'Deeply Alarmed': Trump Administration Slams Ford's Deal With Chinese Battery Company
content:
'Deeply Alarmed': Trump Administration Slams Ford's Deal With Chinese Battery Company
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy pressed Ford CEO Jim Farley to stop working with Chinese companies in a letter on Tuesday.
- DOT Secretary Sean Duffy sent Ford CEO Jim Farley a letter urging the automaker to reconsider its deals with Chinese companies.
- Duffy slammed Ford's licensing deal with CATL to make batteries in Michigan.
- Ford said it owns and operates the plant and called the letter a "wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines."
In a letter sent to Ford CEO Jim Farley that was shared on Tuesday, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy expressed "profound concern" at the automaker's deals with Chinese companies and pressed Farley to cut ties with the country.
"While DOT recognizes the intense competitive pressures of the global market, the Company's recent strategic decisions paint a troubling picture of a foundational American brand actively intertwining its future with Chinese state-backed enterprises," Duffy said.
Duffy called out a few of Ford's deals with Chinese companies, which are at the forefront of global battery and vehicle manufacturing. He pointed to a partnership with Geely that lets the Chinese company manufacture cars at a Ford plant in Spain. He criticized Ford's decision to continue manufacturing some Lincolns in China until 2030. And he took aim at Ford's technology licensing deal with CATL, under which the automaker is producing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries at a new plant in Michigan. China, and CATL in particular, leads the world in production of LFP batteries, which are durable, cheaper cells that have boomed in popularity in recent years.
"DOT remains deeply alarmed by Ford's continued reliance on licensed technology from Chinese battery manufacturer CATL at the operational BlueOval Battery Park facility in Marshall, Michigan," Duffy wrote.
The Ford Fathom will use LFP batteries supplied through the CATL licensing deal.
In a response shared with InsideEVs, the carmaker noted that the plant is owned, controlled, and staffed by Ford. "While others continue to import Chinese batteries, Ford is investing to build batteries here in America. The CATL arrangement is a limited technology-licensing and services agreement, not a joint venture or foreign-owned manufacturing operation," the company said.
Ford also called the letter "a wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines" and pointed out that the White House praised the battery plant in a press release mere days ago.
The CATL ties made the plant politically contentious from the start. Today it is ramping up battery production and will make LFP batteries for Ford's upcoming $30,000 EV pickup, the Fathom.
Pushback against Chinese cars and carmakers has intensified in Washington as of late, becoming practically the only issue that both sides of the aisle can agree on. A new bill that would bar companies with more than a 15% Chinese ownership stake from selling cars in the U.S. passed the Senate Commerce Committee in July with unanimous bipartisan support. That would go into effect on top of existing rules banning certain Chinese vehicle technologies (which forced Polestar out of the U.S.), and in addition to a 100% tariff on Chinese-made cars. Both of those policies on the books were Biden-era initiatives.
There's an irony to Washington's effort to wall off America from Chinese cars. As China further cements its astonishing lead in EVs, Republicans in the U.S. have drastically pulled back federal support for that industry. Critics of the administration's policies say that puts America on the back foot when it comes to the automotive industry of the future.

title: Audi Wants To Sweeten Your EV Lease Buyout Deal With Up to $10,000 Off
content:
Audi must really want its EV lessees to hold onto their cars after their leases are up.
Photo by:
6:10pm ET
If you're currently the lessee of an Audi E-tron model and you're wondering what you're going to get when its lease expires, you might want to reconsider just keeping your current car. According to
CarsDirect
, Audi sent out a bulletin to all dealers nationwide, informing them of a new incentive for EV lessees who decide to buy their car out after their leases, starting September 1. And, depending on how expensive your E-tron model is, Audi will take as much as $10,000 off your buyout price.
That top-dollar $10,000 buyout discount is only available on the
Audi E-tron GT
. Lesser models like the discontinued Q8
Q4 E-tron
get lesser discounts, to the tune of $5,000 and $4,000, respectively. Audi has actually been offering EV buyout incentives since July, 2026, but it increased the Q4 E-tron's discount, as it was $3,000 before. There's no discount for the
A6 E-tron,
though, as that car hasn't even been out long enough for leases to mature.
Unless customers don't like their E-trons, I can see this being a popular discount. Audi E-tron secondhand values have been plummeting, with cars losing at least half of their value to depreciation in just a year or two. You can find
three-year-old E-tron GTs
for less than $50,000 with low miles, so depending on what their original buyout price was, this discount could push many customers in that direction.
This program won't last long. Audi says it goes only until the end of September, so if you're an Audi E-tron owner, strike now. It's always fun getting a new car every three years, and one of the main reasons why so many customers lease. However, these discounts could make your current Audi cheap enough to hold onto.

title: China's Best-Selling EV Can Drift Really Well
content:
China's Best-Selling EV Can Drift Really Well
The Geely EX2 Track and EX2 Street concepts are meant to show off the potential of EV enthusiast customization.
- The Geely EX2 Street and EX2 Track are two concepts introduced in Brazil meant to show the potential of electric enthusiast driving and modifications.
- The Geely EX2 Track has a hydraulic handbrake to make drifting easier.
- The EX2 is rear wheel drive, powered by a 114 horsepower motor.
China’s best-selling car, the Geely EX2 (or E2, in some European markets), has made waves all across the world for being a generally pleasant small EV for not much money. Roughly the same size as a Honda Fit, this small hatchback is often one of the cheapest new EV options wherever it is sold. But how it drives has never been its strong suit. I drove one this year and thought the experience was pleasant, but not all that interesting.
But that could soon change. Recently, Geely introduced the EX2 to the Brazilian market, and it revealed two hotted up concept versions for the country's Festival Interlagos last month. The event features fast cars and exhibition laps, but also showcases from manufacturers. This year, the EX2 Street and EX2 Track concepts made their debut.
Geely EX2 Street
The EX2 Street is the more production-viable version of the two. Geely took the EX2, put it on lowered suspension, and upgraded the wheels to 17-inchers. The interior traded its synthetic leather for real leather, and swapped its light-colored headliner for a darker one made of Alcantara.
The EX2 Track takes things further. For starters, the car is painted with aggressive, yet cartoonish, graphics; a front jagged mouth decal with teeth feels right at home with the comic-book-style Geely EX2 logo. The EX2 Track is just as low as its EX2 Street sibling, but the indigo wheels stand out.
Gallery: Geely EX2 Track
The interior has been gutted behind the front seats, and in its place is now a roll cage. The front seats now have five-point harnesses. Also, there’s a hydraulic parking brake, equipped with a comically long lever to engage it. The 114 horsepower motor and 40 kWh battery are unchanged, but Geely says the chassis stability and suspension tune make the car more track worthy.
This isn’t all just for show, either, as if Geely’s making a joke out of making a small, cheap EV turn into a drift car. It’s been seen on social media immolating its tires and doing donuts.
Many small and cheap EVs, like the BYD Seagull, are front-wheel-drive and not really suitable for getting sideways. The Geely EX2 is rear-wheel-drive, has independent suspension, and has disc brakes on all four wheels for corners. On paper, this sounds like all the right elements to be able to get pretty rowdy when pushed. Brazilian YouTube channel ACF figured out as much about a month ago.
Geely says the EX2 Track and Street aren’t planned for production. But they do show what’s possible for electric vehicle customization, which I think is very important.
Right now, EVs still have a reputation for being soulless and boring appliances. Sporty driving EVs do exist, but they’re expensive. This Geely EX2 is relatively affordable, at a $24,000 base price in Brazil, making it one of the country's cheapest EVs. And if you can turn something like that into a rowdy track car with a few adjustments, then it's clear that car customization and driving enjoyment won't evaporate with the advent of EVs.

title: Is This Mullen Five Concept Car From A Failed Startup Worth Your Money?
content:
Is it possible to make it roadworthy? I don't know, but now's the chance to find out.
Photo by:
Facebook Marketplace
1:59pm ET
You're forgiven for not knowing what a Mullen Five is. The upstart American electric automaker debuted a concept car a few years back as a sort of Tesla competitor, but it never made it past that phase and never even came close to becoming a production car. In fact, there's no evidence that there were even batteries, motors, or even fully functioning vehicle chassis that were anywhere close to production-ready. However, despite the brand's failures, you can actually buy one of Mullen's concept cars (it might be the only one), because one was just listed for sale on
Facebook Marketplace
Where to even begin with Mullen? Here's the brief rundown of Mullen's short-lived but messy existence. The American automaker was mostly going to rebadge Chinese EVs and went public in 2020, but its share price plummeted the following year. It bought a production facility in Mississippi, but never built anything there. It initially had the idea for an electric crossover type thing that would compete with the
called the MX-05, but then it changed the name to just "Five." In 2022, shareholders sued the company and Mullen had to pay out $7.25 million. Then, it bought the controlling stake of
Bollinger Motors
, changed its name to Bollinger Innovations, shut down Bollinger Motors in 2025, and then ultimately went into receivership in 2026. In a nutshell, Mullen doesn't exist anymore.
The Mullen Five was supposed to launch in 2024 and there was even an ultra-fast
Mullen Five RS
announced. This concept car is all that's left of the brand's plans to take on the Model Y and it's barely even a car. While the Marketplace ad shows a video of it driving, it's unclear if it's even built on a roadworthy chassis. It might just be a rolling shell for auto show stands.
Photo by: Facebook Marketplace
As it stands, it only has a top speed of 15 mph, as it's powered by five lead-acid 12-volt batteries in a series. However, it does have a Brembo brake kit that's supposed to be for a BMW M2, but that's hard to prove from Facebook photos. It's also said to ride on coilover suspension, though it doesn't say what kind, and it has 23-inch wheels.
It does have a full interior that seems at least close to production-ready and, dare I say, it actually looks kind of nice. So if someone can put an actual EV powertrain in it, and not just a bunch of 12-volt batteries, maybe it can be a fun, super unique project car. Looking at the batteries under the hood, it's hard to tell what can fit under there or whether it's actually capable of being roadworthy. Since Mullen planned on rebadging Chinese EVs, it's possible that it's a real car underneath, just minus a powertrain.
Is it worth $8,000 to buy this concept car from a defunct upstart just to do an EV powertrain swap? I'm not so sure. There are plenty of cool cars that can be had for cheaper that still serve the same purpose. However, there may not be another Mullen of any kind on the road, so this could be your chance to have something that even the richest people in the world don't have.

title: LG’s Experimental LMR Battery Retained 92% Capacity After 883 Cycles
content:
LG’s Experimental LMR Battery Retained 92% Capacity After 883 Cycles
Researchers tackled a durability problem in cheaper LMR batteries by changing how the cells are charged and discharged.
- LG found ways to improve LMR battery durability by changing operating voltages and the manufacturing process.
- LMR promises lower costs than nickel-rich batteries and higher energy density than LFP.
- The results are promising, but charging speed, cold weather performance, and real-world longevity remain unproven.
Cheaper EV batteries sound great until they start forgetting how to be a battery. That has been one of the main headaches with lithium manganese-rich (LMR) batteries, one of the most promising alternatives to lower-cost chemistries such as lithium iron phosphate (LFP). They hold plenty of promise for cost and energy density, but questions remain about how long they last.
LG Energy Solution and Seoul National University provided a useful answer to at least part of that problem. Their experimental LMR cells retained an impressive 92.2% of their initial energy after 883 charge-discharge cycles. EVs are typically expected to last between 1,000 and 2,000 charge cycles.
“This study identified the causes of degradation in LMR batteries from the perspective of oxygen reversibility and demonstrated that cell stability can be improved through electrochemical protocol design alone," Professor Jongwoo Lim of Seoul National University said in the study. "We confirmed that achieving long-term stability in LMR batteries requires comprehensive consideration of not only charging conditions but also discharge conditions.”
LMR is another member of the lithium-ion family, with a cathode that leans heavily on manganese. This chemistry’s appeal is easy to explain: manganese is cheaper and more abundant than nickel and cobalt. Use more of it, and you reduce the expensive ingredients, while also potentially getting a battery that is not only cheap but also performs just as well as a typical nickel cobalt manganese (NCM) battery.
In these latest experiments, LG tried to better control oxygen reactions inside the cathode. Oxygen is what helps LMR store energy, but the reactions it causes inside the cell need to reverse during discharge, or else they can damage the structure and cause gas buildup, which is not something you want inside a tightly packed battery cell.
The researchers changed the operating voltages to better control those reactions. Lowering the charging cutoff from 4.6 to 4.3 volts improved oxygen recovery from 86% to 97%. Allowing discharge down to 2 volts instead of 3 volts also helped. LG paired those adjustments with a lower-temperature formation process, which is the initial conditioning cells undergo during manufacturing. This optimized protocol also helped reduce both gas generation and structural damage.
LG explains that “This research addresses one of the key challenges facing LMR batteries. It demonstrates that stable battery life can be secured even in large-format cells by effectively suppressing gas generation, providing an important foundation for growth in the next-generation LMR battery market.”
Some automakers are already heavily invested in LMR. GM expects substantial cost savings from implementing this chemistry in its production EVs. However, cheaper ingredients only get you so far. LMR batteries have struggled with capacity loss and declining voltage, both of which reduce a battery's energy output.
GM has projected 33% higher energy density than LFP at comparable cost for its own LMR cells. The promise of LMR is one reason the company is reconsidering whether LFP even belongs in its future EV lineup. GM and LG had previously announced plans for U.S. LMR production in 2028.
But while this new research from LG is encouraging, the company hasn’t yet demonstrated whether its LMR cells beat production LFP batteries on charging speed, cold-weather performance, or lifespan. This is progress nevertheless, and it keeps LMR batteries on the radar, but until we see them in a production EV, we won’t know how much of that promise survives the trip from the lab to your driveway.

title: Tesla Cybercab's Backup Steering Wheel Is A Giant On-Screen Joystick
content:
Tesla hid a virtual steering wheel inside of the Cybercab's giant infotainment screen.
Photo by:
Matthew Skrzypczak / X
12:40pm ET
Tesla's Cybercab might not have a steering wheel, but there's still a way to steer it.
A rider found a car with a hidden menu showing off a joystick-like control pad on the screen.
The rider said that it was for moving the car at low speeds of up to 7 MPH.
Tesla Cybercab is here
and just like Elon Musk promised, it's rolling out without a steering wheel. It also has no pedals to step on, no stalks to flick, or knobs to turn. It's all screen.
Well, it turns out that there is a backup way to move the vehicle
without needing to plug in an Xbox controller
. A new video shows a hidden service menu inside of the Cybercab with a virtual joystick. It seems to allow a driver to control the steering and acceleration of the car using just their index finger.
X user Matthew Skrzypczak says that he happened to hop in a Cybercab where the menu was left up for anyone to see.
"When I got in the vehicle, the display was in a different configuration with a virtual joystick for manual driving," said Skrzypczak in a
post on X
. "I have a feeling I wasn’t supposed to see this… but I try to manually drive the vehicle anyway!"
The video shows Skrzypczak fiddling with some menu items and attempting to move the joystick. The actual controls seem simple: slide the joystick "Forward" and move forward. Drag left or right while holding the directional pad up or down to control the direction of the wheels. Unfortunately for Skrzypczak, the car didn't respond to the movement. It's unclear if there was a another step that needed to be taken before the car could move.
On the display, a row of Superchargers can be seen in view of the car's rear-facing cameras. He hypothesizes that's where the manual controls were last used, as the controls would allow the car to move "up to 7 mph." This tracks with a
video posted just over a week ago
that shows a Cybercab operator steering the car using the touch screen—but this latest look actually shows the interface that operator was using up close.
Skrzypczak wasn't the only Cybercab rider to gtt into a cab with the manual controls displayed and unsuccessfully try to use them.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
It makes sense that Tesla would have a way to manually move a vehicle without needing the help of any other accessories. For example, if a vehicle was stuck and unable to self-navigate out of a situation, or if emergency crews needed to
move it manually
. Indeed, Tesla's official manual for first responders notes that "In situations where Cybercab is operable, Cybercab can be manually moved with onboard vehicle controls." According to the guide, first responders can call up Tesla's support team and flash their badge to a Cybercab's cameras to gain access.
But if these random users was able to access the controls, what safeguards are in place to keep others from being able to pilot the car if they discover the same menu?

title: Tesla May Offer You A Robotaxi Instead Of A Service Loaner
content:
Forget rental cars or Uber credits, Tesla wants to send you home in a robotaxi.
Photo by:
11:29am ET
New code in the latest Tesla app suggests that the automaker is getting ready to update the way it provides service loaners to some drivers.
Hidden in the app are references to robotaxi rides being offered to customers instead of dedicated service loaners.
This could not save Tesla money, but also provide a smarter way for customers to drop off and pick up their cars for service.
Tesla's history with service loaners has been a bit rocky. Many dealerships today use it as an opportunity to provide better customer service or even up-sell new models. I mean, what better way to get a customer to upgrade to a refreshed car or more expensive model than put them in the drivers seat of a new car?
Over time, Tesla eventually augmented its loaner fleet with Uber credits, or just sent customers on their way while their car is was in the shop. But now, the automaker has a better idea:
robotaxis
Photo by: Tesla
Buried in Tesla latest app, according to
Not A Tesla App
, is code that suggests it's getting ready to offer robotaxi loaners to customers who bring their vehicles in for service.
It's kind of a smart idea, honestly. Rather than tie up an entire car for a whole day, just
send a robotaxi to the customer
for just the time that they need it. Tesla already knows where the customer is, where their car is, how long the appointment should take, and when the customer needs transportation to-and-from the service center.
When the robotaxi isn't in use by the customer, it could potentially
service other paid riders
in the meantime to rake in revenue rather than sit idle. It also means that Tesla doesn't have to fork over cash to Uber or appease a customer with service credits because they can't provide a car.
And—perhaps most important to Tesla—it's a way to flex its autonomous driving prowess.
Not A Tesla App
reports that there are a few other references tucked away in the code that suggest Tesla could offer even more methods of transportation for loaners:
sv_transport_robotaxi (Robotaxi)
sv_transport_paid_loaner (Paid Loaner)
sv_transport_e_bike (E-Bike)
sv_transport_bolt (Bolt)
This shows that Tesla could be mulling around the idea of offering other methods of loaners, like an
or whatever a
might be (we really doubt it means a
Chevy Bolt

Of course, this is all long-term thinking that might never see the light of day. And if it does, the rollout certainly won't be instantaneous.
Tesla's robotaxis aren't approved for autonomous use everywhere just yet. In some markets, AVs still require safety drivers and many others aren't proven out to handle a driverless fleet at all. But in large metropolitan areas where robotaxis are king (think Austin, the Bay Area, and other AV hot spots across the U.S.), it feels like a shoo-in.

title: Tesla Will Make Supercharger Stations Just For Robotaxis
content:
Public Superchargers are being used at night right now, where operators manually plug in the electric cabs.
Photo by:
InsideEVs
8:44am ET
Tesla wants to build special Supercharger stations for its Robotaxi fleet.
The driverless EVs are being plugged in manually “for now,” said Tesla’s head of charging for North America.
Further down the road, we might see automatic stations where cars no longer need people to plug them in.
Tesla’s Supercharger network of EV fast chargers, which is widely regarded as the largest and most reliable in the United States, is getting a subtle makeover to make room for the company’s self-driving taxi efforts.
Max de Zegher, who runs Tesla’s North American Charging unit, said that the company is building dedicated stations that will serve its growing fleet of Robotaxis. For now, the driverless cabs are using public Supercharger stations, where they’re usually topped up at night by a human operator.
“They’re plugged in manually, but that’s just for now,” said Max de Zegher, hinting that future Robotaxi Superchargers will do without human operators who plug in the cars. That said, he didn’t elaborate on how the robotaxis will be automatically set up for charging, and Tesla hasn’t exactly followed through with its decade-old idea of a robotic charging arm.
When it comes to the new
Cybercab
, the key might be wireless charging. Back in 2024, when the gold-colored two-door EV was unveiled, Tesla said it would only support
wireless charging
, which makes a lot of sense for a world where nobody drives anymore, and the cars can position themselves over inductive charging pads while they wait for customers to hail a cab.
video released in October 2024
, a Cybercab is shown wirelessly charging at up to 25 kilowatts, which is anything but fast by today’s standards. However, according to documents filed with the Environmental Protection Agency, the steering-wheel-less EV’s battery capacity is just 48 kilowatt-hours, which means a two-hour charging session should be enough for a full charge–at least in theory.
Gallery: Tesla Cybercab Robotaxi
The upcoming Robotaxi-specific Superchargers will be built in areas where demand is high, the land is cheap, and capital expenditures can be kept in check. To successfully scale its Robotaxi business, cabs need to be able to do back-to-back charging sessions, maximizing the sites’ utilization rates.
Until that happens, the driverless Model Ys and Cybercabs will keep using public Superchargers, none of which offer wireless pads. Max de Zegher said cars with passengers have priority when charging, and that the same Trip Planner fundamentals that power the active navigation systems on all Teslas are being used to dispatch robotaxis to chargers.

title: The Slate Truck’s Trailer Hitch Installation Is As Simple As It Gets
content:
The Slate Truck’s Trailer Hitch Installation Is As Simple As It Gets
The startup says that anyone can install the $99.99 receiver in as little as 30 minutes with simple tools.
- Slate’s upcoming electric pickup has a huge accessories list, and a trailer kit is on that list.
- The startup gave an extremely short glimpse into the installation process of the hitch.
- Priced at $99.99, the 2-inch receiver can be installed with a couple of tools in as little as half an hour.
The Slate electric pickup truck is almost here, and that’s a big deal, because when the first units reach customers, it will officially become America’s cheapest new EV. But the low, $26,400 starting price comes with some strings attached.
Namely, the entry-level truck is as bare-bones as they get, with anything and everything available as add-on optional extras. What’s more, the vehicle was designed as “the most DIY-able vehicle ever,” with owners expected to fix common problems and install new kit.
That includes the optional trailer hitch, which is now part of what seems like an endless list of accessories. Priced at $99.99, the kit has a standard two-inch receiver and needs just four bolts to attach to the rear of the pickup, as shown (for a very brief moment) in a new promotional video.
The same video shows some wires dangling from the underside, but the startup hasn’t made up its mind about that yet. A year ago, a reservation holder asked Slate about the trailer wiring, and the company replied that a four-pin cable will be available as an add-on accessory. However, the listing for the hitch receiver kit doesn’t say anything about wiring, and there’s no separate entry for a trailer wiring harness on the website.
This could mean that all Slate pickups come from the factory with a hidden wiring harness for trailers. It could also mean that a separate kit will eventually make an appearance in the online accessories shop.
The startup says that installing the rear hitch receiver can take anywhere from 30 minutes to two hours, and that basic tools will do the job just fine. Judging from the video, a pair of wrenches is just about all you need.
With the receiver secured, the Slate truck can accommodate anything from a standard trailer hitch to a variety of bike racks and other accessories–all of which need to be purchased separately. As far as towing goes, Slate says its two-door truck can haul up to 2,000 pounds, which is adequate for a vehicle that’s nearly nine inches shorter than a Hyundai Ioniq 5.
With an 181-horsepower (135-kilowatt) rear electric motor and a 65-kilowatt-hour lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery pack, the Slate truck can drive up to 205 miles on a full charge. Mind you, that’s without towing, which will undoubtedly lower the range figure. Recharging the LFP battery is done through a NACS port at the rear left of the pickup, with Slate quoting 30 minutes for a 20-to-80% session at a DC fast charger.

title: Toyota Recalls 10,000 C-HR EVs That May Lose Power While Driving
content:
One of Toyota's newest EVs launched in the U.S. has a software issue, and a dealership visit is the only way to fix it.
Photo by:
Suvrat Kothari
3:40am ET
Toyota is recalling one of its newest EVs in America.
The electric drive systems of certain C-HR crossovers sold here could shut down while driving.
It’s a software issue, but in the age of smartphone-like cars, owners need to visit their dealer to fix the problem.
is recalling approximately 10,000 C-HR electric crossovers sold in North America over a potentially dangerous safety issue. The affected vehicles, all 2026 models, could cut power while driving, which increases the risk of a crash.
According to the automaker
, this is caused by a software issue with the Battery Electric Vehicle Electronic Control Unit, which can overcharge the traction battery under regenerative braking when the state of charge is already high. As a reminder, under regenerative braking, the electric motor works as a generator, slowing down the car and sending energy back to the high-voltage battery.
Gallery: 2026 Toyota C-HR
If the traction battery is already full, it will not accept additional energy, and its safety guardrails will shut down the system to prevent overcharging. That’s what’s happening with the affected 2026 Toyota C-HRs recalled in America right now.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has not published relevant documents regarding this recall yet, but the automaker said that updating the faulty control unit’s software fixes the problem. A visit to the dealer is needed, though, which is still hard to grasp in 2026, when over-the-air software updates should be the norm in new cars.
And the 2026 C-HR is a new electric car–it just can’t get software updates wirelessly. Despite debuting at the same time as the new RAV4, which is Toyota’s bread and butter, the C-HR gets an older version of the company’s infotainment system instead of the latest Arene setup.
As we discovered
during our time with the C-HR
, Toyota’s smallest EV gets a slow-to-boot 14-inch infotainment touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity—but that’s about it in terms of modern tech.
Still, this didn’t seem to stop a lot of people from buying one. In the first half of the year,
Toyota’s EV sales in the U.S. exploded by 136%
compared to the same period in 2025, and much of that was down to the launch of the C-HR,

title: Watch Tesla's Wild 'Unboxed' Manufacturing For The Cybercab In Action
content:
Watch Tesla's Wild 'Unboxed' Manufacturing For The Cybercab In Action
- Tesla’s smallest new EV is being assembled using a new technique.
- The company released a video showcasing its “Unboxed” assembly process.
- Similar to Ford’s Universal EV Production System, Tesla’s approach assembles the car in individual modules, which are put together at the end.
For over a century, cars have been built roughly the same way. Thousands of individual parts are put together on a conveyor belt that slowly runs through the factory, and as it moves along, the car takes shape on it.
It’s how the Ford Model T was built over a century ago, but things are starting to change. Now, car companies are trying to streamline the assembly process to cut costs and boost output while also slimming down the size of their factories.
Tesla is one of those companies, and its so-called "Unboxed" technique is now being used to build the new two-door Cybercab. The American technology giant published a video on the official Robotaxi account on X yesterday, offering a first glimpse into how it makes the steering-wheel-less EV.
Instead of bolting separate pieces onto the main chassis, the Cybercab is made from individual modules that are assembled on parallel lines. The video shows the battery box, front section, and rear section being built at the same time. Then, they’re framed together at the end of the line, where the side sections, roof, and doors are added.
Tesla says this technique reduces the assembly line by half, presumably compared to a traditional car factory, which unlocks a higher production capacity in the same footprint. The company bills its new building strategy as “the first real revolution in automotive manufacturing in over a century,” but it’s worth noting that Ford, which invented the modern car production line back in the 1900s, is also gearing up to disrupt the assembly game.
Its Universal EV Production System, which will be used to make the upcoming Fathom electric pickup truck, divides the assembly process into three individual lines. The front, middle, and rear of the vehicle are built on parallel lines, and they’re joined together at the end.
Tesla Cybercab Unboxed Production Line
Mind you, Tesla claims to be mass-producing the Cybercab right now, whereas the first customer Ford Fathom pickups will start rolling off the line next year.
A key part of making this type of production viable is the extensive use of large metal parts that are cast by huge presses. It eliminates the need for hundreds of individual parts that need to be formed and joined together, which makes the whole process faster and cheaper.

title: Batteries just broke another record in the US
content:
Batteries just broke another record in the US
Huge grid-scale batteries are thriving, but smaller residential systems have lagged.
Battery installations hit a new record in the US in the second quarter of 2026. In total, 20.2 gigawatt-hours of new capacity came online, according to a new report. That’s enough to supply the daily electricity needs of about 700,000 homes.
The surge is putting the country on a trajectory to see 71 gigawatt-hours of batteries installed in 2026, a 20% increase over last year. This growth is being driven by a combination of cheaper batteries and an urgent need for more energy storage capacity as renewables such as solar and onshore wind power are added to the grid.
Massive, utility-scale systems are leading the way; they’re responsible for most of the record-setting quarter. Seven new gigascale battery installations (those with a capacity of over one gigawatt-hour) came online during the three-month stretch, according to the report, published by Benchmark Mineral Intelligence and the Solar Energy Industries Association.
“It really came down to a handful of big projects,” says Shan Tomouk, energy storage and energy lead for Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
But there was also growth in the category of so-called behind-the-meter batteries, which include both residential and industrial battery storage systems. These projects, generally smaller than utility-scale installations, are typically owned and operated by homeowners or businesses rather than utilities or power providers.
In the behind-the-meter category, data centers led the way, making up about three-quarters of new batteries in the commercial sector. But residential batteries saw a sharp slowdown. These systems are often installed in homes to store power from solar panels or serve as a backup source in case of a blackout. Home installations are projected to drop by 16% in 2026 compared with last year, according to the report.
That drop happened largely because a tax credit that helped subsidize home battery systems ended in 2025, Tomouk says. Home installations should recover by the end of the decade, he adds. And tax credits for nonresidential batteries have largely survived.
Overall, batteries are a bright spot in energy right now. “This is one of the strong sectors in the US,” says Isshu Kikuma, an energy storage analyst at BloombergNEF, an energy consultancy.
As the battery market continues to grow, one major trend to keep an eye on is a move toward US-made technology. Today, nearly all the systems coming online use cells made in China, though some are put together into complete energy storage systems in the US.
Tariffs were already pushing the US energy storage industry toward domestic production. And beginning this year, energy storage tax credits required projects to limit their reliance on batteries imported from China. There’s a lot of manufacturing capacity set to come online in the US, though these factories probably won’t be able to meet demand until at least 2030 or so, Tomouk says, so prices could tick up.

Danijar Hafner’s office in San Francisco’s SoMa district sits mostly empty, but what it lacks in decor, it makes up for in robots. Humanoids of various shapes and sizes hang like marionettes from racks that run down the center of the wide-open space.
Hafner won’t say too much about his new venture just yet, but describes it as a continuation of his longtime work to enable AI to navigate environments it has not encountered in training.
Over the years, the 31-year-old has honed his approach by pitting agents trained within his world models against popular video games. More recently, he’s begun migrating his agents out of the virtual world and into physical reality.
Learn more about Hafner’s work teaching AI about our world.
—Mat Honan
Danijar Hafner is one of the artificial intelligence honorees on our 35 Innovators Under 35 list for 2026. Meet the rest of them here, or explore the full list across the biotechnology, AI, computing and robotics, and climate and energy categories.
MIT Technology Review Narrated: data from drones in Ukraine is fueling a new Wild West marketplace
Battlefields in Ukraine are littered with the remnants of drones. But behind all that wreckage, there’s a new gold mine for the defense sector: the data those drones generate.
Ukraine has begun making millions of data points gathered during tens of thousands of drone flights available to military contractors and commercial companies. It’s a quick way to attract funding and partnerships, but it turns the front line into a model training site, using the chaos of war to create conditions that AI companies struggle to reproduce.
As this new industry takes shape, we need a regulatory system that ensures battlefield data isn’t treated like ordinary commercial material.

title: Understanding the thermal ceiling in portable power
content:
Understanding the thermal ceiling in portable power
Wireless charging performance is limited less by power delivery than by the physics of heat, and solving it requires rethinking the hardware.
Provided byAnker
Plug a phone into a modern charger and the first 10 minutes are impressive. The next 20 are not.
This is not a defect. It’s the connected device protecting itself. As temperature rises during charging, a smartphone's battery management system reduces the current it will accept, because heat accelerates the chemical degradation that permanently reduces battery capacity. The charger may be capable of delivering more, but the device simply stops taking it.
For anyone building products in the portable power category, this creates an uncomfortable gap between specification and experience. A device rated at 25 watts is accurate in the sense that it can deliver 25 watts. Whether it delivers 25 watts for the duration of a charge is a different question, and one the specification does not answer.
The specification gap
The gap matters commercially because it is invisible at the point of purchase and obvious in use.
Consumers compare wattage figures on packaging. They don’t compare thermal curves, because thermal curves are not published publicly. The result is a category where products differentiate on a number that describes peak output rather than sustained output, and where the actual user experience of two products with identical specifications can diverge substantially.
This is particularly acute in magnetic wireless charging. Inductive power transfer generates heat at both the transmitting and receiving coils, and the magnetic attachment that makes these products convenient also places the heat source in direct contact with the device it is charging. Convenience and thermal performance are working against each other by design.
The industry's response for the past several years has been materials science. Graphite sheets, thermal interface materials, conductive housings, and heat-spreading layers have all improved how efficiently accumulated heat moves away from the source. Each generation has been incrementally better than the last.
But passive dissipation has a structural limitation: it can only move heat that has already been generated, and only as fast as the surrounding air will accept it. In a sealed, pocket-sized enclosure, that ceiling arrives quickly. Improving the materials slows the rate of temperature rise. It does not prevent the temperature rise.
Moving from dissipation to removal
The alternative is active thermal management, which is standard in stationary electronics and largely absent from portable ones for reasons that are easy to understand. Fans add volume, weight, moving parts, and noise. In a product category defined by portability, each of those is a meaningful cost.
At Anker, which manufactures charging and power products, engineering teams spent the past several development cycles working on whether that tradeoff could be made acceptable rather than eliminated. The approach involves several interacting systems: a micro centrifugal fan, dual airflow channels routed to avoid interference with the magnetic array, a three-layer graphene heat-spreading layer, and a control algorithm that modulates fan speed based on real-time temperature and battery state rather than running at a fixed rate. The result is that the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro has become the world's fastest and coolest wireless power bank.
In internal testing, at 77 °F (25 °C) ambient, the back of the power bank stays below 96.8 °F (36 °C) throughout wireless charging, 21.6 °F (12 °C) below the international standard limit of 118.4 °F (48 °C), for a comfortable grip. Comparable magnetic power banks in the same testing typically reached 113 °F (45 °C) or higher within 20 minutes. The functional consequence is that the connected device does not reach the threshold at which it begins reducing charge acceptance, so 25 watts of Qi2.2 magnetic wireless charging is delivered as a working rate rather than an opening rate. In practice, an iPhone 17 Pro reaches 50% charge in 25 minutes. The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro’s premium performance in both charging speed and thermal management is certified by SGS, an independent testing and certification company.
The same principle applies in reverse. Recharging a power bank generates heat too, which is why devices in this category are often slow to recharge, leaving users with an empty accessory at the moment they need it. Active cooling during input allows the unit to accept 45 watts and reach 80% in 52 minutes.
What this suggests about the category
There is a broader pattern here worth naming, because it is not unique to charging.
When a category improves along a single axis for long enough, the constraint usually migrates somewhere else. Charging spent a decade optimizing power delivery. Power delivery is now, for most practical purposes, solved: the electronics can supply more energy than the receiving device is willing to accept. The binding constraint moved to thermal management, and the industry continued optimizing the axis it had always optimized, because that is the axis the specifications describe.
Recognizing when a constraint has moved is difficult precisely because the old metric keeps improving. Wattage figures have continued to climb. Products have continued to get faster on paper. The measurement stayed valid while quietly ceasing to describe the thing users experience.
For product organizations, the practical question is whether their specifications still measure the constraint or merely measure the capability. The two align until the constraint shifts and specifications rarely shift with it.
The transparency problem
A second implication follows from the first. If sustained performance differs meaningfully from peak performance, and if only peak performance is disclosed, then buyers cannot evaluate the products in front of them.
This is one reason Anker is adding displays on charging products. The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro shows real-time power, temperature, battery level, and estimated time remaining. Some of that is user convenience. But some of it is a Anker stating a deliberate position—this category deserves to have the complete and accurate data made transparent to all.
Anker expects independent reviewers to test these claims and considers our internal numbers to be the correct outcome. The gap between specification and experience closes faster when the experience is measurable. The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro will be available in the U.S. on September 17, 2026.

title: 中科院电工研究所：低温锂离子电容器电解液研究获进展 - NE时代
content:
中科院电工研究所：低温锂离子电容器电解液研究获进展
锂离子电容器在低温高功率储能场景中具有重要应用潜力。低温下，传统碳酸酯基电解液中的锂离子溶剂化效应强，脱溶剂化效应慢，导致电极界面电荷转移动力学滞后、储能反应匹配性变差，大幅度制约器件的能量输出和倍率性能。因此，亟需从电解液分子结构调控出发，削弱溶剂屏蔽作用，提升锂离子电容器低温动力学性能。
近日，电工研究所研究员马衍伟团队提出“溶剂化解蔽电解液”设计策略。团队采用兼具中等极性、低熔点和适度配位能力的γ－戊内酯（GVL）为主体溶剂，二氟草酸硼酸锂（LiDFOB）为功能锂盐，并引入弱配位乙酸乙酯（EA）作为溶剂化调节组分，削弱溶剂对锂离子的包裹和屏蔽作用，促进阴离子参与构建局部溶剂化结构，形成弱束缚、阴离子参与的溶剂化解蔽环境。该设计有效降低了低温条件下脱溶剂化势垒与界面电荷转移阻力，提升了电极－电解液界面稳定性。
溶剂化解蔽电解液促进低温锂离子电容器界面电荷转移示意图
研究表明，采用该溶剂化解蔽电解液制备的全碳锂离子电容器在－40　℃条件下仍保持优异的能量输出性能，基于电极材料质量的能量密度达到106.8　Wh／kg，为传统碳酸酯基电解液的8.9倍。该研究突破了低温锂离子电容器因强溶剂化屏蔽引发的界面反应动力学迟缓的瓶颈，为开发低温、高能量、高稳定性锂离子电容器提供了新方案。
该研究成果发表于《先进功能材料》（Advanced　Functional　Materials），相关工作得到国家自然科学基金、高密度电磁动力与系统全国重点实验室开放课题等项目的资助支持。

亿纬锂能何巍博士：大圆柱电池正加速驶入全场景时代
9 月 4 日，2026 世界动力电池大会“全球先进电池前瞻技术专题会议”在四川宜宾举行。作为大会唯一的技术专题，本次会议汇聚行业权威专家，共话先进电池技术的未来方向。亿纬锂能副总裁、乘用车电池产品线总裁何巍博士受邀出席，并发表《大圆柱电池技术创新与全场景应用进展》主题演讲，系统分享了大圆柱电池的独特价值与广阔前景。
多元技术共存，大圆柱展现独特生命力
“技术进步与场景需求始终处于动态匹配之中，多元路线将持续共存。”何巍博士开宗明义。
他提出，技术路线的选择，除了材料体系的演进，封装形式与整车工程的深度融合同样深刻塑造着市场格局。而大圆柱电池的生命力，恰恰在于“One for All”——一颗电芯，覆盖无限场景。
这一理念的根基，源于三大本征优势：标准化，让一颗电池覆盖从 A 级到全尺寸的多元车型，也为极致制造提供稳定基础；零膨胀，使电芯全生命周期尺寸始终如一，为整车长期可靠性提供底层保障；高强度，钢壳强度达铝壳 6 倍，配合气电分离设计，为高比能材料应用筑牢安全载体。
全场景验证，原位升级彰显平台价值
基于三大本征优势，大圆柱电池在高能量、高功率、快充及长循环方向持续迭代，并在规模化应用中取得扎实进展：260Wh/kg 产品已装车超 5 万台；280Wh/kg 产品装车近 7 万台；300Wh/kg 产品今年实现整车量产；320Wh/kg 产品率先落地低空经济。
“同一结构、同一产线，仅切换化学体系，即可实现电量从 80 度到 114 度的灵活覆盖。”何巍博士以量产实践为例，阐释了“原位升级”带来的平台价值——从入门到高配，车企无需改动整车结构即可完成性能迭代，验证周期与研发成本大幅降低。
而支撑这一能力的，是亿纬锂能“3 + 2”化学体系的系统性布局与日产能 500 万颗的规模化制造根基。目前，大圆柱电池已配套宝马、红旗等多款车型，装车应用稳步推进。
不止于车，大圆柱赋能全场景智慧生活
大圆柱的想象空间，远不止于乘用车。依托圆柱电池在高功率领域的技术积累，亿纬锂能已将大圆柱拓展至 HEV、12V/48V 等场景，并向 100C 超高倍率持续突破——今年顶级赛车赛事搭载亿纬锂能电池并取得优异成绩。何巍博士说：“曾经我们认为 100C 是不可能的，但现在我们把它做成了。”
从两轮出行到四轮驾乘，从地面交通到低空经济，从赛道竞速到全场景出行。大圆柱正以“一颗电芯，无限应用”的理念打破场景边界，赋能智慧未来。深耕圆柱电池二十余年，亿纬锂能正将技术积淀转化为可量产、可交付、可拓展的全场景能力，以极致创新驱动产业迈向更广阔的未来。

title: 全面迈向48V车载新架构！思瑞浦首发全国产化80V CAN SIC收发器TPT1662xQ - NE时代
content:
全面迈向48V车载新架构！思瑞浦首发全国产化80V CAN SIC收发器TPT1662xQ
48V车载系统正加速取代传统12V架构，凭借功率承载能力提升4倍、线束重量降低60%的显著优势，成为燃油车向纯电动过渡的关键技术路径。
然而，48V系统带来的不仅是性能提升，更是对车载电子元件耐压能力的严峻考验。ISO 21780:2020标准的发布，为48V车载电气系统建立了统一的技术规范。该标准明确了供电电压范围最高达60V，过压实验更要求70V/40ms的短时过压。这意味着，48V车载网络中的CAN总线节点，必须具备远超传统12V系统的耐压能力。
48V电源系统重构汽车未来
针对48V车载应用的严苛需求，3PEAK推出TPT1662VQ与TPT1662Q系列CAN FD SIC收发器。TPT1662xQ系列完全符合ISO 11898-2:2024、CiA601-4以及SAE J2284-1至J2284-5高速CAN物理层标准，支持经典CAN和优化CAN FD SIC网络，数据传输速率最高可达8Mbps。
产品核心优势对比：
领先业界的±80V耐压，从容应对最恶劣工况
ISO 21780是针对48V车载系统电源电压标准。标准要求48V系统芯片的供电耐压至少60V，并且能抗住瞬态高压可到70V/40ms。因此对CAN芯片总线耐压要求较高，TPT1662芯片总线故障保护电压高达±80V，完美覆盖ISO 21780标准所定义的全部过压场景——无论是60V长期过压还是70V短时浪涌，
ISO 21780 48V供电电压标准
48V系统CAN短路工况
总线有CMC条件下总线短路60V，
芯片端振荡可达80V
TPT1662xQ针对性优化总线耐压设计，具备±80V超宽总线耐压范围，远超行业常规水平，无论瞬态耐压还是长时间耐压表现均大于±80V。
总线高压脉冲和1min短路耐压测试均＞80V芯片无损伤，故障撤销可恢复通信
高共模输入电压：48V车载CAN通信的“隐形守护者”
ISO 25769是针对12V/24V/48V车载电气系统的电气要求和试验方法，明确将“地丢失”纳入考核，48V系统设计中，“地丢失”导致的共模电压骤升是必须通过的硬性考核项。当ECU接地回路断开时，参考地会被拉至48V电池电位，总线共模电压实测可达70V以上的高压脉冲。常规CAN收发器共模范围仅±12~±30V，接收器立即饱和失效，无法满足ISO 25769测试要求，节点通信中断甚至拖垮整条总线。
TPT1662xQ凭借±60V超宽共模能力，在面对60V共模冲击下接收器仍能精准识别差分电平，确保RXD输出无误。确保通信不中断——是满足ISO 25769标准、保障48V系统极端故障下通信可靠性的关键保障。
Lost of Ground下共模电压路径
地丢失工况下靠近芯片端总线共模电压最大飙升至70V
模拟芯片在不同共模电压下5Mbps通信表现，TPT1662xQ凭借极高抗干扰表现，在＞±60V共模干扰接收器都能保持稳定工作，有效抑制共模噪声，确保仅有差分信号被正确放大。这使得TPT1662xQ在48V高噪声环境中依然能实现零误码的高可靠通信。
TPT1662xQ共模±80V 无错误帧
竞品共模±20-30V 有错误帧
卓越EMC性能，保障通信稳定
在48V车载系统中，CAN收发器除了承受高压冲击与共模干扰外，还需在复杂网络环境和强电磁干扰中可靠通信、协同工作。TPT1662xQ系列在IOPT互操作测试与EMC电磁兼容测试中的出色表现，为系统提供了额外一重保障。
无需共模电感即可通过全部车规EMC测试：针对总线信号质量与EMC性能进行特殊优化，省去外部共模电感，降低BOM成本与PCB面积；
同时TPT1662xQ凭借卓越的BCI（大电流注入）抗干扰能力，有效抵御电磁干扰，保障CAN总线通信稳定，满足车载电磁兼容性（EMC）标准要求。
不止硬核性能，更懂客户需求
TPT1662xQ完全兼容ISO 11898-2:2024、CiA601-4以及SAE J2284-1至J2284-5高速CAN物理层标准等行业标准，可直接替换传统CAN收发器，无需修改系统软件，大幅降低客户的升级成本和研发周期，性能更是行业领先，实现从晶圆制造、芯片设计到封装测试的全流程国产化，为国内车企提供48V自主可控方案。
未来，我们将持续深耕车载半导体领域，以技术创新驱动产品升级，推出更多具备核心竞争力的48V车载器件，助力汽车电子化、智能化产业高质量发展！

双向奔赴 产业协同 | 华域电动与巨力自动化开启战略合作新篇章
签约仪式视频预览
2026 年 8 月 28 日，华域汽车电动系统有限公司与巨力自动化设备（浙江）股份有限公司的战略合作签约仪式在巨力自动化公司隆重举行。华域电动总经理顾湧与巨力自动化董事长章日平携双方核心管理团队共同出席，依托多年项目合作基础，正式达成战略合作伙伴关系。
巨力自动化董事长章日平回顾了双方的合作渊源：早在 2018 年，巨力自动化有幸为华域电动交付了国内首条扁线驱动电机定子自动化产线。此后数年间，双方联合攻坚克难，开启了多项电驱动项目的深度合作。
章日平表示，历经多年持续技术攻关，巨力自动化实现多项核心工艺迭代突破，掌握 0.8 秒高速扁线成型技术，同时也是国内首家实现扁线电机定子整线装备出口欧洲的国产装备企业。
章日平指出，互信是双方合作的根基。巨力自动化始终秉持 “努力让客户成功” 的服务理念，高度重视与华域电动建立的深厚合作情谊，期待以本次战略签约为全新起点，迈向更高层次的合作共赢。
华域电动总经理顾湧高度肯定巨力自动化的技术实力与行业成果，对过往项目落地过程中高效的交付能力、完备的技术配套服务予以认可。
顾湧强调，双方不要把战略合作签约作为一种形式过场，而是需要开展务实的工作：要搭建框架抓落实，做好产业链协同；要关注所有合作项目进程，要有结论；要半年开展一次交流，定期回顾和审视，形成合力和聚力。
顾湧希望，双方能充分释放产业与技术优势，合力攻克行业关键技术壁垒，实现优势互补、互利共生。
在双方团队的共同见证下，签约代表上台签署战略合作协议。
仪式结束后，华域电动来访团队在巨力自动化管理层陪同下，深入生产制造车间开展实地参观。
一行人实地观摩巨力新一代 0.8 秒节拍线成型设备，近距离查看设备运行工况，深度了解这套行业标杆级高速扁线成型装备的核心技术优势与工艺实力。
随后，代表团一行到访巨力自动化研究院，实地参观企业前沿技术研发平台。现场观摩具身智能机器人、X-pin自动化设备等多项研发成果，详细了解巨力自动化在新兴产业领域的技术路线、研发进展及产业化布局，并就下一代电驱动技术、新型装备的技术难点与商业化前景开展深入交流。
面向未来，华域电动和巨力自动化将打通技术、研发、制造全链条协同通路，深耕新一代电驱动技术、智能制造装备与新兴领域自动化解决方案。依托双方资源禀赋互补优势，开展全维度深度协同，抢抓产业变革机遇，合力赋能先进电驱动系统与高端智能制造产业实现高质量发展。

title: 小马智行多哈Robotaxi商业运营再进一步，全无人驾驶体验首次开放 - NE时代
content:
小马智行多哈Robotaxi商业运营再进一步，全无人驾驶体验首次开放
9月7日至9日，由卡塔尔交通部主办的第二届自动驾驶电动出行论坛（AEMOB）在多哈国家会议中心举办。在这场中东智能出行领域的重磅盛会上，小马智行与卡塔尔国家运输公司Mowasalat共同发布Robotaxi商业化运营的阶段性成果，同步推出多哈首个全无人驾驶Robotaxi体验项目。该项目成为本届论坛最受关注的技术落地标杆案例。
从测试到商业化运营：
多哈模式成为全球化可复制样本
自2025年8月启动
多哈公开道路测试
以来，小马智行与战略合作伙伴卡塔尔国家运输公司Mowasalat仅用四个月即完成从道路测试到商业运营的跨越。
用户目前可通过Mowasalat旗下Karwa应用呼叫Robotaxi服务，覆盖多哈老城区、CBD核心商圈、旅游地标及哈马德国际机场接驳线路，串联起日常通勤、商务出行、旅游观光等高频场景，这成为小马智行海外首个实现规模化商业落地的自动驾驶项目。
卡塔尔交通部在今年7月的官方通报中明确指出，该项目乘客满意度与安全表现均超出预期，技术与运营体系已具备大规模推广条件，下一阶段将推动全无人驾驶Robotaxi在多哈的商业运营。这一官方认可，标志着小马智行的自动驾驶技术与本地化运营能力，已获得全球高潜力市场的权威认可。
卡塔尔交通部高度认可多哈Robotaxi商业化运营
全无人体验首秀：
第七代平台支撑全球规模化部署
本届论坛期间开放的全无人驾驶试乘，是多哈城市交通史上首次真正意义上的无安全员自动驾驶体验。本次试乘采用的第七代Robotaxi是小马智行面向全球市场打造的标杆车型，通过成本结构与运营效率的双重优化，为全球范围的大规模商业化部署奠定了核心基础。
卡塔尔当地青年企业家穆罕默德·埃尔萨耶格体验后感到兴奋：“这是在多哈第一次真正的全无人驾驶汽车体验，太厉害了，自动驾驶比人开车安全多了。”
小马智行创始人兼CEO彭军表示：
“多哈的实践，是中国自动驾驶技术走向全球的关键一步。我们将持续深化与Mowasalat的合作，不仅将助力卡塔尔打造更智能、更可持续的交通体系、树立智能出行新标杆，更将为全球城市交通升级提供可落地、可复制的解决方案。”
Mowasalat运营着卡塔尔规模最大的出租车和巴士、商务用车等服务网络，并承担起国家交通战略的重要任务。双方合作项目在卡塔尔交通部的监管下开展，通过推动自动驾驶技术安全融入公共交通系统，助力实现“卡塔尔国家愿景2030”的可持续交通目标。
全球化战略核心支点：
共建车队模式打开全球增长空间
多哈项目的落地，是小马智行“共建车队”全球化战略的标志性成果——通过将自研自动驾驶核心技术与全球合作伙伴的本地运营资源、用户渠道、车队网络深度整合，实现了自动驾驶技术在海外市场的快速商业化。“中国+海外”共同构成拉动业务增长的战略引擎，通过多元市场布局释放更大增长潜力。
截至目前，小马智行全球化布局已覆盖中东、亚洲、欧洲9个国家，在克罗地亚、新加坡、卡塔尔等地均已实现公开载客运营，并在近期获得包括Uber在内的全球头部出行平台合作订单，将在海外部署超4000辆Robotaxi。
依托中国复杂交通场景打磨的成熟技术体系、全流程运营经验，叠加第七代Robotaxi平台的成本优势，小马智行正持续为全球合作伙伴构建可盈利的自动驾驶商业闭环，成为中国智能驾驶企业出海的核心代表力量。

广汽高域与广州铁投战略合作，共建全国首个“枢纽+低空”空地联运示范项目，探索协同新模式
2026年9月9日，广州——广东高域科技有限公司（以下简称“广汽高域”）与广州铁路投资建设集团有限公司（以下简称“广州铁投”）在广州签署战略合作协议，共同探索建设全国首个“枢纽+低空”空地联运示范项目。围绕未来广州立体交通规划，双方还在广州白云站举办了场景发布活动，并同步开展低空经济科普、高域飞行器展示等配套活动。
作为大湾区低空产业的代表企业，高域此次携手广州铁投，标志着低空出行从单点场景示范迈出交通枢纽网络化布局的关键一步，是双方低空战略合作全面启动的新起点。
一、从试点到运营 “枢纽+低空”加速落地
此次战略合作的核心，是共同推进全国首个“枢纽+低空”空地联运示范项目建设。依托广州铁投的轨道交通枢纽资源与运营优势，发挥高域载人eVTOL（电动垂直起降飞行器）技术研发、全链条解决方案及产业运营能力，双方将从标准体系编制与试点项目建设入手，进一步探索空地联运的实施路径。
双方计划在未来完成首批试点站点的选址论证、可行性评估及建设方案设计，并优先从广州白云站等综合交通枢纽中选取条件成熟的站点，启动首批“枢纽+低空”试点起降场建设。在此基础上，双方将进一步推动试点方案从规划设计走向实际建设。下一阶段，首批试点站点将进入建设及试运营阶段，逐步验证低空交通与轨道交通、综合交通枢纽协同衔接的可行性，为后续拓展更多应用场景积累实践经验。
值得期待的是，随着首批试点项目逐步推进，双方将围绕空地联运的换乘衔接、安全保障及运营服务等关键环节开展验证，持续完善“轨道+低空”融合发展的实施路径，助力构建面向未来的立体化综合交通网络。
二、立足广州 探索低空交通发展新模式
对于高域而言，此次与广州铁投的合作，不仅是一次低空出行场景的拓展，更是双方探索低空交通融入城市综合交通体系的重要实践。未来，双方将以此次合作为起点，持续推动低空起降设施与轨道交通枢纽的融合布局，探索从单点示范走向体系化发展的低空交通新路径。
“枢纽+低空”出行服务的战略布局并不止于单一试点项目。随着合作不断深化，双方将围绕不同交通枢纽的低空适配条件，持续推进技术、场景与运营模式的协同探索，拓展“高铁+城际+地铁+低空”的立体交通场景，推动低空科技从单一场景走向更广阔的城市空间，逐步构建起一套可持续、可复制、可推广的空地联运商业模式。
从广州白云站出发，双方希望将一个个可落地的实践场景沉淀为可复制的城市经验，推动“枢纽+低空”从广州实践走向大湾区应用，并为全国轨道交通企业布局低空经济提供“广州样板”。
从“飞行”走向“出行”，从“低空”融入“城市”，高域正进一步打通轨道与低空的连接，加速推动低空科技走进真实生活，向构建城市立体交通新生态更进一步！
高域科技企业介绍
广东高域科技有限公司（GOVY）是广汽集团孵化的低空出行科技企业，致力于构建一键式、放心的低空智慧出行生态。
目前，高域已形成GOVY AirCab、GOVY AirCar、GOVY AirJet三款产品矩阵，覆盖低空观光、城市短途接驳、城际快速出行等场景。其中，AirCab于2025年6月在香港全球首发，获超2000架意向订单；AirCar于2023年6月全球首飞；AirJet面向200公里级城际出行。
自2024年12月品牌发布以来，高域加速产业化：2025年累计融资5亿元，产品亮相慕尼黑车展、迪拜GITEX、迪拜航展、巴西圣保罗车展、泰国车展及卡塔尔国庆盛典等国际舞台；2026年3月完成AirCab在海心沙城市核心区飞行演示，获AS 9100D认证，牵头三项飞行汽车团体标准；5月黄埔工厂落成、首台AirCab下线；7月携手大湾区气象分中心签署战略合作协议，打造“低空运营示范中心”。
作为"低空出行生态引领者"，高域正以技术创新与场景落地，推动低空出行从概念走向现实。

title: 开疆拓“界”，伯特利EMB接连获得两家著名车企重磅量产项目定点 - NE时代

开疆拓“界”，伯特利EMB接连获得两家著名车企重磅量产项目定点
近期，伯特利EMB接连获得两家著名车企重磅项目定点，销售总额超20亿元。至此，伯特利已累计获得四家车企四个量产项目，应用车型涵盖混动SUV、纯电SUV及纯电轿车等多种平台。凭借深厚的技术积淀与显著的先发量产优势，伯特利将精准把握未来1-2年的战略窗口期，加速推动EMB量产应用，让创新价值真正惠及广大消费者。
随着汽车智能化不断深入，制动系统对响应速度、控制精度和系统协同能力提出了更高要求。相比传统液压制动，EMB采用纯电控架构，通过电信号完成制动控制，响应时间可控制在TTL≤100ms，能够满足高阶智能驾驶对快速响应和精准控制的需求。同时，伯特利EMB支持四轮独立控制，并通过系统冗余设计提升制动安全性；产品还可与整车能量回收系统协同工作，优化机械制动与电制动之间的配合，在提升制动平顺性的同时兼顾能源利用效率。取消了传统制动液管路，为整车布置优化和轻量化提供更多可能。
这些产品能力的背后，是伯特利围绕EMB持续多年的研发投入与技术积累。公司已形成覆盖执行机构、控制器、核心算法及系统集成的全链路自主研发能力。自主研发的高精度夹紧力估算算法，可在减少压力传感器配置的同时优化系统结构，提升系统鲁棒性，并有利于整车布置；Reverse-Guide-Pin设计进一步降低卡钳滑阻，并结合软件算法实现制动系统“零拖滞”表现。在安全方面，伯特利EMB已获得全球首张EMB TÜV NORD最高安全等级ASIL-D认证，为产品面向量产应用提供安全基础。
在项目竞标评审期间，客户将伯特利EMB与多家供应商的产品分别搭载于不同测试车辆，在不预先获知供应商信息的情况下开展体验评价。测试涵盖制动响应、踏板脚感、不同工况下的制动表现，以及机械制动与能量回收之间的协调效果。经过多轮测试，伯特利EMB凭借稳定的制动响应、良好的踏板脚感和顺畅的制动协同表现获得客户一致认可，最终赢得项目定点。
连续获得多个量产项目定点，充分体现了伯特利EMB的产品开发和量产交付能力。围绕EMB，公司采用模块化、平台化和标准化设计思路，将经过研发验证的成熟模块和零部件，沉淀至产品平台，并根据不同客户车型的安装接口、尺寸参数、整车匹配及软件标定需求开展适配开发。在满足差异化需求的同时，减少重复开发，提升项目开发效率和量产交付周期。
当前，汽车底盘正加速从传统机械控制向电子控制演进，制动、转向、悬架等核心系统的协同程度不断提升。伯特利在制动、转向、悬架及智能驾驶领域已积累丰富的研发与量产实践，并具备核心Know-How的自主掌控能力。未来，公司将持续推进EMB及智能底盘相关产品的研发、验证与规模化应用，为客户提供更加安全、高效、可靠的智能底盘系统解决方案。

斯年智驾完成新一轮战略融资，依托产业协同加速重载物理AI落地
2026年9月，全球领先的自动驾驶重卡解决方案提供商斯年智驾（Senior Auto）宣布完成新一轮战略融资 ， 本轮融资由悦达资本投资，融资资金将主要用于世界模型能力升级、自动驾驶系统持续优化及相关场景拓展，加速物理AI在重载场景中的落地应用。
悦达资本为江苏悦达集团旗下核心产业资本平台。作为长期深耕整车制造的产业集团，悦达集团在商用车制造、供应链整合及产业资源协同方面具备深厚积累。 本轮融资，不仅为斯年智驾带来持续的资金支持，也将为公司在主机厂协同、整车平台适配、工程化落地和场景拓展等方面提供更强支撑，推动重载物理AI从技术能力加速走向产业能力。
此前，在C轮融资之际，斯年智驾确立了以世界模型驱动的智能决策能力为核心，构建面向多车型、多场景、多作业链路的系统化平台能力，形成了从算法研发、系统验证到多场景交付与持续优化的完整链路，并进一步推动业务向开放场景拓展。
在此基础上， 本轮融资将进一步强化斯年智驾在车规级工程化、整车协同和规模化交付层面的能力建设。 依托悦达集团在整车制造和供应链体系上的产业积累，斯年智驾将持续推进SWM世界模型与自动驾驶决策、车辆控制系统等关键环节的深度融合，提升产品成熟度、工程效率和综合运营表现。
同时，悦达集团在工厂园区、能源供应、干线物流等场景中也布局了多元业务，在全国多地拥有深厚的产业资源积淀，这也将为斯年智驾开放更多场景的准入权限，加速其从封闭场景向更大范围重载场景中的技术验证、项目落地和复制推广。
而斯年智驾积累的以世界模型为核心的物理AI能力，也能为悦达集团在开放的真实作业场景中验证迭代，双方将共同把“技术可行”转化为“商业可复制”。
从C轮聚焦车规级技术全域落地，到本轮进一步引入产业协同资源，斯年智驾正在技术持续迭代的基础上，加快形成面向更大范围重载场景的规模化落地能力。 随着量产交付、场景运营、数据沉淀与技术迭代不断形成正向循环，斯年智驾有望进一步夯实其在重载物理 AI商业化进程中的领先位置。
