title: How competitive is BESS for data centers, really? - Energy Storage
content: By now the standout advantages of BESS for data center developers are known. Vendors like Energy Vault, Eolian, Fluence, Hithium, ZincFive and more are supplying their systems to data centers while on the other side of the coin AI hyperscalers like Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance , Meta, Google, and Microsoft have been investing in BESS. Speed-to-power and cheaper power per megawatt-hour (in comparison to gas) are the two biggest areas BESS wins at, and these are highlighted in a report by Volta Foundation in which the organization’s AI & Data Center Infrastructure committee examined where, how, and why BESS are attractive and unattractive for data centers. “BESS earns its place alongside firm generation,” said Volta Foundation’s report, adding that flexibility is a battery’s main benefit for data centers and grid operators. Besides the areas where BESS wins, Volta Foundation singled out four areas for improvement (where batteries are competing but not yet winning) and two where it is losing opportunities to other technologies. “BESS wins the jobs that reward speed and daily cycling: peak shaving against demand charges, and bridge power as the battery layer of a gas-or-engine hybrid,” said the report, pointing out that although batteries cannot solve every problem, they are uniquely positioned to solve some of the most urgent issues. In peak shaving and demand-charge management, for example, BESS can discharge through the costly hours. However, its benefit here depends on a region’s rate structure. In areas with no demand charges, its strong economic advantage disappears. BESS provides temporary, or ‘bridge’ power for data center assets while they wait in an interconnection queue – the speed-to-power piece. But standalone batteries rarely carry a bridge alone, and Volta’s report identifies fuel cells as a competitor for bridge power jobs. Meanwhile, BESS competes where software tools and power electronics have caught up – i.e., curtailment flexibility, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) ride-through, grid services, and sub-second power quality. Losing out and problems faced Big batteries remain uncompetitive in the jobs that demand sustained energy, long-duration backup, and continuous prime power. Long-duration backup jobs beyond four hours go to diesel and continuous prime power is still primarily served by gas turbines and fuel cells. Volta Foundation noted that the use case for batteries for data centers could receive a boost as regulators continue to push for flexibility. Similarly, changing power architectures inside the data center and gas turbine supply chain shortages are also pushing operators towards batteries. The next few years will see more data center deployment globally, and Volta Foundation’s AI & Data Center Infrastructure committee is calling for more collaboration between developers, battery and integration companies and grid operators to define a load profile the industry can design for. As the report pointed out, the lack of load visibility is one of the biggest stumbling blocks for power suppliers trying to meet data centers’ demands, and batteries could provide value more effectively with a greater understanding of data centers’ power needs. There is also no clearly defined way to integrate batteries into a data center, and that lack of certainty presents a risk for investors. Problems arising during the deployment stage tend to appear mostly at commissioning and during the first two years of operation. Integration, controls, and dispatch governance are the biggest culprits rather than cell chemistry. As for future developments, Volta’s report said the next two to three years will decide whether batteries are remembered as a bridge the industry crossed or a fixture it built. “If curtailment-based interconnection becomes the norm and duration economics keep improving, then installed BESS also earns a standing operational role in shaping load, shaving peaks, and selling grid services for the life of the facility,” the report stated. “However, if queues clear faster than expected and gas supply loosens, more of it reverts to idle backup,” the authors warned. In any case, however, batteries provide an arbitrage-economics-independent value by serving as a facility’s power management layer. But how much of this value is realized depends on both industry and regulators’ next steps. Hyperscalers such as Google and xAI seem to prefer vertically integrating their storage, and if this pattern continues and the data center operator becomes the biggest buyer for grid-scale batteries, this could have consequences for how systems are specified and financed. The United States will be BESS’s biggest data center market and it is rewriting the rules for how these loads connect. Volta Foundation concluded its report with a series of recommendations addressed to the stakeholders involved. For data center developers and hyperscalers, it recommended that they design hybrid architectures from day one and specify the battery for daily duty so that backup capability arrives as a byproduct. Finally, because speed decides a project’s viability, hyperscalers should rank power options on time-to-power alongside levelized cost. Grid operators and policymakers should standardize curtailment-based interconnection. They should clarify dispatch rates and market participation for batteries serving large loads and standardize large load tariffs to avoid confusion and delays. Lastly, battery and integration companies should increase emphasis up the stack and develop products based on load archetype. For example, some loads call for high-power cells while others call for energy-dense cells. The post How competitive is BESS for data centers, really? appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Scottish government approves two BESS projects totaling 10 GWh in one day - Energy Storage
content: The Scottish government’s Energy Consents Unit has granted planning permission to four BESS projects in a single day, including one 16-hour BESS and one 18-hour BESS. Combined power output for the four projects is 1.4 GW. Two of the projects that secured a development consent order (DCO) on Sept. 7 were previously selected for the UK government’s cap-and-floor program, which will provide revenue support for long-duration energy storage projects. First announced in October 2024, the cap-and-floor scheme is intended to de-risk investment in UK LDES. The first selection round identified 16 projects from a shortlist of 77, including 11 BESS projects, three pumped hydro projects, one compressed air energy storage (CAES) project and a vanadium redox flow battery. LDES cap-and-floor works by providing a revenue floor for projects, with a revenue ceiling above which projects must pay back excess earnings. A similar program for interconnector projects has already proved successful in building out UK capacity. The two newly consented LDES projects are both being developed by Field Energy in the north of Scotland. The 200 MW Fyrish BESS, near Alness in the Scottish Highlands, is listed as a 16.5-hour duration in the LDES cap-and-floor decision released earlier in 2026, while the 400 MW New Deer BESS in Aberdeenshire was announced as an 18.03-hour duration project. LDES projects were not the only large BESS applications approved by the Energy Consents Unit. Scottish government officials also approved Field Energy’s 300 MW Spittal BESS near Caithness, and the 500 MW Abbotshaugh BESS, also near New Deer in Aberdeenshire, developed by Island Green Power. While no capacity energy storage figure was listed for Abbotshaugh BESS, planning documents list 246 battery containers for the project, which will connect to the 400 kV New Deer 2 substation according to Great Britain’s Transmission Entry Capacity (TEC) register. Field Energy’s New Deer 2 substation will also connect at the site. The flurry of BESS approvals on Sept. 7 follows success for the 500 MW Muttonhole Road BESS in Hamilton, South Lanarkshire, which secured planning consent on Aug. 17. The project site is located around 20 km from the 539 MW Whitelee Wind Farm, the largest onshore wind farm in the United Kingdom. Other recent planning consent approvals include the Sept. 4 sign-off of a 50 MW solar project with 40 MW BESS in Kintore, Aberdeenshire. Abbotshaugh BESS Island Green Power chief executive officer Bob Psaradellis, who was celebrating the company winning approval for the 500 MW / 2 GWh Abbotshaugh BESS, thanked the ministers and the Energy Consents Unit (ECU) for the Abbotshaugh project. “Great work by Nick Bowen and our fantastic ecosystem of internal and external teams that drove this project forward.  We are grateful for the support of Scottish ministers and the ECU and for everyone who participated in the process,” said Psaradellis. Bowen, who is the project development manager at Island Green Power, said that the company will continue to work with the local community. “We will continue working closely with the local community and our project partners as we progress towards the next stage,” Bowen said. Construction is expected to take approximately 18-24 months, with a connection target of 2033, though that date may change depending on the approval secured. title: Why Fidra Energy is building the UK’s biggest BESS project - Energy Storage
content: From a trading perspective, Fidra Energy’s under construction Thorpe Marsh BESS project can be thought of as five gas peaker plants rolled into one. The 1.45 GW/2.9 GWh project is split into five 290 MW units with separate offtake contracts: one on a tolling agreement with Octopus, three floor contracts – two with EDF, one with Statkraft – and one uncontracted unit. “Whether you’re trading a gas plant or a battery, you know, in some ways there’s a very similar skill set involved in that,” said Fidra Energy CEO Chris Elder. The battery developer boss told ESS News that the Fidra Energy team does not come from a solar or wind development background, but instead has experience building and operating large flexible assets. This partly explains why Fidra Energy decided one of its first BESS projects should also be the United Kingdom’s largest. Elder himself worked for 16 years at gas plant developer InterGen, including four years as managing director. It was during his time at InterGen that the Fidra CEO first began exploring large-scale battery storage as a possible option for repowering combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) plants. Biggest BESS: Thorpe Marsh Thorpe Marsh is on course to be Great Britain’s biggest battery when commissioned and the project, which can be seen as a way to reduce reliance on gas, owes at least some of its origin to the gas industry. The project was initially developed by EIG-owned subsidiary West Burton Energy, a company created when EIG bought the West Burton B gas plant and battery storage project from EDF in 2021. Elder joined West Burton Energy that year as CEO, re-consenting West Burton C as a 500 MW battery project, acquiring and progressing Thorpe Marsh as a development project. In August 2024, the West Burton gas plant and 50 MW BESS were sold to TotalEnergies with EIG retaining the two development assets – Thorpe Marsh and West Burton C. Fidra Energy was born. Now scheduled for commissioning in 2027, Thorpe Marsh BESS reached financial close in September 2025 by securing GBP 445 million ($606 million), with major backers including the UK government’s National Wealth Fund. Fidra’s pipeline also includes the 500 MW/1 GWh West Burton C BESS, and the 1,025 MW Enderby BESS project – which it acquired for an undisclosed sum from UK developer Innova. Big investors , diverse funding Large BESS assets are clearly the model for Fidra Energy, and Elder said this strategy was driven by a combination of the economies of scale that are accessible to larger BESS projects, and the internal capabilities of the Fidra team. To build projects of this size means sourcing significant financing from institutional investors, and Fidra Energy has managed to bring major state and private sector bacon boardboard. The Edinburgh-based developer is backed by institutional investor EIG as well as the National Wealth Fund. Elder said a combination of the scale of Fidra Energy’s projects and some fortunate timing were key to raising the capital needed, “Number one, we had a differentiated strategy,” Elder explained. “Nobody else was doing anything of the scale of Thorpe Marsh.” The CEO added that discussions with the National Wealth Fund began two or three years before the investment, and were focused largely around debt financing as opposed to equity financing – but then things changed. “At the time we were looking to raise equity, and we were looking to bring in a minority anchor alongside EIG, the National Wealth Fund were really keen to do that for projects that could make a difference to the storage targets in the UK.” Thorpe Marsh was almost a perfect project for the state investment vehicle, according to Elder, given it will make a major contribution to government flexibility targets and is significantly de-risked by having roughly 50% of its offtake contracted. The pipeline Fidra Energy’s large-scale BESS pipeline is growing, and Elder said the developer has two acquisitions in progress that would bring the total to 4 GW to 4.5 GW in power terms. The ambition is to have 5 GW of deployed UK BESS by 2030. West Burton C BESS is the next project in line, consisting of two 250 MW phases, one tolled to Drax and one to be traded by an optimizer – with oversight from the developer. Fidra Energy also retains a long-term option on land for the proposed 1.2 GW Bicker Fen 1&2 project, however the site has only secured a Gate 1 offer in Great Britain’s recently reformed grid connections queue, pushing any prospect of connecting well into the 2030s. Fidra Energy has not been immune to the headaches that UK connections reform has caused developers. Elder described the process as a “necessary pain” for the whole industry. “Were mistakes made along the way? Absolutely. It took too long. Administratively, it wasn’t run particularly well. But I think we’re now past the worst of it. I think we’re making decent progress,” he said. Elder added that Fidra Energy received connection offers for Thorpe Marsh and West Burton, and accepted them almost immediately. Now the developer wants to see delivery of these connection dates as promised, which will be a question for the transmission system owner – National Grid, in the case of Thorpe Marsh and West Burton. “Have we got the right engineering skills? How do we upgrade and maintain the grid at the same time? I think that’s a massive challenge for this country in the next three to five years,” Elder said. What’s next? The market may be getting more competitive but Fidra Energy is still on the hunt for new viable projects, according to Elder. Despite being headquartered in Edinburgh, and significant investment in local BESS projects, the developer is generally looking at opportunities outside of Scotland. “We’re not yet convinced on the economics, and this sounds a little bit contrarian, but we’re not convinced on the economics of batteries in Scotland,” Elder explained. “We think people will make money out of them for the next few years, but beyond that, we think there’s a huge risk of overbuild, high transmission charges, and we’re not convinced on the case for that – but we’re certainly looking at other bits of England. “I wouldn’t say location is our top factor. Top factors are size and grid connection. I think anything from 400 MW up we would look at in terms of a site size in the UK.” Elder said Fidra Energy is starting to look at European markets, too, and would possibly even consider smaller projects than its UK assets – although the developers broader strategy means larger markets on the continent will be the focus. “Given what we do, which is really looking at big, large standalone batteries, we’re not going to buy a battery in Ireland because it’s just too small a market. So realistically, it’s going to be one of the big European markets, or one or two of the big European markets, Germany, Italy, Spain, Poland.” The post Why Fidra Energy is building the UK’s biggest BESS project appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Zhero and Tesla Energy sign agreement for 3 GWh of BESS in Italy - Energy Storage
content: Zhero has signed a framework agreement with Tesla Energy, in collaboration with H1 Holdings, for approximately 3 GWh of battery energy storage capacity in Italy. The companies announced the deal to pv magazine . “The framework agreement covers storage projects totaling around 3 GWh, starting with 200 MW of shovel-ready plants. The initiative combines the expertise of H1 Holdings—a leading South African developer and independent power producer (IPP)—with Zhero’s pipeline of battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Italy,” the companies told pv magazine Ital y. According to Zhero, the projects will be backed by long-term purchase agreements, ensuring market access while reducing reliance on regulated support mechanisms such as MACSE. Tesla Energy will supply Megapack batteries for the projects. Zhero is currently developing utility-scale storage projects exceeding 1.5 GW and is expanding its presence in the commercial and industrial flexibility market, the company stated. “This marks a pivotal step in the transformation we have anticipated from the start: evolving from mere developers into true owners and operators,” commented Daniele Moriconi, CEO of Zhero’s Battery Storage division. title: Congressman presses DOT on Tesla FSD after 43 sleeping-driver videos
content:
Tesla Autopilot
Fred Lambert
| Sep 10 2026 - 8:48 am PT
A US congressman is demanding the Department of Transportation explain what it’s doing about Tesla’s Autopilot and Full Self-Driving after an NBC News investigation surfaced dozens of videos of drivers apparently asleep at the wheel.
Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi gave Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy until September 30 to answer five questions about the systems, which Tesla itself says “require active driver supervision and are not autonomous driving systems.”
What the letter says
Krishnamoorthi, an Illinois Democrat, wrote to Duffy on September 9. He points to an NBC News investigation that identified 43 videos of drivers who appear to be asleep in moving Teslas, 17 of them posted this year alone.
The letter ties that behavior directly to a federal probe that’s already underway. NHTSA’s engineering analysis, EA26002, covers roughly 3.2 million Tesla vehicles equipped with FSD.
Krishnamoorthi also flags a message Tesla vehicles display to drivers: “Drowsiness detected. Stay focused with FSD.” He argues the prompt does the opposite of what safety requires.
“FSD requires continuous human supervision, yet the message appears to encourage use of the system precisely when the vehicle has detected that the driver may be less capable,” he wrote.
Tesla has indeed often posted message on social media about being more rested when driving with FSD.
NHTSA is already one step from a recall
The probe Krishnamoorthi cites isn’t new. NHTSA
upgraded its FSD investigation to an engineering analysis in March
, the final phase before the agency either closes a case or orders a recall. That probe identified nine incidents tied to reduced-visibility conditions, including one fatality and one injury.
The letter zeroes in on a gap Electrek has been
tracking for months
: Tesla’s in-car monitoring doesn’t reliably keep drivers engaged. Owners have found cheap ways around it. Some drape a folded bill over the cabin camera. Others wear sunglasses to defeat the eye-tracking. We’ve documented a whole
genre of drivers filming themselves breaking the law on FSD
and posting it for clout.
That’s the core of the problem. Tesla’s own manuals say continuous supervision is required, and drivers keep proving how easily the supervision check can be faked.
The five questions
Krishnamoorthi wants specifics from NHTSA. He asks whether the agency is aware of the videos and whether they point to a systemic problem, whether it has contacted Tesla about the incidents, and what data it has collected on driver inattention in crashes since January 1, 2024.
He also wants NHTSA’s own assessment of how effective Tesla’s cabin camera actually is, and, pointedly, what findings would trigger a safety recall.
Electrek’s Take
Congressional letters rarely move a federal agency on their own, and this one lands on a DOT that hasn’t shown much appetite for taking on Tesla. So I wouldn’t expect fireworks by September 30.
But the question Krishnamoorthi is asking is the right one. Tesla built the cabin camera as its answer to years of criticism about driver monitoring. And a $20 bill defeats it. If your system detects that a driver is nodding off and its response is “stay focused with FSD” rather than pulling over and forcing hands on the wheel, you’ve designed the monitoring around keeping the feature on, not around keeping the driver awake.
NHTSA already has nine incidents and a fatality in front of it in EA26002, and Tesla has conceded its own software fix would have prevented only three of those crashes. Those sleeping-driver videos just show the behavior Tesla’s design invites. The real question is whether Duffy’s team answers honestly by the deadline, or lets it slide the way this DOT has let most Tesla safety questions slide. We’ll be watching and of course, you can stay on top of our own

title: Electric car sales doubled in Russia after Ukraine blew up oil refineries
content:
oil and gas
EV sales
Jameson Dow
| Sep 10 2026 - 7:00 am PT
Electric car sales
continue to rise
around the globe, driven to
newer heights
wholly unnecessary oil conflict
. Only a few backwards-thinking countries are resisting the rise… and one of those backwards-thinking countries is now seeing the light, but it’s for a unique reason.
Russia, as one of the world’s foremost oil nations, has never had any difficulty fueling its own vehicles. The abundance of gasoline has always led gas prices to be cheap in the country, which is one reason why electric cars have never taken off there.
Sure, there have been some EV sales, but for the largest and one of the most populous nations on Earth, the numbers have been quite low…until now.
The world is not in a normal time right now. Every country is dealing with spiking oil prices due to the
whims of a senile former reality TV host
, and lots of people are finally coming around to the idea that we should stop using this resource that literally everyone knows we should have stopped using decades ago.
Russia has been somewhat insulated from the effects of the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, primarily because it’s not really connected to global oil markets at the moment, related to
dumb war started by
doddering dictator: that is, Putin’s invasion of Ukraine.
Russia first began its war of aggression by seizing Crimea from Ukraine in 2014. For some reason (read: Europe’s
addiction to Russian fossil gas
), everyone ignored that for 8 years, until Russia decided to invade eastern Ukraine in 2022, starting the current “phase” of the conflict which remains ongoing.
In the last 4 years of back-and-forth in that war, Ukraine has shown significant resilience and has innovated new war tactics, in particular being perhaps the first, or most clear,
demonstration of systematic drone warfare
Most recently, Ukraine has focused on a tactic of penetrating surprisingly deep into Russian airspace and
blowing up oil refineries
Due to Ukraine’s refinery strikes, Russia is finally having difficulty distributing oil, even within its own borders. Reportedly the country’s refining capacity is now only 70% of its domestic usage, with 24 out of the 33 biggest refineries in Russia having been struck.
There are reports of long lines at Russian gas stations, restrictions on fuel sales in several regions, and a ban on exports of gasoline from the country.
All of this has been enough that in the last 3 months of the year, EV sales have
more than doubled
in Russia as compared to the previous year. From June to August of 2026, 26,543 BEVs/PHEVs were sold in Russia, up 118% from 12,187 last year.
This is still a relatively small number – in the same period of time, around 400k total cars were sold in Russia. So we’re talking about a market share on the order of 6% for BEV and PHEV combined, which is still well below the worldwide average (~25% and growing). And, since it started as a small number, a large percentage increase is easier to achieve.
But it nevertheless makes the point that, even in a country that is so heavily committed to oil, electric cars can make inroads when the case becomes so plainly obvious to everyone. Now if only it took less than 24 massive burning refineries to open their eyes…

title: Elon Musk's Boring Company raises $3B at $23B valuation, led by UAE
content:
Elon Musk
The Boring Company
Fred Lambert
| Sep 10 2026 - 5:57 am PT
The Boring Company has closed a $3 billion Series D funding round led by the United Arab Emirates, valuing Elon Musk’s tunneling venture at $23 billion.
That’s roughly four times its 2022 valuation of about $5.7 billion. And most of the case for it sits in tunnels the company hasn’t dug yet.
The company
announced the round
on September 9. Alongside the UAE and its affiliated investment entities, the investor list includes Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Temasek, Valor Equity Partners, Vy Capital, Human Capital, Shamal Holding, and Baron Capital. Musk marked the raise with a line about the company’s reason to exist: “Defeating traffic is the ultimate boss battle. Even the most powerful humans in the world cannot defeat traffic.”
The money is earmarked for hiring across engineering, operations, and production, for scaling Loop projects, and for more Prufrock tunnel-boring machine R&D.
The UAE is buying an unproven promise
The centerpiece of the deal is a commitment to build more than 150 kilometers of tunnel across the UAE. That’s on top of the Dubai Loop pilot the company was already awarded: 6.4 km of tunnel and four stations, with construction slated to start late 2026.
So the country leading the round is also the customer for the biggest piece of work it’s funding. Precast production for the Dubai pilot is underway, per the company, but no passenger tunnel is open in the UAE yet.
The one place Boring actually moves people is Las Vegas. Vegas Loop has now carried more than four million passengers, and Clark County has entitled a 123-station network after approving 19 more stations. The company recently started boring its 14th tunnel in the city, its 25th overall.
Vegas has gotten better since we last rode it. When we
took some of the first rides in 2021
, it was human drivers piloting Model Ys at low speed with no Autopilot. Now, it still pretty much that, but there are at least a few more stations.
The main problem with the Vegas Loop is that the company has yet to prove, even in simulation, that it is actually helping with traffic and is more useful than other forms of mass transit.
The company also started its first work in hard rock. Music City Loop in Nashville got its state permit on February 25, 2026, and tunneling began the same day. By August, two Prufrock machines were mining at once, with a third in final assembly in Texas.
A long trail of tunnels that never got dug
Since 2017, Boring has announced roughly a dozen city projects. Vegas is the only one carrying passengers. The rest is a graveyard.
The flagship was the Chicago O’Hare Express, unveiled in 2018 under Mayor Rahm Emanuel: 150-mph pods from downtown to the airport, with Boring footing a ~$1 billion bill. It never had financing or a signed contract, and it was
dead by the time Lori Lightfoot took office
in 2019.
The 2017 Washington-to-Baltimore Loop got conditional permits from Maryland and then quietly
vanished from the company’s own website
. In Ontario, California, a $45 million airport connector ballooned toward $500 million, and Boring withdrew rather than sit through a third-party environmental review. San Antonio’s transit authority picked Boring for a 9-mile airport-to-downtown system in 2022, then said the company simply
stopped answering emails
and the deal died in 2023. Fort Lauderdale’s beach tunnel, selected the same era, has been stuck in the same “ghosted” limbo. Los Angeles lost both the Sepulveda test tunnel and the Dodger Stadium “Dugout Loop” to community opposition and permitting.
That’s the record the new valuation is priced against.
Electrek’s Take
UAE is probably a better investor/project partner for The Boring Company.
They can probably guarantee permitting, and they like to throw things at the wall and see what sticks, which is basically Musk’s and the Boring Company’s way of operating.
My main problem with the Boring Company is that Musk promised me back in 2018 that he would release simulations to show how his loop concept was more efficient than other forms of mass transit, and he never did.
Without that, The Boring Company’s only innovation is boring tunnels a bit cheaper, and even that is up for debate since most of the cost reduction is tied to tunnel size and, therefore, capacity.

title: Nanrobot LS7+ review: This 70 mph electric scooter is absolutely insane
content:
electric scooter
Micah Toll
| Sep 10 2026 - 6:01 am PT
There are electric scooters, there are fast electric scooters, and then there are machines like the Nanrobot LS7+ that make you wonder whether we’ve stretched the definition of “scooter” about as far as it can possibly go.
The LS7+ is an absolute monster. It packs a pair of 3,000W motors for 6,000W of nominal power, with Nanrobot claiming up to 10,000W of peak power.
The company advertises a top speed of 74.5 mph (120 km/h), though Nanrobot itself notes that figure was achieved under optimal testing conditions and says typical riding speeds are closer to 58-65 mph (93-105 km/h).
And no, I didn’t take it all the way up to 74.5 mph. I like you guys, but not that much. I also like my skin in all of its current places very much, thank you.
I’m not opposed to going fast, but I choose my risks carefully. I’ve watched the speedometer tick into triple digits on electric motorcycles, but there’s something about hitting those speeds in the same position I ride an escalator that just gives me the heebie-jeebies.
Once I hit the 40s of mph (above 65 km/h) in a standing position on wheels the size of a salad plate, I start to nope out. So don’t expect this to be a top speed review like
on my last Nanrobot testing
, but in every other sense, I was there.
Lots and lots of power
The LS7+’s dual motors provide the kind of acceleration you’d expect from a combined 6,000W setup, which is to say: tons. The thing wants to go like a bat out of hell. And all of that power and torque available at the curl of an index finger means there’s plenty of oomph available for climbing hills too, not just simply rocketing away from a stop.
That’s also why I want to make one thing abundantly clear: This is not a beginner scooter. Not in the slightest.
If your scooter experience consists of cruising around on rental scooters or commuting on a typical 20-25 mph model, the LS7+ is a massive step up. This is the kind of scooter that should be reserved for experienced riders who already understand how powerful scooters handle, how quickly things happen at higher speeds, and how important proper protective gear becomes when you start pushing these performance levels.
Fortunately, Nanrobot has equipped the LS7+ with hardware that at least acknowledges what kind of performance we’re dealing with here.
There’s a steering damper to help maintain stability and reduce the possibility of speed wobbles, which is something I definitely appreciate on a scooter capable of these speeds. You also get adjustable KKE hydraulic suspension and four-piston NUTT hydraulic brakes.
The scooter rides on 11-inch tires, with both street and off-road versions available. The suspension gives it a substantial, planted feel, and overall the scooter feels well-built and appropriately beefy for the performance it offers.
Of course, “beefy” also means heavy. The LS7+ weighs around 119 lb (54 kg), so forget casually tossing this thing over your shoulder and carrying it up three flights of stairs. This is much closer to small electric motorcycle territory than your average last-mile commuter scooter.
Nanrobot also rates the LS7+ for a 30-degree climbing angle and a maximum load of 330 lb (150 kg). I barely approach half that with all my gear on, so I can’t speak for riders on the higher end of that range, but if they build it for climbing huge hills with a lot of weight, then you can imagine how it flew with me on it!
A seriously big battery
Feeding those motors is a 72V and 35Ah Samsung battery, giving us a hefty 2.52 kWh of capacity.
Nanrobot claims up to 81 miles (130 km) of range, though that figure is based on relatively gentle riding at 25 km/h (15.5 mph) with a 75 kg (165 lb) rider. Start regularly tapping into those dual motors at higher speeds and you’re obviously going to get considerably less range.
But that’s exactly why I’m glad to see such a large battery here. High-performance riding consumes energy quickly, and having more than 2.5 kWh onboard means you can actually enjoy the scooter’s performance without watching the battery gauge plummet quite as quickly as it would with a smaller pack.
That big battery is certainly part of what helps float the price all the way
up to $2,299
, though the dual motors, big suspension, and rest of the robust build all add to that figure, too.
Probably more scooter than you need
After riding the Nanrobot LS7+, my biggest takeaway is that it’s actually a pretty good scooter. It feels solid, the suspension is capable, the hydraulic brakes match the performance level much better than mechanical brakes would, the steering damper is a welcome inclusion, and there’s enough battery here to make the ridiculous power somewhat usable.
Sure, I can’t stand the annoying NFC card for unlocking feature, but that’s long been a pet peeve of mine, despite others enjoying the added security benefit.
Suffice it to say though, that in terms of build quality, the scooter checks all the boxes.
But it is also completely, hilariously excessive for most riders.
Most people simply don’t need a scooter capable of somewhere around 60-70+ mph. In fact, depending on where you live, a scooter this powerful and fast may not be street legal at all. Riders should check their local regulations before assuming they can simply blast down public roads at highway speeds.
For riders who have private property or appropriate off-road riding areas, the optional knobby tires could make even more sense. With dual motors, adjustable hydraulic suspension, plenty of ground clearance, and that enormous battery, there’s a compelling argument for treating the LS7+ as an extreme off-road recreational machine rather than trying to shoehorn it into the role of a normal commuter scooter.
That’s ultimately how I’d look at the Nanrobot LS7+. It’s not the scooter I’d recommend to someone looking for their first commuter. It’s not even the scooter I’d recommend to most experienced commuters. Really, it’s for the craziest out there that want something so powerful and fast that it’s barely a scooter anymore.
So if you’ve already ridden powerful scooters, understand exactly what you’re getting into, and want something truly extreme, the LS7+ certainly delivers.
Remember though, that just because a scooter can do 70 mph, it doesn’t mean you have to find out whether you can too.

title: Volvo kills off another EV for the US, but it has a replacement coming in 2027
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 10 2026 - 7:56 am PT
is pulling the EX40 from its US lineup, leaving the $60,000 EX60 as the brand’s most affordable EV, at least for now.
Volvo EX40 EV discontinued in the US after 2027
After it
discontinued the EX30
, its smallest, most affordable EV, earlier this year, Volvo is pulling yet another electric vehicle from its US lineup.
The EX40, which initially arrived in 2019 as the Volvo XC40 Recharge, will be dropped following the 2027 model year.
Volvo introduced the updated EX40, which will continue to be sold in Europe, but it will not be available in the US or Canada.
With the EX30, EC40, and now EX40 gone, the EX60 will be Volvo’s most affordable electric vehicle, starting at about $60,000. According to an
Automotive News
report, a new entry-level EV will arrive soon to replace it.
Volvo is reportedly planning to launch a new electric crossover by the end of 2027, starting at under $50,000.
The new EX50 will ride on Volvo’s SPA3 platform, the same one that underpins the EX60, bringing much-needed improvements, including a longer driving range, faster charging, and more interior space.
filed a trademark
with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) under the name EX50 on July 14, 2026. Although the filing didn’t reveal much, it did confirm it will, in fact, be electric.
Volvo EX50 trademark filing (Source: EUIPO)
According to the
report, Volvo’s new electric EX50 crossover will be taller and longer than the current EX40.
While $50,000 isn’t necessarily what most would consider an “entry-level” vehicle, it is still cheaper than the EX60.
2027 Volvo EX60 P6 Plus
starts at $59,795 (including destination fee) and offers an EPA-estimated range of up to 307 miles. The outgoing 2026 EX40 starts at $56,545 and offers up to 296 miles of range.
Volvo EX60 (Source: Volvo)
As the first vehicle based on its SPA3 platform, Volvo calls the EX60 a “game-changing SUV,” offering more than enough range, ultra-fast charging, and improved performance.
Thanks to its 800V electrical architecture, the new EX60 can add 165 miles of range in just 10 minutes.
Volvo EX60 interior (Source: Volvo)
It’s also Volvo’s first EV with a built-in NACS charge port, enabling access to over 29,000 Tesla Superchargers without an adapter.
Measuring 189.1″ in length, 81.4″ in width, and 64.4″ in height, with a wheelbase of 116.9″, the EX60 is about the size of a Tesla Model Y (188.8″ L x 83.8 ” W x 63.4″ H).
Electrek’s Take
While it is sad to see another EV being discontinued in the US, hopefully Volvo comes through and launches the new EX50 in 2027.
The EX40 was a solid electric SUV, and still is. However, with the Trump Administration’s policy changes, including ending the $7,500 federal EV tax credit and the added import tariffs, Volvo has struggled to sell electric vehicles in the US.
Volvo already scaled back on its commitment to go all-electric by 2030. The EX60 is only about $3,000 more than the EX40, but $60,000 is still not cheap.
At about $50,000, the upcoming EX50 will become Volvo’s new entry-level EV, which is still around $15,000 more than the promised $35,000 EX30 that never arrived in the US.

title: 超5GWh，天合、亿纬锂能等4企发布储能订单新动态
content:

天合储能工商业储能柜项目落地
9月9日，天合储能宣布，近日浙江绍兴一家铜铝精深加工企业储能项目正式落地。该储能项目配置12台天合储能Potentia蓝海2工商业一体化储能柜，建成1.5MW/3.132MWh用户侧储能电站。
值得注意的是，这是行业首款AI仿生液冷工商业储能产品。天合光能蓝海2搭载A级优+车规级314Ah天合芯，自研Pack Pro模组，采用AI仿生变频液冷温控，电芯温差稳定≤2.1℃。
亿纬锂能签约5GWh储能合作
9月9日，亿纬锂能宣布，已于近日与中铁北京工程局集团有限公司进行战略合作协议签约。
双方围绕新能源领域合作愿景、储能技术应用场景及基础设施建设协同等话题充分交换意见，将建立长期稳定的战略合作关系。
此外，双方明确将建立专项工作对接机制，约定未来三年储能项目合作规模不少于5GWh。
华为数字能源签泰国储能系统合作
据泰媒Thailand4 9月8日报道，Siam Global House、AESCON、Integra R.E.三家泰国企业在华为深圳展厅签署谅解备忘录，将部署华为的电池储能系统技术。
根据备忘录，三家泰国企业计划在3年内在Siam Global House的所有分支机构中部署华为的241kWh LUNA2000-241-2S1 BESS解决方案。
此次合作中，Siam Global House将作为项目业主，牵头推动合作，Integra R.E.则与华为合作，负责当地的协调工作、技术支持及质量保证，AESCON则承包项目EPC，涵盖安装、现场项目管理及系统调试。
派能落地中国台湾表后储能项目
9月9日，派能科技宣布，近期在中国台湾地区多个大型制造业用户侧储能项目投运，合计总容量14MWh。

title: Fraunhofer IFAM develops real-time diagnostics for electrolyzers and fuel cells
content:
Conventional impedance spectroscopy requires systems to be taken offline to reach a steady state, making measurements time-consuming and unable to reflect actual fluctuating operating conditions. The new dynamic method superimposes a small multi-frequency signal onto the normal operating current and simultaneously measures how current and voltage respond. The ratio of these quantities is used to calculate complex impedance – the system’s frequency-dependent electrical resistance – which reveals the condition of individual components such as the membrane and electrodes.
“With our new dynamic measurement method, we are obtaining meaningful data directly from the actual running process for the first time, using significantly higher current levels than in the previous laboratory setup,” said Dr. Hermann Pleteit, project manager at Fraunhofer IFAM.
The method has been scaled from laboratory conditions to real-world dimensions, allowing operating currents of up to 30 amperes to be superimposed on the measurement signal. Online data processing calculates and displays the temporal evolution of impedance in real time, enabling predictive maintenance and early detection of issues such as catalyst degradation, membrane wear, and deteriorating electrical contacts.
“Instead of reacting only after the system has already shut down, we can precisely predict maintenance needs and avoid costly downtime,” Pleteit continued.
The system is designed for direct integration into plant control systems, including energy management systems, for operators of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells and alkaline electrolyzers. Combined with AI-based models, the results can be applied to changing environmental conditions such as pressure and temperature fluctuations, as well as to new material compositions.
“This allows us to significantly reduce lifetime costs and ensure the economic viability of green hydrogen projects – a key component for the competitiveness of the hydrogen economy,” Pleteit added.

title: Metacon and PERIC bring upgraded electrolysis stacks to Europe
content:
The new stack design offers up to 17% higher operating current density and up to 13% lower cell-plate weight compared with the previous reference design. It is designed to operate flexibly across a broad load range, including temporary operation above nominal capacity, depending on final system configuration and operating conditions.
Design and manufacturing improvements are also expected to reduce stack-level costs and improve competitiveness at the system level. The technology is being deployed in ongoing, planned, and future commercial projects.
PERIC Hydrogen Technologies, based in Handan, China, is a state-owned hydrogen technology research institute. Its portfolio includes a range of stack sizes, with the 5 MW stack used in large industrial production designs. PERIC also manufactures 10 MW and 15 MW stacks and has annual production capacity of around 6.5 GW.
Metacon said the new stack generation is intended to address key cost drivers in large-scale hydrogen production and improve competitiveness based on levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH).
Christer Wikner, Chief Executive Officer and President of Metacon, said: “For industrial hydrogen production, the decisive factor is not only the cost for installed capacity, but also the long-term aggregated cost of every kilogram of hydrogen produced. By improving stack efficiency, durability and operating flexibility, this next generation of pressurised alkaline electrolysers directly addresses key drivers of LCOH and strengthens the commercial case for large-scale green hydrogen projects.”

Under the agreement, Hydrasun will develop production capabilities for the assembly and integration of Nel’s containerized PEM technology platform, procuring, integrating, and manufacturing the balance of plant systems surrounding the electrolyzer stack. The partnership gives Nel an integration partner in Europe to complement its existing setup in the US, expanding manufacturing flexibility and strengthening supply chain resilience. Hydrasun’s initiative is supported by the Scottish Government’s Just Transition Fund, and the company plans to invest in and upgrade its facilities in Aberdeen, Scotland, to support clean technology manufacturing.

Tushar Ghuwalewala, SVP PEM Operations at Nel, said: “We are pleased to be working with Hydrasun to establish an experienced European integration partner for our standardized PEM electrolyser solutions, the MC Series. title: Check Out The Ferrari Luce EV's New Look
content:
The massive wheels can stay but the fixed rear wing needs to go.
Photo by:
6:50pm ET
Well that was fast. The tuning market is never slow to slap its brands all over brand-new supercars, and
Vossen Wheels
is the latest to put its gear on the all-new
Ferrari Luce
. Maranello's first-ever EV has been controversial, to say the least. Its pebble-smooth sedan design hasn't exactly been welcomed by the Ferrari faithful. So it'll be interesting to see how enthusiasts customize them over time, and this Vossen-modded car is the first glimpse we'll get.
Unsurprisingly, Vossen's main upgrade is a new set of wheels, being a wheel company. I'm not one for massive wheels but I actually like the choice here. Big, dished G2-13T wheels that really fill out the Luce's massive wheel arches actually really work well with the electric Ferrari's design. Or maybe it's just because I'm a sucker for dished wheels. The size works, too, as I felt the stock Luce's wheels looked a bit too small, like it was a HotWheels car. But fitting these dishes, and potentially lowering the suspension, seems to really fill in the arches nicely.
What doesn't look great is the tacked-on rear wing. I think the Luce might actually look good with a rear wing, but this one looks like cheap and doesn't really flow with the car's design. I'd say leave the rear wing and keep the wheels—that'd be the best look.
When the
Luce first arrived
, the general consensus among internet enthusiasts and keyboard warriors seemed to be that it's a good looking car, just not a good looking Ferrari. Even with these upgrades, I still think that's true.
It's definitely better looking with the wheels and lowered stance—I just wonder how well the enthusiast and aftermarket communities will take to it as time goes on.

title: EVgo Is Adding More Fast Chargers Where You Buy Groceries
content:
More than 400 additional charging stalls are planned at Regency shopping centers, expanding a partnership that dates back to 2020.
Photo by:
1:29am ET
EVgo plans to add more than 400 fast-charging stalls at Regency shopping centers across the U.S.
The partnership began in 2020, and EVgo already operates more than 150 stalls at Regency properties.
New sites will feature up to 24 chargers, giving more drivers a chance to charge while buying groceries.
Public charging is a much more pleasant experience when you have something useful to do while the car is plugged in. Buying groceries beats waiting around and watching the battery percentage creep upward, especially if it means avoiding a separate trip just to charge. That’s why more
retailers are adding fast charging
for customers to top up their EVs while checking items off their shopping lists.
EVgo is expanding its footprint through its existing partnership with shopping center owner Regency. The companies plan to add more than 400 fast-charging stalls at Regency properties across the United States, focusing on centers with grocery stores.
These won’t be the first EVgo chargers in Regency parking lots. The operator installed its first chargers at a Regency location in 2020 and already runs more than 150 stalls across its properties. However, the announcement signals a substantial expansion of that arrangement.
More On This
The new sites will feature up to 24 high-power chargers each. Planned markets include Colorado, Florida, Illinois, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Virginia, with other states that weren’t specifically named also in the mix. Neither company provided a completion deadline or a full list of locations, though.
It also follows
another EVgo shopping center expansion
. In August, it announced that it was adding at least 500 additional stalls through its partnership with Brixmor Property Group. That rollout is intended to bring EVgo charging to at least 90 Brixmor shopping centers.
another deal
, Kroger and EVgo announced plans to install at least 150 fast-charging stalls annually through 2035, covering supermarket brands including Fred Meyer, Harris Teeter and Smith’s. The Regency is clearly part of that broader push to make charging part of the weekly routine.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The latest announcement doesn’t specify charging rates or power ratings. Its recently confirmed rollout at Brixmor shopping centers and Kroger lists 350-kilowatt chargers, so that may be the peak output of the chargers installed at Regency locations.
Putting chargers near groceries is certainly sensible, but the experience still needs to be painless for them to be popular. As InsideEVs’ Suvrat Kothari
discovered during a recent visit to a Walmart charging station
, app problems turned plans for a shopping stop into 40 minutes of troubleshooting without adding any charge.

title: EVs Cost A Lot Less To Drive Than Gas Cars in Europe—Even With Public Charging
content:
EVs Cost A Lot Less To Drive Than Gas Cars in Europe—Even With Public Charging
Plus, EVs have gotten cheaper to buy, and there are hundreds of new models to choose from.
- New research shows that EVs were cheaper to run than combustion cars in Europe by at least a quarter in 2025.
- The ICCT’s latest study underlines that even when using more expensive public charging, EVs are still more affordable.
- Purchase prices have also gone down, with dozens of affordable models to choose from and over 150 in total.
It’s a good time to drive an electric car in Europe. With gas selling for roughly $9/gallon (€2/liter) in the European Union, EVs are gaining a lot of popularity, and lower running costs are a big part of the boom.
Last year, EVs that were charged at home and at public stations were 33% cheaper to run than gas-powered combustion cars, according to new research published by the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT), a leading nonprofit organization that provides research to environmental regulators.
Even when using public charging stations exclusively, which are typically much more expensive than home charging, EVs driven on European roads were 28% cheaper to run than comparable gas cars, making the ownership experience a little easier to bear in times when everything seems to be more expensive.
“Electric car drivers in Europe are paying about a third less than those with gasoline cars,” said Marie Rajon Bernard, ICCT senior researcher and lead author of the report. “Those savings are hard to ignore. They also explain why the car market keeps moving in one direction. We expect battery electric car adoption across Europe to scale up in the coming years if current policies are maintained.”
But the day-to-day costs aren’t the only thing that attracts car buyers to EVs. The same report shows that Europe now offers a huge number of electric models to choose from, with plenty of affordable options on the table. In Germany, the region’s largest car market, the number of passenger EVs has quadrupled from 2020 to 2025, reaching roughly 160 offerings. Of these, approximately 35 models are priced below €30,000 ($35,000) and are considered affordable.
The latest-generation Dacia Spring is one of the cheapest new EVs in Europe.
Except for the small and lower-medium segments, EVs have now reached price parity with their combustion counterparts for the medium, upper-medium, and luxury segments. When compared to plug-in hybrids, EVs cost the same irrespective of the segment.
Electric cars have also become cheaper over time, as long as we take inflation into account and compare similar vehicles. Between 2020 and 2025, prices have decreased by about 18%, whereas combustion cars have gotten 2% more expensive. It’s worth noting, however, that the landscape has evolved considerably in the first half of this decade, with many new models offering outrageous performance and extra-long driving ranges. These features come with much higher price tags, which in turn have increased the median price for a new EV by 42%. That said, there was no point of reference for many of these cars five years ago.
A big reason for the democratization of electric cars is the decreasing battery costs. The high-voltage battery is the single most expensive component of an electric car, and battery prices have gone down globally by about 35% in the past five years, the ICCT said.
Adding to all of this is an increasingly large, more reliable, and more powerful charging infrastructure. The EU now has nearly 1.2 million public EV chargers for cars, with an additional 2,450 for heavy-duty vehicles. That’s nearly eight times more than in 2020, and there’s still plenty of room for growth.
In the United States, where gas is roughly half the price compared to the European Union, driving an EV still makes a lot of sense financially. According to the Zero Emission Transportation Association (ZETA), driving a Tesla Model 3 costs roughly 55% less to run compared to a Honda Civic, as long as the EV is charged at home, though the figures vary depending on the state and the cost of electricity.

title: More And More Americans Are Interested In EVs: Study
content:
While high gas prices have done their part, it's the expanding charging infrastructure that's mostly pushing Americans toward EVs.
Photo by:
Suvrat Kothari
4:23pm ET
It isn't a matter of if electric vehicles become more popular than internal combustion, but when. It might not come for a while, but it's happening one way or another. And the switch is already starting, as data from the recently released
HERE-SBD EV Index 2026
shows that more American car buyers are interested in EVs than they were last year. And the main driver of American EV interest is its growing charging infrastructure.
What's interesting is that
EV market share
in America is actually down to 5.37% this year, an almost 3% drop, after the tax credit went away. However, despite the drop, when polled, 10% fewer ICE vehicle owners said they intended to buy another gas-powered car, according to the the report. Around 8% of ICE drivers said they'd switch to an EV if price and options were the same, while 12% wanted to switch over to electric regardless of price. That latter figure has doubled from last year, when only 6% said the same. So EV sales might be down, relative to piston power, but interest is up.
Gas prices are certainly having an impact, as around 57% of drivers polled said that gas prices are influences their desire to shift toward EVs. And eight out of 10 existing EV owners cite fuel costs as one of the main reasons to never look back. However, despite high fuel costs driving people to EVs, improvements in charging locations, charge speed, and EV range are still the biggest factors. With improved vehicles and an EV infrastructure that's getting better, more and more Americans feel more comfortable in making the switch than ever.
Photo by: Electrify America
"This year’s EV index shows Americans are becoming more open to the idea of driving an EV and more confident in the infrastructure needed to support them,” said Robert Fisher, Senior Consulting Manager at SBD Automotive. “While EV uptake may be slowing, the findings suggest continued investment in charging infrastructure is starting to translate into greater consumer confidence. Consumer sentiment often leads purchasing behavior, making confidence an important indicator to watch as the market continues to evolve.”
It isn't everywhere, as states like Iowa and South Dakota actually dropped in EV interest, due to a lousy charging infrastructure. Other states saw massive spikes in their EV Index, like Alaska, Oklahoma, and Utah. The top five states for EV Index were, in order from first to fifth, Delaware, Washington D.C.,
New Jersey
, Massachusetts, and Connecticut, proving that the East Coast is the most rapidly improving part of the country.
So while EV sales by themselves might not indicate that the country is moving in favor of them, the whole picture suggests that we're trending in the electric direction.

title: The Volvo EX40 EV Is Dead In The U.S.
content:
The Volvo EX40 EV Is Dead In The U.S.
Volvo’s first mass-market EV is being retired stateside, but a revised version lives on in Europe and other markets.
- Volvo is discontinuing yet another electric model from its American lineup.
- The EX40, initially known as the XC40 Recharge, has been retired stateside.
- Yet another facelift keeps the model alive in Europe and other markets, though.
The Volvo EX40, the Swedish automaker’s first mass-produced electric model, is being discontinued from the United States market. The electric crossover, which began life as the XC40 Recharge back in 2019, received yet another facelift for the European market, where it will continue to be sold alongside the EC40.
In the U.S., the coupe-like EC40 was dropped after the 2025 model year, and now the EX40 is joining that list, which also includes the entry-level EX30. All of this means the EX60 will become the de facto entry-level EV for Volvo in the U.S.
However, dealers won’t have to wait too long to get a fresh electric model, as the company is already working on a much more modern car that will replace all three discontinued EVs.
The refreshed Volvo EX40 lives on in Europe with a slightly redesigned front fascia and a bigger infotainment screen.
According to an Automotive News report, the new EX50 will ride on the automaker’s SPA3 platform, the same one that underpins the extremely capable and popular EX60. With such modern underpinnings, the new EV is expected to offer true over-the-air software update capabilities, as well as faster charging speeds and longer driving ranges.
The entry-level crossover is expected to arrive in the U.S. by the end of 2027 with a starting price below $50,000, which is not exactly cheap. That said, it will still be cheaper than the 2026 EX40, which starts at over $56,000.
Over in Europe, the aging EX40 and EC40 are getting a modest exterior redesign, with new LED lights front and rear, redesigned bumpers, a new tailgate for the EX40, and an updated front grille.
Volvo EX40 (2026)
Inside, a larger and crisper 11.2-inch central infotainment touchscreen comes standard and integrates Google’s new Gemini AI-enabled voice assistant. There’s also an updated wireless phone charger, new premium upholstery, and decor options.
On the safety side, the cars get new front and corner radars, a new front camera, new corner radars, 12 new ultrasonic sensors, and new parking cameras. All of these features are part of a new software and sensor platform that enables several new and upgraded safety functions, including a Door Opening Alert that warns occupants of cyclists and other road users before opening the door into passing traffic.
The optional Pilot Assist feature can now do lane changes and follow the car in front more smoothly, while the available 360-degree camera adds a 3D view that should make parking a little easier.
All of these improvements are also coming to the gas-powered 2028 Volvo XC40, which is going to be sold in the U.S.
Under the skin, the refreshed EX40 is available with either rear-wheel drive or dual-motor all-wheel drive, and a selection of three battery packs that don’t make much sense.
Gallery: Volvo EX40 (2026)
The P4 Long Range, P5 Long Range, P8 AWD, and P8 Performance AWD get a 79-kilowatt-hour (usable) pack that can be fast-charged at up to 205 kilowatts. Then, there’s the P5, which has two battery options: a 66 kWh pack that accepts up to 135 kW, and a 67 kWh version that can take in up to 180 kW.
The shortest-range model is the one with the smallest-capacity battery, which can travel between 270 and 292 miles (435-471 kilometers) on a full charge on the WLTP combined cycle. The longest-range model is the P5 Long Range, which maxes out at 356 miles (576 km) on the WLTP cycle.

title: This Electric Camper SUV Has Heated Floors, A Loft, And Built-In Storage. See The SkyNomad N90 Max Studio.
content:
This Electric Camper SUV Has Heated Floors, A Loft, And Built-In Storage. See The SkyNomad N90 Max Studio.
The SkyNomad N90 Studio is meant to be the ultimate camping crossover, or even a live-work space for professionals.
- SkyNomad is a newsub-brand of Xiaomi focused on family-oriented extended-range EV (EREV) crossovers.
- The SkyNomad N90 Max Studio includes two beds, an electrically operated loft, and heated floors.
- The SkyNomad N90 Max Studio starts at about $44,600 in China.
Xiaomi has been on a roll ever since it decided to branch out from consumer electronics to making cars. The sporty SU7 and YU7 have been critically acclaimed abroad, while maintaining a healthy presence on China’s sales charts. Now it's expanding its reach with the N70 and N90, big, family-friendly extended-range EVs launched Monday under a new SkyNomad sub-brand.
Xiaomi first spilled the beans on the basics of the SUVs in July. But this week it threw a curveball by revealing a previously unannounced top-trimmer variant called the N90 Max Studio. I’ll admit that at first I brushed the N90 Max Studio off as just another big Chinese luxo-barge. But this one seems special, even in China's already over-the-top car market.
Why? Well, because it sleeps four people. Pretty comfortably too, it seems.
Xiaomi SkyNomad N90 Max Studio
Xiaomi says the N90 Max Studio is meant to be a kind of live-work space for professionals, or the ultimate car-camping vehicle. The features and finishes are designed to be suitable for a mini, wheeled living space, and not just a car. The idea is to make the vehicle feel like a house, and a true private space to spend time. Now, we've heard that concept from automakers dozens of times, but Xiaomi has added some ingenious touches that make this SUV livable.
Xiaomi SkyNomad N90 Max Studio
The third-row seats have been replaced with a mattress. And the second-row captain's chairs are now a three-person-wide bench with upholstery that is more similar to a mattress, rather than a typical car seat. It folds down in one touch, Xiaomi says, and turns into a bed that sleeps two. The bed is about six feet long by four feet wide, roughly the same size as a full-size mattress. The bench also features a 60/40 split design, so you can sleep on just one section and leave the rest as a seat.
Xiaomi SkyNomad N90 Max Studio
But the real standout feature here is a built in pop-top tent that raises electronically to let campers stand up. On top of that, it can be closed off from the rest of the cabin to function as a loft. It looks wide and long enough to accommodate two more people.
The floors feature a wood-grain texture and are heated as standard. The second-row center screen can be removed and functions as a remote for the car’s features. One of the interior windows was replaced with a few storage cubbies, for a total of 20 liters of storage. The door of one includes a vanity mirror with a ring light.
Xiaomi SkyNomad N90 Max Studio
There’s now an add-on desk that slots right into the car’s center cup holders, power outlets, and a refrigerated compartment. In theory, you can drive the N90 Max Studio to a campground and have a nice time without much additional equipment.
The two-row N70 starts at $31,200 (209,900 RMB), while the top-of-the-line N90 Studio is $44,600 (299,900 RMB). Like most other Chinese vehicles, these prices wouldn’t likely resemble what they’d cost in markets outside of China. However, even in China, the SkyNomad EREV crossovers are competitively priced, undercutting big rivals from brands like Li Auto by about $3,500.
Xiaomi SkyNomad N90 Max Studio
Most SkyNomad vehicles are powered by the same 76 kWh battery, sending power to a 281 horsepower front motor and a 134 horsepower rear motor. They use a 1.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine to charge the batteries and extend the driving range as needed. Xiaomi claims up to 1059 miles of combined driving range (310 miles of pure electric driving) for the N90 Max Studio its most efficient N70, but this is on China’s CLTC cycle. If this car ever makes it out of China, expect these numbers to be lower.
SkyNomad N70
On the one hand, this concept isn’t super different from the conversion vans or mini-campers that were popular in the 1970s and 1980s. But it’s still not very common to see modern manufacturers craft their own ideas of what these features would look like from the factory. Volkswagen’s ID. Buzz California camper van is one effort, but not all that many other brands have followed suit. Xiaomi’s efforts look really clever. The Xiaomi SkyNomad series has officially gone on sale in China, and the company hasn't announced plans to export it elsewhere.

title: Waymo Just Made A New Friend In Nashville, And It's Not Uber
content:
Waymo Just Made A New Friend In Nashville, And It's Not Uber
With Uber partnership on shaky ground, Waymo teams up with Lyft in Tennessee.
- Waymo has started offering rides in Nashville, Tennessee via the Lyft app.
- The autonomous ride-hail company also offers rides through its own app in the city.
- Riders don't have to pick a Waymo and can choose to ride with human drivers.
Waymo is showing no signs of slowing down. The Alphabet-owned autonomous ride-hail company has started offering rides in Nashville, Tennessee, through the Lyft app, the companies said in a press release Wednesday. Waymo already serves Nashville through its own app, but teaming up with Lyft could widen its pool of potential riders.
The autonomous ride-hail industry in the U.S. is approaching an inflection point. Automakers, ride-hailing companies, and driverless-tech companies have bet billions on commercializing driverless technology, anticipating that self-driving cars will prove safer than human drivers. Tesla started rolling out its steering-wheel-free Cybercab in Austin last week, while Uber is gearing up to deploy Lucid Gravity robotaxis in the Bay Area by the end of the year.
Lyft said riders won't pay extra to get a Waymo. They just need to book a ride, whether Standard, Priority Pickup, Wait & Save, or Extra Comfort, that falls within Waymo's service area in the city. Right now, that area covers Downtown/Broadway, North Nashville/Germantown, East Nashville, Midtown, and South Nashville.
Jeremy Bird, Lyft's executive vice president of global growth, told Axios that the Waymo partnership in Nashville could serve as a blueprint for future roll outs in other cities. "The thing we will hold ourselves most accountable to ... is the utilization being high, regardless of what app it's on," he told the outlet. "We want this to be a long-term thing. We want you to grow with us, and we want to grow with you," he added referring to the Waymo tie-up.
But Lyft riders don’t have to pick a Waymo if they don’t want to. The Lyft app will include an opt out option for anyone who doesn't want an autonomous ride. Behind the scenes, though, the Waymos will run as a single fleet serving both Waymo and Lyft app users. That fleet is being managed by Lyft subsidiary Flexdrive, which will handle charging, cleaning, and day-to-day operations. Flexdrive is set to open an 80,000-square-foot depot in Nashville next month to support Waymos.
The team up comes at a time when Waymo's relationship with Uber is looking increasingly shaky. Waymos are currently available exclusively through the Uber app in Austin and Atlanta, but Waymo plans to end that contract by 2028 and serve riders directly through its own app in those cities, according to a Financial Times report. For its part, Uber has dozens of other AV rollouts in the works beyond Waymo, including partnerships with Rivian, Lucid, Motional, Zoox, Nissan, May Mobility, and more. The company has also lobbied for a law in Washington, DC, that would require robotaxi companies to also operate human-driven cars.
Waymo now offers fully autonomous rides, with no human safety driver on board, in 14 U.S. cities. Last week it added snowy Denver into the mix, which will be a real test of its ability to contend with harsher weather. By the end of the first quarter, the company had surpassed 500,000 weekly paid autonomous rides in the U.S. It is aiming to cross 1 million per week by year's end.

title: ZF Wants You To Repair Rather Than Replace Your EV’s Drive Unit
content:
New parts and training will give independent garages more ways to fix motors in EVs and hybrid cars.
Photo by:
3:19am ET
ZF’s new repair kits let workshops fix individual components instead of replacing entire EV drive units.
Over 100 variants of these electric axle repair kits are coming, alongside new options to service hybrid transmissions.
ZF hasn’t disclosed vehicle compatibility or pricing, so potential savings remain unclear, but it is a step in the right direction.
A worn bearing shouldn’t automatically mean that an EV drive unit needs to be replaced rather than repaired. That’s standard procedure for many EVs, but ZF wants to change that with its new repair kits for electric motors powering EVs and hybrids.
The automotive supplier announced more than 100 electric-axle repair-kit variants that will be rolling out in the coming weeks as part of its “Maintain-Repair-Replace” strategy. It prioritizes component repairs where practical, with remanufactured assemblies available when replacement makes more sense.
ZF says it has manufactured over six million electric motors for multiple automakers, for both pure electric and hybrid vehicles. For fully electric cars, it now offers what it calls the Repair Kit RD, which supplies bearing components for drive unit reduction gearboxes. The latter is the transmission that reduces the motor’s speed and multiplies its torque to drive the wheels, with bearings supporting the rotating shafts.
Gallery: ZF New EV Repair Kits
Those bearings are under significant strain as the shafts spin, and poor lubrication, contamination, or misalignment can lead to premature wear and failure. Other kits target ZF’s 8HP transmissions for hybrid applications. The first is called Kit EM, which combines rotor and stator assemblies for second-generation hybrid modules. Kit IN addresses fourth-generation inverters, while Kit ME provides remanufactured fourth-generation mechatronics (a transmission’s electronic and hydraulic control units).
ZF is pushing the message that a gearbox bearing problem does not necessarily mean the motor itself has failed and needs replacing. Giving a workshop the appropriate replacement parts (and training material) creates another option before the entire assembly gets tossed in the scrapheap.
According to Markus Wittig, Head of Business Line Passenger Cars at ZF Aftermarket, “The new solutions are an important next step in our Maintain-Repair-Replace strategy for electrified drivetrains. They make repairability more accessible for workshops and show how ZF is transferring OE expertise into practical aftermarket solutions for e-motors, hybrid modules, inverters and mechatronics. Together with our remanufactured portfolio, this gives workshops more options to reduce downtime, use resources responsibly and support electrified vehicles throughout their service life.”
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
There’s a growing market for cheaper remanufactured replacement drive units, like these for early Hyundai Kona and Kia Niro EVs, which are
around 30% cheaper
than what a dealer would quote. You can also get remanufactured
motors for the Tesla Model S and Renault Zoe
ZF’s wider remanufacturing catalog for electrified vehicles includes roughly 2,400 transmission entries, including around 600 mechatronics parts. Its EV parts range covers about 92% of Europe’s 20 most common EVs, encompassing brakes, steering, suspension, and drivetrain fluids, not just these new repair kits.
What ZF didn’t say is which cars the new repair kits are for, what they cost, or how much labor the repairs require. Until those details arrive, it’s unclear how big the savings are. Still, replacing the worn part rather than everything attached to it sounds like a step in the right direction and seems to fit with the EU’s broader push to make everything easier to repair and reuse, although ZF hasn’t said whether that influenced its plans.

content:

为你的 4 个不同角色解锁数十个独特的法术。优化你的构建或尝试一个新的方式试图击败 12 个强大的 boss。随着时间的推进你会变得更强，拥有匹配与敌人抗衡的实力。每次跑关都将测试你的技能和反应能力。

title: Newzoo 报告：若没《GTA 6》，今年主机营收将出现同比下滑
content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）无疑会成为年度重磅大作，但如果深入思考这款游戏即将大获成功背后的影响，就能发现它会产生连锁效应，为整个游戏行业带来积极拉动作用。
分析机构 Newzoo 近期发布的《全球游戏报告》披露了《GTA 6》的巨大影响力，报告给出多项大胆预测，其中最引人关注的结论是：如果没有《GTA 6》发售，主机硬件销量将会大幅下滑。
《GTA 6》定于 11 月 19 日发售，有望成为史上销售速度最快的游戏，单日销售额有机会突破 10 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 67.26 亿元人民币），将远超 2013 年《GTA5》创下的成绩。
Newzoo 这份全新报告指出，《GTA 6》的号召力不只是体现在游戏软件销量上。机构专家用一句话概括了它的作用：
如果没有《GTA 6》，主机营收将出现同比下滑，各大发行商也会围绕本作调整自家产品上线计划。2026 年 11 月《GTA 6》发售档期，还会挤压同期其他游戏的市场空间。
除此之外，《GTA 6》的上市“预计将整体拉高主机业务收入”以及买断制游戏消费。这点从《GTA 5》过往的成功就能看出，这款游戏十余年间累计卖出 2.5 亿份。
Newzoo 评价，《GTA 6》是全年市场的“压舱石”。仅仅依靠预售数据估算，它就已经登顶主机平台冒险类游戏收入榜单。
报告还认为，本作会成为今年行业的重要催化剂，重新拉动主机玩家规模增长，把普通玩家转化为付费用户，推动第九代游戏主机的普及。
《GTA 6》近期放出的实机演示，是 Netflix 史上流量最高的内容，短短几小时就吸引数千万观众。演示发布后的几天里，部分内容创作者获得了在苏格兰闭门提前试玩《GTA 6》的专属机会，陆续发布视频，讲解游戏的各类细节。

title: OpenAI 将为美国政府机构提供 AI 模型五折优惠，终止每年 1 美元试点项目
content:
9 月 10 日消息，据彭博社报道，美国总务管理局（GSA）发布声明称，OpenAI 将终止一项政府机构试点项目。该项目允许政府机构每年仅花 1 美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.7 元人民币）
使用其模型；新方案改为按用量计费，联邦工作人员使用该 AI 技术，可以享受标准售价五折优惠。
为推动模型在政府落地，OpenAI 在去年 8 月入驻 GSA 的 OneGov 采购平台，这个平台供联邦机构批量采购 AI 软件。当初协商的首年每年 1 美元
（现汇率约合 6.7 元人民币）
条款，是美国政府中央采购部门有史以来谈下的力度最大的科技产品折扣。GSA 介绍，试点期间共有 350 万名联邦雇员使用 ChatGPT，累计节省 14 亿美元
（现汇率约合 94.16 亿元人民币）
虽然新方案相比去年的 1 美元
（现汇率约合 6.7 元人民币）
协议涨价，但五折定价依然可以帮助政府机构测试并大规模部署 AI 工具，其中就包括 OpenAI 新款模型 GPT-6 Astra。OpenAI 将于周四宣布，这项折扣不再局限于联邦政府，州政府、地方政府以及部落政府都可享受。
这份与美国政府达成的新协议将于 10 月 1 日生效，有效期超过两年。
就在 OpenAI 2025 年和 GSA 签约几天后，竞争对手 Anthropic PBC 也谈成了同样每年 1 美元
（现汇率约合 6.7 元人民币）
的合作。几周后，这家开发 Claude 聊天机器人的企业在华盛顿联合车站举办大型活动，面向联邦工作人员推介自家 AI 产品，Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥 · 阿莫迪还现场发表演讲。
但对 Anthropic 来说，政府业务很快陷入麻烦：该公司与国防部爆发了激烈争执，起因是 Anthropic 希望在国家安全类合同中加入有关监控和自主打击系统的安全约束条款。
这场矛盾导致美国国防部长皮特 · 赫格塞斯将这家企业列为供应链风险。特朗普还在其 Truth Social 平台发文称：美国绝不允许一家秉持激进左翼、政治正确理念的企业，对我们强大军队的行动指手画脚，要求所有政府机构停用 Anthropic 的产品。
Anthropic 随即起诉美国政府。由于双方诉讼仍在审理，目前还不清楚不涉及国家安全的联邦机构最终是否会停用 Anthropic 的 AI 工具。GSA 最初下达指令，把 Anthropic 从官方 AI 模型平台移除，但加州受理此案的法官发布临时禁令后，GSA 撤销了该决定。
上月，加州案件的法官裁定，特朗普政府必须解除联邦机构使用 Anthropic AI 的禁令。法官表示，国防部固然可以在自身业务中禁用这套技术，但无权单方面强制其他政府机构停用 Anthropic 模型。另一桩相关诉讼仍在华盛顿法院审理，由三名法官组成的合议庭尚未就另一项法律主张作出裁决。
OpenAI 曾在今年 2 月发布声明，表示已经达成协议，向国防部提供 AI 工具。

title: 宝马回应新世代 BMW iX3 是否有哨兵模式：提供“停车碰撞记录”功能
content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，宝马中国今日发布新世代 BMW iX3 答网友问第四期，回答了关于是否有哨兵模式等问题。
据介绍，宝马提供类似的驻车安全功能，官方名称为停车碰撞记录。当车辆处于停车并上锁状态时，如果检测到碰撞事件，车辆会自动记录碰撞发生时周围环境的视频，并通过 MyBMW App 向车主发送通知。用户随后可在车内查看记录视频，并导出至手机保存。
该功能能够帮助客户在车辆驻车时遇到剐蹭、碰撞等情况 (达到一定力度) 时，及时了解情况并保留相关视频证据。
同时，停车碰撞记录功能主要针对可能造成车辆损伤的碰撞事件进行检测和记录。对于极轻微的接触或振动，系统可能不会触发记录。这样的设计有助于避免因风吹、轻微震动或停车场日常环境干扰而频繁触发提醒，为用户提供更加准确更有价值的通知体验。
宝马采用的是碰撞触发式记录逻辑。只有当车辆检测到真实的停车碰撞事件时，系统才会自动录像并通知车主。而部分品牌的“哨兵模式”采用持续监测模式，在有人或物体靠近车辆时就可能开始录像，并可能配合灯光或鸣笛提醒。
简单来说，宝马停车碰撞记录专注于在车辆发生实际碰撞后自动留存视频证据，并第一时间通知车主，在兼顾使用体验的同时，为停车安全和事故取证提供支持，且更加省电。
今年成都车展期间，该车正式开启预订，将于 11 月正式开启交付。各车型全国统一价（IT之家注：裸车价和选装价在全国范围内统一）如下：

- 新世代 BMW iX3 40L xDrive：29.99 万元起
- 新世代 BMW iX3 50L xDrive：33.99 万元起

title: 宝马氢动力 iX5 Hydrogen 上路测试：目标 5 秒内破百及 750 公里续航
content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，据外媒 BMW Blog 今天（10 日）晚间报道，宝马 iX5 Hydrogen 的开发计划正持续推进，原型车开始实际道路测试，为本世纪 20 年代末量产车型上市做准备。
宝马将该车的 0—100km/h 加速目标定在 5 秒以内，与纯电 iX5 相当。作为参考，全新 iX5 60 xDrive 的零百加速为 4.6 秒。燃料电池版本的最终功率和扭矩尚未公布，目前可以确定的是，该车将配备 xDrive 四驱系统，前后轴各由一台电机驱动。
宝马将效率视为该车的核心卖点，目标是加满一次氢气后，WLTP 续航里程达到 750km。相比之下，搭载 141kWh 大容量电池的 iX5 60 xDrive 标称续航里程最高为 845km。
氢气用尽后，预计不到 5 分钟即可加满，耗时接近汽油版或柴油版 X5 加油。iX5 Hydrogen 搭载 7 个高压碳纤维储氢罐，总储氢量最高为 7kg，乘员空间相比纯电 iX5 也不会缩水。
据IT之家了解，该车采用宝马与丰田联合开发的第三代燃料电池系统，体积较上一代缩小 25%。
目前，原型车正接受严苛环境与工况的考验，以验证燃料电池、驱动电机等部件能否按设计协同工作。车辆的动态表现也是工程师关注的重点：宝马希望氢能源 X5 保有品牌应有的驾驶质感，而不只是换一种燃料。
氢能源能否成为电池动力的有效替代选择，最终仍要看基础设施和氢气供应。宝马期待一款零排放、续航长、补能速度接近油车的车型会吸引消费者。
iX5 Hydrogen 目前仍是原型车，不过实际道路测试的展开，让宝马的氢能源试验距离量产上市更近了一步。作为宝马 X5 的第五种动力版本，该车预计最早于 2028 年上市，预计不会面向全球销售。

title: 沃尔沃在美推出 2028 款 XC40：外观内饰焕新，纯电 EX40 当地停售
content:
感谢IT之家网友
9 月 10 日消息，沃尔沃今天（10 日）宣布，将在美国停售入门级纯电车型 EX40，并为上市多年的混动 SUV XC40 带来改款车型。
2028 款 XC40 将于明年初抵达经销商，外观焕新，内饰全面改造。谷歌 Gemini AI 助手、更大的中控屏，以及采用新传感器和软件的安全系统都将上车。
预计将由尺寸稍大的 EX50 接替
。后者采用成本更低的 SPA3 平台，起售价或接近 5 万美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 33.6 万元人民币）
2028 款 XC40 重新设计了标志性的“雷神之锤”LED 大灯，前格栅、前保险杠、发动机盖和前翼子板也有调整，车尾换上新灯组和新保险杠。轮圈提供 18 英寸、19 英寸和 20 英寸三种规格，均采用钻石切割工艺。
此次改款的重点在车内。中控屏扩大至 11.2 英寸，最新的车机界面减少了操作步骤，方便用户更快找到所需功能。语音助手则由谷歌 Gemini 担任，可借助 AI 规划路线、寻找特定地点和绕行路线、管理消息。
2028 款 XC40 在安全方面也有升级，新的软件和传感器平台可支持实时避撞、自动紧急转向和自动紧急制动。据IT之家了解，新车前部及角部雷达、前视摄像头、后角雷达和泊车摄像头均有更新，还配备了 12 个新的超声波传感器。这套硬件带来了多项新功能：开门预警、变道辅助，以及更平顺的车道跟随辅助。用户还可选装 3D/360 度全景影像，方便低速行驶和泊车。

title: 法国总统马克龙呼吁欧洲大力发展自主载人航天，力争 10 年内送宇航员上太空
content:
感谢IT之家网友
软媒用户1238620
9 月 10 日消息，据法新社报道，当地时间 10 日，法国总统埃马纽埃尔 · 马克龙呼吁欧洲在 10 年内
具备自主载人航天能力
，推动欧洲航天业发展。
欧洲航天局（ESA）局长约瑟夫 · 阿施巴赫尔也提出了类似呼吁。当地时间 9 日，他在闭门会议上敦促各国部长和政要增加投入，建设
独立自主的欧洲航天业
。他在演讲稿中问道：“我们要做乘客，还是驾驶员？”
阿施巴赫尔指出，各国航天技术突飞猛进，进展遍及卫星研发、月球和火星探索等领域。“面对这一新形势，欧洲
必须拥有自己的能力
，成为不可或缺的合作伙伴。”
近年来，欧洲一直希望减少航天领域的对外依赖。但在载人航天方面，
欧洲尚未独立执行过任务
，仍需借助俄罗斯和美国的火箭及太空舱。
马克龙周四为欧洲提出了
未来十年的阶段性目标
：“两年后，我希望看到欧洲的第一个货运太空舱‘尼克斯’与国际空间站对接。还有五年后，欧洲首个月球着陆器 Argonaut 能够登陆月球；十年后，欧洲首个载人太空舱将从库鲁升空，载着欧洲和其他国家的宇航员进入太空。”
库鲁航天发射场位于法属圭亚那，是欧洲的航天发射基地。
然而，实现这些目标需要巨额投入。阿施巴赫尔估计，未来十年中每年约需 10 亿欧元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 78.17 亿元人民币）
。继续依赖其他合作伙伴同样昂贵，向外国服务商购买欧洲宇航员的飞行服务，十年就要花费 50 亿欧元
（现汇率约合 390.83 亿元人民币）

title: 看似不可能的黑洞合并，或许只是时空扭曲带来的宇宙错觉
content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，一项新研究提出，两个超大质量黑洞之间那场看似“不可能发生”的并合事件，或许并没有原先认为的那么违背物理规律。研究认为，参与并合的黑洞实际质量比此前测算的更小。
2023 年 11 月 23 日，激光干涉引力波天文台（LIGO）探测到时空泛起的微弱涟漪，信号来自一次黑洞并合。这个编号 GW231123 的信号之所以震惊学界，是因为它最初的解读结果显示，一个 140 倍太阳质量的黑洞和一个 100 倍太阳质量的黑洞发生了碰撞。
这一结果让研究人员十分费解。现有的恒星演化模型很难解释为何会形成质量如此巨大的黑洞，更何况这两个黑洞的自转速度看起来还极高。科学家一直在寻找这类特殊双黑洞系统的形成机制。而这支新研究团队提出，其实不必费心解释它的形成原因，因为这两个黑洞的巨大质量只是一种假象。
造成这种假象的核心效应是引力透镜。该效应最早由爱因斯坦 1915 年提出的引力理论，也就是广义相对论预言，引力波同样是广义相对论的推论。广义相对论认为，有质量的物体会扭曲时空，时空是时间与空间一体的四维结构。物体质量越大，时空弯曲程度越强，引力正是由这种时空弯曲产生，弯曲程度越高引力作用越强。
引力透镜效应是指：当背景天体发出的光线经过前方大质量天体附近时，前景天体会扭曲时空结构，让光线的传播路径发生偏折。来自同一个背景光源的光线，会因为偏折程度不同，在不同时间抵达地球。
光线抵达时间的差异，还会放大背景天体的亮度。天文学家早已利用这一效应，观测那些原本过于暗淡、难以直接观测的遥远古老星系。
这支研究团队认为，引力透镜效应同样适用于引力波。他们提出，GW231123 信号就是被引力透镜放大的时空涟漪，透镜效应让黑洞看起来比真实质量更大。
阿尔伯特 · 爱因斯坦研究所天体物理与宇宙学相对论课题组组长米格尔 · 苏马拉卡雷吉作为团队成员在一份声明中表示：“和光一样，引力波也能被大质量天体偏折、放大，还会拆分成多路信号。对于引力波来说，衍射与干涉效应，为我们识别、研究经过透镜效应处理的信号提供了额外手段。”
为验证猜想，研究团队搭建了引力透镜的数学模型，并开发出高性能、运算速度足够快的配套分析软件。
参与这项研究的斯拉什蒂 · 戈亚尔（研究期间任职于爱因斯坦研究所）介绍：“如果假设 GW231123 信号被一个质量约 190 至 850 倍太阳质量的致密天体，或是球状星团这类延展结构偏折、扭曲，我们就可以解释观测到的‘超大质量’结果。而且用引力透镜来解释，就不需要假设黑洞拥有极高自转。”
研究团队把这个条件纳入模型重新模拟该事件后发现，发生并合的系统总质量为 140 倍太阳质量，而不是最初估算的 240 倍太阳质量。
目前团队还无法确定，究竟是哪个大质量天体充当了透镜，扭曲了 GW231123 引力波信号。但无论这个透镜天体是什么，如果该研究结论成立，它本身就会是一个很特别的天体。
苏马拉卡雷吉说：“在我们的分析中，透镜天体的本质仍然是一大谜团。因为质量介于 100 至 1000 倍太阳质量的独立致密透镜天体本身就极为罕见。后续研究需要确认这类透镜天体能否形成，或是能否由恒星等大量轻质天体的集合体来解释本次事件。”
团队目前还不能下定论，确认 GW231123 就是人类探测到的首个经过引力透镜作用的引力波信号。想要找到更多同类信号，还需要提升 LIGO 这类探测器的灵敏度。
即便还没有找到更多实例，这项研究也证明，引力波天文学可以用来研究宇宙中最剧烈的天体活动。
IT之家注意到，该研究成果已于 8 月 25 日发表在《天体物理学快报》上。
