title: Battery tech firm Dukosi confirms Cook as CFO – Batteries International
content: Dukosi, the Scotland-based chip-on-cell tech battery systems firm, announced on September 9 it had appointed Graeme Cook as chief financial officer. Cook, who has more than 25 years of senior management experience across operations in the semiconductor, electronics and software development industries, has been working as interim CFO at Dukosi for the past eight months. Before joining the company Cook was COO at Apsis Business Components, a resource planning and project management SaaS company for the built environment and construction industries. Dukosi said Cook’s experience in financial management and strategic development will support the firm as it scales up to meet demand for its Dukosi Cell Monitoring System (DKCMS) and moves to commercialisation of the firm’s C-SynQ tech. C-SynQ is a communications protocol for EVs, industrial transportation and stationary energy storage markets. DKCMS monitors installed on cells capture accurate measurements of voltage and temperature using C-SynQ. Batteries International reported in November 2025 that Dukosi had won an innovation award for its technology from the European Association of Automotive Suppliers (CLEPA) in Brussels. title: Campine posts lower H1 earnings amid volatile global markets and lead price fall – Batteries International
content: European lead and metals recycler Campine has reported half-year EBITDA of over €47 million ($55 million), down from €53 million in H1 2025, warning that significant market volatility could dent full-year performance. The Belgium-based group said on September 1 the “resilient” results included overall revenue up to June 30 this year of €298 million (previously €384 million). However, if current market demand and low metal-price conditions persist, EBITDA for the whole of 2026 could fall by around 30% compared to last year’s record of €89 million. Existing low lead prices are expected to continue weighing on smelting profitability in the near term. This September LME three month lead future stands at $1,893/a tonne compared to $2,018/tonne in September 2025. The LME lead cash settlement stands at $1,870/tonne compared to $1,994/tonne last September. The drop in pricing makes lead one of the weaker performing base metals over the past year. Analysts attribute this slump to persistent high inventories sitting in LME warehouses, strong refined lead production out of India, and lead’s relative lack of exposure to booming AI and renewable energy infrastructure compared to metals like copper or zin Campine said it is yet to realise the full potential of battery recycling and speciality lead manufacturing operations in France, which it acquired from Ecobat last year. The acquired Ecobat smelters did not yet contribute to H1 earnings, partly reflecting the lower LME lead price — leaving what Campine said was meaningful scope for further operational improvements and synergies as it improves and further invests in the facilities. The downstream Le Plomb Français plant, also an ex-Ecobat business, performed strongly, supported by its activities in specialised anodes for zinc and copper smelters and radiation-shielding applications. Revenue from Campine’s circular metals unit amounted to €167 million, up 46% year-on-year, an increase fully attributed to the Ecobat acquisition. As a result of the less favourable metal-price market, the unit’s EBITDA dipped to €14.8 million compared to €16.8 million in the year-ago period. Despite sharply lower metal prices and reduced antimony trioxide demand (Campine’s main speciality chemicals product), EBITDA generated by speciality chemicals in the first six months of the year were more than twice the level in H1 2024 and around three times that of H1 2023. Campine CEO Wim De Vos said: “Downstream activities are performing well and the first synergies from the Ecobat acquisition are becoming visible. “With antimony prices returning to more sustainable levels and further improvement potential within our enlarged recycling platform, we remain confident in Campine’s longer-term prospects.” The post Campine posts lower H1 earnings amid volatile global markets and lead price fall appeared first on Batteries International .

title: China’s Reliance agrees €100m start for Serbia battery cells project – Batteries International
content: Serbia is to become the latest European nation to host a Chinese battery manufacturing plant under a deal with Jiangsu Reliance New Energy Technology. Reliance, whose portfolio spans NCA and LFP chemistries, confirmed on September 1 it will invest more than €100 million ($116 million) in the first phase of the project in the municipality of Inđija. This facility will be the company’s first overseas factory. Details of the agreement, including manufacturing capacity and the plant’s construction schedule, were not disclosed. However, Reliance said the plant would be its first such manufacturing operation outside China and would be dedicated to high-performance battery cells. Reliance is a cylindrical cell manufacturer and is also researching semi-solid and solid-state battery tech. Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić, who attended the project’s signing ceremony with Serbian economy minister Adrijana Mesarovic, Indjija municipality president Marko Gasic and Reliance co-founder and COO Xu Fenlan, said Serbia would be providing unspecified investment and other support. According to Chinese state news agency Xinhua, Vučić has said previously the plant will also support Serbian efforts to develop a domestic supply chain for batteries, robots and drones, while reducing the country’s reliance on imported components. Xinhua said Reliance’s investment followed the recent opening of a separate factory, in the western Serbian city of Sabac, by Chinese humanoid robots producer the Minth Group. Earlier this year, Batteries International reported that European LFP battery tech developer ElevenEs — which is backed by the venture capital arm of construction and mining giant Caterpillar — had completed the first closing of an investment round for its planned gigafactory in Serbia. title: Lanxess looks to European LFP market with new materials test lab in Germany – Batteries International
content:
Energy Storage, Lithium, News
Read Later
Lanxess tests impact of different grades of iron oxide and iron phosphate in LFP materials directly within battery cells
Speciality chemicals company Lanxess has opened a lab in Germany to test and further develop its materials for LFP batteries.
Lanxess said on September 4 the Krefeld-Uerdingen lab tests and develops battery materials based on iron oxide and iron phosphate.
Testing material properties of its products directly in battery cells allows the company and its customers to more quickly assess the impact of iron oxide and iron phosphate grades on cell performance, processability and suitability for specific applications.
The lab’s technical equipment is also suitable for other types of batteries.
Three-quarters of all electric vehicles use LFP battery tech in China. Meanwhile, the LFP market share in Europe is forecast to hit 50% by 2030 — an increase of 10% from now.
In addition to EVs, demand for LFP materials is being driven by stationary energy storage systems for renewable energy, datacentres and critical infrastructure.
Murat Gürsoy, head of innovation for iron oxides and iron phosphate at Lanxess, said cell manufacturers increasingly consider more than just raw material availability.
“What matters is the reliability of processing and its contribution to cell performance. This is precisely where our laboratory comes in. We bring material development and cell testing closer together. This gives us an earlier indication of whether a material works in a real cell assembly.”
Lanxess has more than a century of experience in manufacturing iron oxide and has developed specialised grades that can be used as raw materials in the synthesis of LFP cathode materials.
In addition to precursors for LFP cathode materials, the company offers key chemicals for electrolyte salts.
In September 2025, China’s CATL
unveiled
an LFP-based EV battery, Shenxing Pro’, specifically targeting the European market.

title: ProLogium investment as Li ceramic product sets new energy highs – Batteries International
content: A major Japanese utility has made an undisclosed investment in Taiwan-based ProLogium Technology — which has started mass production of the latest iteration of its lithium ceramic batteries (LCBs). ProLogium confirmed the strategic investment from Kyushu Electric Power on September 9, after the battery firm announced ‘giga-scale’ manufacturing of its LCBs in Taiwan on September 2. The ramping up of production of what ProLogium described as Gen 3.5 LCBs moves high-energy-density all-solid-state battery technology beyond laboratory and pilot-scale development, the company said. The Taiwan plant has been operational since 2024. A third-party test report, from German technical inspection body TÜV, showed ProLogium’s 185.4 Ah large-format cell reached 381 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density and 903 Wh/L volumetric energy density, the battery maker said. Comparisons follow. Lead-acid                                               ~30–50 Wh/kg Sodium-ion.                                            ~150–200 Wh/kg LFP lithium-ion                                      ~160–210 Wh/kg High-performance NMC/NCA Li-ion.   ~250–330 Wh/kg CATL Qilin Condensed cell (2026)          350 Wh/ kg ProLogium Gen 3.5 LCB                          381 Wh/kg Separately, UL Solutions tested the cell under Chinese solid-state battery standard GB/T 43568-2026. After six hours under vacuum at 120°C, the cell recorded weight loss of less than 0.05%, well below the 0.5% maximum threshold for all-solid-state classification, ProLogium claimed. The company said the Chinese standard has also been submitted to the International Electrotechnical Commission as a reference for international standardisation. The LCB platform was defined in 2012 and ProLogium has since shipped more than 2.4 million cells for a variety of applications. ProLogium’s cell architecture combines a ceramic separator with a proprietary edge-frame structure, creating an additional separator around the electrode perimeter to help isolate potential burrs while providing sealing and insulation. The company said the investment boost from Kyushu, an existing ProLogium partner, will spur the firms’ continued work on studying the potential of next-gen battery tech across a range of sectors, including construction machinery and other electrification uses where safety, environmental resilience and performance are critical. Batteries International reported in February 2026 that ProLogium had broken ground on the phased construction of a solid-state lithium ceramic batteries gigafactory in France. The Dunkirk facility will be home to production of ProLogium’s European fourth generation ‘superfluidised all-inorganic solid-state lithium ceramic battery’. title: Property Tax: The Value Driver that AI Data Centers Overlook
content:
In the race to bring new AI data centers online, the evaluation checklist has been standardized down to a site’s access to power and water, reliability, infrastructure density, connectivity, and room to scale. Yet one of the highest and most persistent costs of owning a US data center rarely makes it into early conversations: ad valorem taxation – property tax assessed on value under state and local law. Too often, property tax is treated as an accounting matter that surfaces once a year with the assessment notice or bill, rather than as a value driver in its own right. In practice, tax positions can and should be shaped, tested, and defended at every stage of a facility’s life, from design through years of operation.
Related:
Power Availability Now Determines Where Data Centers Get Built
The AI buildout has already altered the industry’s assumptions about power, land, and cooling. It is also rewriting assumptions about tax as compressed asset lifecycles and evolving ownership structures reshape who holds facilities and for how long. Less has been said about the tax consequences of that shift, where value is being quietly won or lost.
Facility vs. Servers: Two Tax Realities
The starting point is the often-overlooked difference between the facility and the servers inside it, from both value and taxation standpoints. A modern facility’s property tax value should consider both its replacement cost and its ability to earn income.
Server value
is driven far more by rapid technological depreciation and by which components within the rack are considered taxable in the first place.
On the facility side, most of what moves valuation traces back to one reality: capacity is getting harder to secure. As former NFL coach Bill Parcells would say, “The best ability is availability.” Power and water availability now take precedence over everything else, with scarcity increasingly dictating where a data center can be built at all. The rest follows from there – higher reliability tiers demand exponentially more infrastructure but command premium rents, while
rising rack densities
push AI workloads past the limits of traditional air cooling toward
costlier, specialized systems
. More generally, the ability to scale at high density, with matching connectivity, is rare enough to command its own premium. Each of these factors increases value and becomes a line item that a tax assessor can point to.
Related:
For High-Density AI, Available Data Center Space May Not Be Usable
Useful Lives and Obsolescence
The tax question centers on useful lives – the period over which an asset is expected to be usable and therefore depreciated – as well as functional and economic obsolescence. The most expensive components of an AI facility live far shorter economic lives than the building shell and back-end cooling plant (such as water loops, chillers, and cooling towers) around them, compressing depreciation assumptions into a much tighter window. Design deficiencies or “overbuilding” in speculative markets can themselves be value-diminishing factors. Whether that equipment is even taxed at all depends on state law, but where it is, the lower value pulls the assessed value and the tax bill down with it.
That lower assessment reflects that the asset is genuinely losing value over time, and its effects reach beyond property tax. But recognizing those short lives and insisting they be accurately reflected is exactly what keeps the tax bill in line with the equipment’s true value. The same short-lived fixtures can be broken out through cost segregation to accelerate federal depreciation under US rules, thereby shaping the depreciation schedules, income projections, and capitalization rate studies on which any credible valuation rests. Getting the useful lives right compounds savings across all of them.
Related:
Do Data Centers Really Boost Property Values? A Closer Look
Servers, Software, and Intangibles: Getting Costs Right
Servers require a separate review because their tax treatment complicates the valuation of the data center as a whole. A large share of the AI stack is effectively intangible and considered non-taxable in many states. And because integrated rack systems function as single computational units that fuse hardware, networking, and infrastructure, an assessor’s cost records may not map neatly to what is taxable. With few comparable assets to anchor valuations, the cost approach is often the only viable path, placing a premium on getting the underlying data and assumptions right.
The goal is not to pay less than what is owed, but to ensure the assessment reflects what these assets are genuinely worth. In practice, that means segregating taxable from non-taxable costs: identifying software, warranties, and pollution-control equipment that may be excluded or exempt. It means treating shorter useful lives as a genuine through-line rather than an afterthought, while still recognizing that more specialized infrastructure is not always the answer. And it means using income-based valuation where the facts support it and staying engaged across the full tax cycle rather than treating assessment as a once-a-year formality.
Conclusion: Put Tax on the Checklist
The point is simple. In an environment with few comparables and fast-moving technology, cost and income approaches carry more weight, and the assumptions behind them deserve scrutiny from the design stage onward. Power and site have earned their seats at that table. Tax and valuation belong there, too.

title: Electric cars and solar are the hedge against this out-of-control energy crisis
content:
A drone strike shut down Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline this week, knocking roughly 5 million barrels a day offline. That’s about 5% of global supply, and it pushed Brent crude above $104. US diesel is at record highs.
That’s the fossil fuel crisis making headlines. The quieter one is on your own utility bill, and it’s not getting better either.
The East-West line, also called Petroline, is the pipe Saudi Arabia uses to move crude to the Red Sea and skip the Strait of Hormuz. With Hormuz already choked and the Houthis squeezing Red Sea shipping, that bypass was one of the last shock absorbers left in the oil market. Now it’s gone too. One analyst put it bluntly: the buffers that got the market through the past six months “have basically been worn away.”
For anyone driving on gasoline, there’s nothing to do here but pay. A combustion car gives you exactly one option: the pump. When a drone hits a pipeline halfway around the world, that’s your problem, and your only move is to hand over more money at the station.
An EV gives you a second option. And right now, a second option is the whole game.
The domestic energy crisis nobody’s bombing
Look at the chart of average US electricity prices and you’ll see the other half of the story. Power in the US city average just hit roughly $0.20 per kilowatt-hour. It was around $0.13 in 2020. That’s a jump of more than 50% in six years, and the line has gone nearly vertical since 2022.
This isn’t a blip. The EIA expects wholesale power prices to keep climbing, up 23% in 2025 and another 8.5% in 2026, with natural gas costs and surging demand doing the damage. And the biggest new source of that demand isn’t you. It’s data centers and crypto mining, which the EIA pegs at about two-thirds of projected US electricity sales growth for 2026.
So here’s the setup. AI companies are building power-hungry data centers as fast as they can, utilities are passing the cost of new generation and transmission onto everyone, and residential ratepayers are absorbing the bill. We covered how data centers are straining the grid and driving homeowners toward solar and batteries back in May. It’s only accelerated since.
At this pace, US electricity prices are on track to roughly double over the decade. Two crises, oil and power, both trending the same direction. Up.
Don’t count on the people in charge to fix it
The honest read is that no one steering this is coming to rescue your bill.
Federal energy policy swings with every election. Utilities are regulated monopolies that make money by building more and charging you for it, so rising rates aren’t a bug in that model. And the data center boom driving demand is backed by the most valuable companies on earth, who have far more lobbying power than the average family watching their power bill climb. When the incentives of everyone with authority point toward higher prices, waiting for them to lower yours is a bad bet.
We wrote last month that energy independence has gotten personal. This is the same point, scaled up. The only part of this system you actually control is your own roof and your own driveway.
What independence actually looks like
Start with the EV. Forget performance and emissions for a second. I’d argue BEVs are better cars than ICEs overall, but their core advantage is choice. A gas car sources energy one way. An EV can charge from the grid when rates are low, from your own solar panels for close to nothing, or from a battery you filled at 3 a.m. on an off-peak plan. Every one of those is a lever a combustion car doesn’t have.
Add home solar and the math gets serious. Homeowners who’ve installed panels keep sharing real-world data showing bills cut to almost nothing, and pairing panels with storage locks in your cost of energy for 25 years while everyone else rides the rate escalator. Fuel your car off that solar and your cost per mile drops toward zero. No pipeline, no pump, no rate hike. You now own your own power plant that isn’t dependent on the whims of megalomaniac world leaders.
Then there’s the piece that ties it all together: vehicle-to-home. Bidirectional charging turns your EV into the biggest battery you’ll ever own. A Chevy Silverado EV paired with GM’s charger can power an average home for up to 21 days. And this isn’t a one-truck novelty anymore. The Ford F-150 Lightning, GM’s Ultium lineup, the Kia EV9, the Tesla Cybertruck, and the new Model Y Performance all support powering a home. Utilities are even starting to pay for it, like PG&E’s expanded V2X program offering up to $17,000 in incentives.
Solar fills the car. The car backs up the house. The house leans on the grid only when it wants to, not because it has no other choice.
Electrek’s Take
We’ve spent years making the environmental case for EVs and solar, and that case still stands. But this week is a reminder that the argument doesn’t even need the climate. It’s about not being a hostage.
Top comment by Cary Chevrolet
The "buffers" mentioned really are running out. Our Strategic Oil Reserve is virtually tapped out, and I'd guess China's reserves are close to the same. So I was expecting bad results going forward even before this pipeline hit.
On the electricity pricing, I don't know how common this is, but in Washington state we're also being hit by the forced elimination of NG electrical roduction by something like 2035. So there's a lot of investment required in new production facilities, and that adds to the costs.
Every combustion car on the road is exposed to a drone strike in Saudi Arabia, an OPEC decision, and a refinery outage, with zero ability to respond except to pay. Every home on grid power alone is exposed to whatever rate the utility and its regulators decide on next, and the trend there is one direction. Up. That’s the position most people are in right now, and both crises driving it are getting worse, not better.
The value of an EV, home solar, and V2H isn’t that any one of them makes you fully self-sufficient overnight. It’s that together they turn energy from something done to you into a set of choices you get to make. When oil spikes, you charge on sun. When rates jump, you pull from your battery. When the grid goes down, your car keeps the lights on. That optionality is worth more in a volatile market than in a calm one, and the market is not going to be calm.
You can wait for someone in charge to make electricity cheap and oil stable again. How’s that bet looking? Or you can put the panels on the roof and the plug in the driveway, and stop asking permission.
Oil is spiking on a pipeline attack and your electricity is on track to double this decade, so the one energy cost you can actually lock in is the one you generate yourself. title: New fleet of battery electric trains promises faster, more reliable UK travel
content:
Electric train
Jo Borrás
| Sep 12 2026 - 7:50 am PT
A new fleet of British-designed and built battery electric trains has been announced, promising thousands of new jobs, faster and more reliable rail service, and significant reductions in carbon emissions across northern England.
Often the butt of jokes for its frequent delays and confusing ticketing practices, the British rail system is set to receive a significant upgrade thanks to a broader series of transit contracts totaling more than €1.2 billion. Those upgrades will see Alstom and TransPennine Express will deploy 29 fully electric Adessia Stream electric trains,
which will be the first of their kind to be put to work on long-distance mainline journeys in the UK when they go into service in 2034
“This agreement is a landmark moment for Britain’s railway, and we couldn’t be prouder that the country’s first mainline battery-electric trains will be designed and built in Britain,” said Rob Whyte, Managing Director UK at Alstom. “The fleet will transform journeys across northern England while showcasing the very best of British engineering, innovation and advanced manufacturing.”
The British government says the new fleet of trains, which will be built in Derby, will support more than 6,000 permanent jobs across the UK. The focus, however, isn’t the jobs – it’s the rail service, itself.
“I’ve lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came. And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments and missed opportunities,”
British PM Andy Burnham told
The Guardian
. “Today that starts to change. These 29 new trains will bring faster, more reliable journeys to the north, and thousands of British jobs for the next generation.”
More than a rendering
Operating between Liverpool and Cleethorpes; via TransPennine.
Despite the fact that these trains aren’t expected to enter service until 2034, this story isn’t about something that’s just a rendering of some far-off technology. TransPennine Express has been testing battery-electric locomotives on its intercity trains since 2024. In that trial, the company replaced one of the diesel engines in a Class 802 Nova 1 train with a battery-electric system developed by Hitachi.
The new trains, developed by Alstom, will take that concept considerably further in becoming Britain’s first mainline fleet designed to operate primarily on battery power while operate at speeds of up to 110 mph. The trains will provide “around” 300 seats per train, including a comfortable First Class area with catering and dining facilities that promises to make the British rail a generally more enjoyable experience than it is now.

title: Europe's First Truly Driverless Robotaxi Just Started Rides In Croatia
content:
Europe's First Truly Driverless Robotaxi Just Started Rides In Croatia
A little known Croatian startup backed by Rimac is leading the way for robotaxis in Europe, with help from a Chinese AV company.
- An increasing number of autonomous ride-hailing services are coming to Europe.
- A little-known startup just began the continents first truly driverless rides.
- They're available in the Croatian capital via the Uber app.
Verne, the Rimac-backed autonomous ride-hail startup, has started fully autonomous passenger rides on public roads in Zagreb, Croatia, marking the first time that's happened anywhere in Europe.
The test rides run in partnership with Chinese autonomous driving company Pony.ai, and are available through the Uber app. They cover 22 kilometers (13.6 miles) between Verne's headquarters and a downtown business district with Zagreb's airport. Pony.ai already runs a robotaxi service in four Chinese cities and is now looking to expand in Europe while also growing in its home country.
Arcfox Alpha T5 robotaxi
Unlike the Ford Mustang Mach-E robotaxis recently launched in London by Uber and Wayve, which have human supervisors on board, the Verne test rides are fully driverless. Pony.ai's autonomous software actually executes the driving actions. Verne monitors the vehicle remotely, while its system makes all the active driving decisions like steering, braking, and acceleration.
Verne and Pony.ai already launched Europe's first commercial robotaxi service in Zagreb back in April, but those rides still had a human operator riding along as a backstop. Ditching that operator is the bigger next step for pretty much all big robotaxi companies. Even early Waymos here in the U.S. had humans supervising them, and so do some of the Tesla Model Y robotaxis currently. The Cybercab that launched in Austin last week is fully driverless.
That said, the Verne robotaxis are quite different from what we get here in the U.S. The base vehicle is an Arcfox Alpha T5 electric crossover from China. Verne has removed its front passenger seat to open up space for luggage and installed a larger display for the passengers seated at the back. This big screen is mounted where the passenger seat’s backrest would be. It shows key information like the route and riders can also stream videos or play games on it. Since there’s no co-driver’s seat, the rear passenger can fully stretch their legs too.
The company also showcased a Tesla Cybercab-like purpose-built robotaxi a couple of years ago. That concept, however, was far more suave than the Cybercab, with sliding doors, a panoramic sunroof, a much more opulent interior, and a giant theater screen. Verne says the purpose-built model is still under development.

title: Lawmaker Demand Feds Take Action After 43 Tesla Drivers Filmed Asleep At The Wheel
content:
One congressman is demanding that NHTSA look into continued misuse of Tesla's Full Self-Driving software.
Photo by:
Out of Spec Testing (YouTube)
3:13pm ET
A recent investigation by NBC found at least 43 videos and 13 citations tied to sleeping while using Tesla's Full Self-Driving software.
Owners are becoming comfortable with misusing the system as it improves, according to one owner.
One congressman is looking for answers from regulatory agencies on whether or not Tesla is doing enough to keep it from happening.
Tesla has a long history of controversy around the branding and marketing of its
Full Self-Driving and Autopilot software
. Despite what the names might suggest, neither software is
actually
absolving the driver from the accountability behind the wheel. That's caused confusion in the public eye, which many claim have enabled drivers to be more lackadaisical when either feature is switched on.
Lawmakers across the globe have taken up issue with the marketing in the past. And now, one U.S. congressman is calling for action after surfacing more than 40 videos of Tesla drivers seemingly sleeping while their cars barrel down the highway.
Photo by: Tesla
Illinois representative Raja Krishnamoorthi published a
statement
on Thursday outlining a demand sent to the Department of Transportation and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
Krishnamoorth's letter specifically calls out an investigation published by
that surfaced at least 43 videos—17 of which were posted in 2026—of Tesla owners operating their cars while sleeping or otherwise distracted.
also found 13 additional cases where drivers in California were cited for this kind of unsafe driving.
Some drivers are aware that what they are doing is against the law. One Tesla owner from California who agreed to be interviewed for the article (with the condition that his last name be withheld because he was aware that he was breaking the law) even admitted that he sleeps while FSD is activated, but seems to justify it because Tesla's tech has improved over the years.
As it’s gotten better
, the taboo has fallen away," said the owner.
Tesla does explicitly call out in its user manual that drivers must remain engaged and are responsible for the car while its Level 2 driver assistance features are active. It also has several safeguards in place to help prevent drivers from disconnecting. For example, Tesla's cabin camera tracks driver attention through eye and head movement. It also senses driver input through the car's steering wheel and will prompt the driver to take action if it believes the driver isn't paying attention.
However, some drivers have found clever ways to defeat Tesla's methods in a long-standing game of cat-and-mouse. Some simply put on sunglasses to hide their eyes. Others
place a doll head or photo of themselves in front of the car's cabin-facing camera
. There are a handful of other methods which don't rely on the camera as well. All of these workarounds make it possible for drivers to break Tesla's terms and conditions (and the law).
The nag is a fine line for Tesla and other automakers to walk. On one hand, it ensures that drivers are paying attention to the road. On the other, too much nag and drivers simply won't use the feature. When that feature is a $99 per month subscription and is
tied to the CEO's trillion-dollar pay package
, making it frictionless to use is likely a major priority.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Krishnamoorth's letter calls on NHTSA to answer several questions specifically aimed to scope just how much the agency has probed Tesla on the topic of its self-driving software. He asks for details on the data that the agency has collected, its current assessment on Tesla's effectiveness to deter misuse of its systems, and specifically if its current findings conclude a broader safety defect that may require a recall.
NHTSA, meanwhile, already has an open investigation into 3.2 million FSD-equipped Teslas in a separate probe. And while the drivers are unquestionably responsible for remaining awake and in-control, the question then becomes whether or not Tesla's current detection methods are reasonable, or if the automaker is responsible for stricter policing of these features.

title: This Chinese Luxury Brand Wants To Take Europe By The End Of The Year
content:
This Chinese Luxury Brand Wants To Take Europe By The End Of The Year
In 2023, Li Auto said it wouldn't go global until 2028, but it now plans to launch an EV before the end of this year.
- Li Auto will show off the European version of the i6 electric crossover and announce its full European expansion plans at this year's Paris Auto Show.
- The Li Auto i6 will be called the "Li 6" when it goes on sale in Europe.
- The Li Auto i6 is a 5-seat crossover with an 87.3 kWh battery. In China, it competes with the Tesla Model Y. It is one of Li Auto's best-selling models.
Chinese brands like BYD, Geely, Zeekr, and Jaecoo are quickly becoming known quantities all around the globe. Li Auto, a popular Chinese brand that hasn't pushed as hard for global domination thus far, could join them soon.
This luxury brand makes medium- and large-sized extended-range EVs and full EVs, is not doing much outside of China, save for a cautious launch in the Middle East. In fact, Li Auto CEO Li Xiang said in 2023 that it has no plans to go global before 2028.
Well, it looks like that’s changing. Li Auto announced on Thursday that it will show off the i6 crossover—its first model destined for Europe—at the Paris Auto Show in October. The automaker said it was targeting a European entry in the second half earlier this year. On Thursday, it said the Paris Auto Show will be where it reveals "global full product lineup and market rollout plans, alongside deeper insights into its European strategy and future product roadmap."
Li Auto has two product lines. Firstly, the L series are conventionally styled, extended-range SUVs. For those cars, the power is electric, but there’s a gas engine under the hood that is used to increase driving range when the main battery runs out.
Li Auto L6
The brand’s fully electric line is called the “i” series. Li Auto markets these as SUVs, but in reality they're more like low-slung MPVs. The i6 is Li Auto’s entry-level electric car, and one of its best-selling models. In China, the i6 goes head-to-head with cars like the Tesla Model Y. For the European market, the company will drop the “Auto” part and just go by Li. Similarly, the i6 will simply be called the 6.
Gallery: Li Auto i6
The specifications of the European version of the Li Auto i6 haven’t been released. In China, all i6’s come with the same 87.3 kWh battery. That energy goes to either one rear-mounted motor or two, proving all-wheel drive. Single-motor i6s produce 335 horsepower, or 536 horsepower in dual-motor form. The car can travel up to 447 miles on a charge, although that is on China’s more lenient CLTC standard.
I’m curious to see just how well Li Auto’s models will fare. Li Auto’s prices may seem cheap for those outside of China; the Li Auto i6 starts at about $36,000 in its home country, but it isn’t the cheapest in its segment. Li Auto’s top-of-the-line EREV models can easily touch more than $75,000 in China. Add in tariffs and a naturally higher price due to a different competitive environment in Europe, and I don’t anticipate the Li Auto i6 being all that cheap. Depending on pricing, the i6 could easily end up going head-to-head with cars like the new BMW iX3 or Mercedes-Benz GLC.

title: Unpacking Ford's Spat With The Trump Administration Over China
content:
Washington wants to push back against China's car industry. But what exactly does that mean?
Photo by:
7:00am ET
The political battle over China’s car industry is heating up, and Ford just got caught in the crossfire.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy sent a
scathing letter
to Ford CEO Jim Farley this Tuesday, urging him to cut ties with Chinese companies. Duffy expressed “profound concern” at Ford’s strategic direction, and said he was “deeply alarmed” by the automaker’s licensing deal with CATL to make lithium iron phosphate batteries in Michigan.
“When a company intentionally chooses to deepen operational dependencies on strategic competitors, it fails to act as the reliable partner the American public and this DOT require,” the letter reads. Brutal stuff.
Clearly, even American companies aren’t safe from the growing backlash to China’s auto industry. But the Ford spat also exposes just how scattered America’s China-car policy is becoming. Washington seems certain that it wants to disentangle the U.S. auto industry from China—and less sure what that actually means.
[We discuss the Ford situation, Mack's first drive in the Jeep Recon, the Tesla Cybercab hitting streets, and more on this week's Plugged-In Podcast.
Check it out!
It’s not obvious why Ford, of all the Detroit automakers, got singled out. General Motors uses Chinese batteries in the Chevy Bolt. Stellantis (which is only part American, but still) owns part of Leapmotor and distributes that company’s cars abroad. Slate (small potatoes, to be sure) is using LFP batteries produced in the U.S. by China’s Gotion.
Notably, Duffy doesn’t accuse Ford of breaking any laws, so it’s even less clear why the administration is lashing out at it specifically.
Ford seemed completely blindsided by this, and it clapped back hard. The company slammed Duffy’s letter as a “wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines” and posted a
response on its website. Farley gave an interview to
The Wall Street Journal
to correct the record.
On the one hand, it has seemed like “we don’t want Chinese cars” is a rallying cry both sides of the aisle can get behind—a rarity these days. The U.S. already has 100% tariffs on Chinese vehicles and a ban on certain Chinese tech. Both were established in the Biden years. A Senate committee recently advanced an even stricter bill that would bar auto companies that have more than 15% Chinese ownership from selling in America. Another proposal would keep Chinese cars from crossing the Mexican or Canadian borders into America, even if they were sold legally in those countries.
Critical Materials subscribers got this early.
Our newsletter breaks down the biggest mobility news every Friday.
At the same time, the anti-China effort at the federal level comes off as increasingly unpredictable. Just days ago, the White House praised the very same battery plant in Michigan that Duffy’s letter blasted. After this controversy blew up this week, the White House’s rapid response X account posted that Ford “is a GREAT American company and has done a tremendous job on increasing investments domestically and shoring production back to the U.S.” So which is it?
Likewise, Geely-controlled Polestar was kicked out of the U.S. market this year due to its Chinese tech, while Geely-controlled Volvo managed to stick around. (The Volvo EX90 and Polestar 3 even share a platform and are built at the same facility in South Carolina.) Polestar still has no idea what happened. On top of it all, Senator Elissa Slotkin
on X this week that she heard a rumor that President Trump plans to open the U.S. to Chinese cars within weeks.
It’s not even clear that prohibiting U.S. automakers from dealing with China is the right move. There’s a solid argument that it isn’t. After all, China’s auto companies learned from American and European ones through joint ventures, then leapfrogged the world. Now Chinese manufacturers set the bar in terms of development speed, in-vehicle technology, and battery production.
Duffy says the goal is to “out-innovate competitors.” But based on how far ahead China is right now, that may not be possible on American gumption alone.

title: Your EV Has Two Horsepower Ratings. Automakers Only Advertise One
content:
One is the peak output available for short bursts. The other reveals how much power the drivetrain can sustain for considerably longer.
Photo by:
Andrei Nedelea
9:00am ET
Advertised EV horsepower is usually the peak output available only for short bursts.
The UN’s 30-minute rating shows how much power an EV can sustain for longer.
Cooling, battery charge, and drivetrain design determine how consistently an EV delivers full power.
That EV you see advertised with over 1,000 horsepower should probably carry an asterisk and an explanation. Yes, it can deliver that much power, but only temporarily when you mat the accelerator. Look at its registration documents in some European countries, and you might be surprised to see a much lower power figure than what the manufacturer advertises.
Auto Motor und Sport
recently highlighted that electric drivetrains effectively have two legitimate power ratings: maximum peak output and sustained output. Automakers build their advertising around the first, while the second is largely confined to homologation documents. The sustained figure is not a number that gets much attention.
It’s the continuous power that the complete drivetrain can maintain without overheating.
Peak power figures are what sell EVs, particularly performance models, so manufacturers typically only show this figure, and they’re not lying. Electric motors can accept a lot of current for a short burst, allowing the drivetrain to deliver far more power than it can maintain for extended periods.
More On This
The main reason for the gap between maximum and sustained power is heat. High current generates heat inside the battery, motor windings, and the inverter. Once any of these components reach a certain temperature, the control system reduces current—and therefore torque and power—to protect them.
Peak power also depends on the battery state of charge. You likely won’t notice it in normal driving, but as the battery discharges, its voltage falls, and the drivetrain may eventually be unable to provide its rated peak power. When that reduction happens and how noticeable it is varies considerably between EVs, and they typically draw more current to compensate for the voltage drop.
The size of the gap between peak and sustained output doesn’t depend on motor type alone. Permanent-magnet, induction, and externally excited motors generate and shed heat differently, but battery output, inverter efficiency and the design and efficiency of the cooling system matter even more.
Photo by: Andrei Nedelea
EVs also have a less familiar official power number. It’s called “maximum 30-minute power,” and it’s defined under
UN Regulation No. 85
. It measures the highest average net output an electric drivetrain can maintain over a standardized 30-minute test. That is why an EV advertised with 1,000 hp may have a much lower figure in its registration papers. This is its continuous power.
The 30-minute figure is more relevant to repeated acceleration, sustained high-speed driving or pulling a heavy trailer. It still can’t predict exactly how an EV will perform in those situations because temperature, battery charge, and cooling strategy all have an effect on the outcome, but it provides a standardized way to compare how much power different EVs can sustain.
Real-world testing shows why the advertised number tells only part of the story. In a
Car and Driver
track test, an 835 hp
Rivian R1T
and a 430 hp
Lucid Air
began slowing as their batteries discharged, while a 320 hp
Hyundai Ioniq 5
maintained consistent acceleration until its charge dropped below 20%.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The Hyundai’s battery could supply more power than its motors demanded, giving it useful headroom. That is ultimately what buyers aren’t being told: peak horsepower describes an EV’s best moment, while thermal engineering and power reserves determine how consistently it can reproduce it.
Automakers also understand the difference between peak and sustained power, even if they don't advertise it. Tesla’s Track Mode includes a 'Powertrain Endurance' setting that deliberately reduces power to slow battery and motor overheating, sacrificing outright pace for more consistency. This is a direct admission by a manufacturer that peak and sustained power figures are different and that there is a tradeoff if you want full power.
In the Model 3
owner's manual
, Tesla explains that "You can configure Track Mode to improve thermal management of the vehicle over long distances by reducing drive power output as speed increases. Reducing power output improves thermal management, which helps to reduce the rate at which the Battery and motors overheat. Reducing power output leads to slower lap times, but provides more consistent performance and times over multiple laps."
In a manufacturer-organized test, a Porsche had a pre-production
complete 26 consecutive 0–200-km/h runs, with only 0.8 second separating the fastest and slowest. That’s a very small difference, and Porsche attributed it to the vehicle’s cooling and thermal management, which didn’t have to cut power even in such an extreme scenario.
So next time you see a huge horsepower number on an EV, remember that's not going to be your experience most of the time. It's often enough for real-world use case, as you're not running at full throttle all of the time. But if you want sustained horsepower, you might have to dive a little deeper into the specifics of any performance EV you consider.

title: ‘It Feels Like It Can Do Another 250,000 Miles’: High-Mileage Tesla Model 3 Needed Only One Minor Part Replacement
content:
It’s still on its original battery and motors, and it drives like new, even though it spent most of its life as a taxi.
Photo by:
RSymons “RSEV” (YouTube)
10:00am ET
A Tesla Model 3 traveled 250,000 miles in less than five years.
The American EV is still on its original powertrain, and the running costs have been minimal.
A single part needed replacing because it failed prematurely, with the rest of the money going to regular maintenance.
Electric cars are cheaper to run than their combustion-powered counterparts. It’s something that hardcore EV enthusiasts have known for years, and now that more and more people are getting behind the wheel of a battery-powered car for the first time, that knowledge pool is slowly getting bigger.
An EV has significantly fewer moving parts than a gas car, so there are fewer things that can go wrong. (Yes, battery failures happen, but research shows that modern packs, built after 2022, have
a failure rate of just 0.3%
As an experiment,
Richard Symons
, who runs the largest used
showroom in the United Kingdom, bought a second-hand Model 3 that was previously used as a taxi. The idea was to see how a high-mileage EV would perform in the long run, and the results are pretty impressive.
The 2021
Tesla Model 3
Long Range in question recently passed the 250,000-mile mark, but despite the high number on the odometer, surprisingly little has been needed to keep the car on the road.
The front bumper exterior speaker failed prematurely and needed replacing, but other than that, the car only needed regular maintenance. With an average of 150 miles traveled every day, it chewed through six sets of tires, several wiper blade sets, and various bushings.
It’s still on its original battery and electric motors, and the traction battery still has 84% of its original capacity. In the real world, on a nice summer day, it can deliver roughly 284 miles on a full charge, which is still plenty for most people.
When it comes to charging performance and daily usability, the 250,000-mile Model 3 still feels like new. There are no squeaks, no rattles, and it can still hit 60 miles per hour from a standstill in 3.8 seconds. After an 11-minute Supercharger charging session, the battery’s state of charge increased by 30%, and the real-world range increased by 85 miles.
During Symons’ ownership, the high-mileage Model 3 has averaged 4.15 miles/kilowatt-hour, which is very good, though the average speed wasn’t disclosed in the video. Charging the car from solar energy or during the night on cheap electricity also helps keep the costs down.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The original brake rotors, brake pads, brake fluid, and coolant are still there, and the only improvement made to the car is a set of upgraded rear shock absorbers. The originals were still good, but they were swapped for a little bit of extra comfort.
Though it might seem like an outlier, this Tesla Model 3 is certainly not the only high-mileage EV out there. There have been countless stories from owners who have been running their electric cars for hundreds of thousands of miles with minimal problems and costs.
One Tesla owner we spoke to
drives a 160,000-mile 2015 Model S P85D every day, and it still feels like new.

title: Anthropic CEO 阿莫迪称 AI 行业应当放缓发展速度，并承诺让第三方评估机构获得员工级访问权限
content:
9 月 12 日消息，Anthropic CEO 达里奥 · 阿莫迪（Dario Amodei）今日发文，称人工智能行业应当放缓发展速度。
阿莫迪表示，从 2026 年夏季开始，AI 协助构建下一代 AI 的能力快速演进，
不加节制，技术突破速度将彻底超越人类的理解与掌控能力
他提到了 OpenAI 模型入侵 Hugging Face 事件，称这绝非单家公司的偶发事故，类似但较轻微的问题在包括 Anthropic 在内的全行业都曾发生，未来 6–12 个月内更强大的类似集群极可能演变为席卷互联网的僵尸网络并造成灾难性破坏。
阿莫迪称放缓并不等于彻底停滞，而是利用争取来的 1–2 年窗口期，将资源投入到以下四个关键领域：
解决因复杂基础设施、强化学习环境过滤缺陷等执行失误带来的安全漏洞，建立媲美民航工业级别的工程标准；
确保安全合规训练能够跟上模型能力的扩张，消除偶发且不可预期的违背意图行为；
提升类似于“模型大脑 fMRI”的内部机理探查技术，深挖模型未言明的隐性动机；
开发更强大的评测基准，防止高智能模型伪装对齐或欺骗安全检测。
Anthropic 将向第三方评估机构提供针对其系统的永久性、员工级别的访问权限
，使评估人员能够监督 Anthropic 安全措施的执行情况、报告相关事件，并评估模型在训练过程中的对齐表现。
IT之家注意到，据彭博社本周报道，OpenAI 正在考虑放缓尖端 AI 的开发速度，该公司 CEO 萨姆 · 奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）希望其他 AI 公司也能采取同样的做法。

title: Counterpoint 预测：2026-2030 年折叠屏手机面板出货将增长 74%
content:
IT之家 9 月 12 日消息，根据 Counterpoint 最新报告，预计 2026 年至 2030 年，折叠屏智能手机面板出货量将增长 74%，对应约 15% 的复合年增长率（CAGR）。增长将日益集中于大折叠和多折叠产品。
该机构称，预计 2026 年至 2030 年，大折叠面板出货量将增长 79%，份额由 81% 升至 84%；多折叠面板出货量预计增长 179%，份额由 2.8% 升至 4.5%；翻盖式面板出货量预计增长 27%，但份额将下降约 4 个百分点至 12%。
以 2026 年仅在下半年形成的出货量为基数，预计到 2030 年苹果出货量将增长 167%，品牌份额提升约 15 个百分点至 42%。三星出货量预计增长 27%，但份额将降至 24%；华为出货量将增长 3%，份额降至 15%。三大品牌的合计份额预计下降约 5 个百分点至 81%。
2026 年上半年的数据进一步确认，出货重心正从翻盖式面板转向大折叠面板。整体出货量同比下降 13%，其间大折叠面板出货量同比增长 35%，翻盖式面板出货量同比下降 62%。第二季度出货量较第一季度增长 85%，但仍比上年同期低 16%，表明截至年中，复苏仍不均衡。
全年预测取决于下半年项目的执行情况，预计该期间出货量同比增长 71%。苹果和三星新品上市预计将推动出货爬坡，使市场在 2026 年恢复增长，增幅达到 23%。预计到 2030 年，出货量将较 2026 年进一步增长 74%，主要由大折叠面板持续增长及多折叠产品增速加快所带动。

title: 中国聚变：正全力推进全球首个高温超导强场稳态燃烧实验平台研发
content:
IT之家 9 月 12 日消息，9 月 11 日，2026 浦江创新论坛成果发布会在上海张江科学会堂举行。中国聚变能源有限公司（以下简称“中国聚变”）总工程师钟武律作为青年科学家代表出席并演讲。
钟武律指出，当前全球聚变研究加速迈向“燃烧”阶段，实现氘氚聚变燃烧等离子体运行，与实现高增益持续燃烧的聚变等离子体之间，仍有根本性的科学门槛需要跨越：要依靠聚变产生的 α 粒子把等离子体维持在上亿度，进入长期自维持、稳定可控的“燃烧”状态。“只有把科学问题搞清楚，工程上才知道往哪走。”中国聚变正全力推进全球首个高温超导强场稳态燃烧实验平台 —— 中国环流四号研发，为解答这一科学之问提供关键支撑。
“从一个好问题出发，向科学最深处走去”，中国聚变将把握高温超导与人工智能两大技术机遇，沿着“实验堆-示范堆-商用堆”稳步推进聚变能开发，用勇攀高峰的决心、久久为功的信心、矢志报国的恒心，把今天的“科学之问”变成明天的“中国答案”。
“中国环流”系列装置由中核集团核工业西南物理研究院（西物院）研发建造，该院成立于 1965 年，是我国最早致力于可控核聚变和等离子体物理研究的专业科研院所。此前已建成三代聚变平台：上世纪 80 年代建成中国环流一号，是我国核聚变领域第一个国家大科学工程装置；本世纪初建成中国环流二号，奠定我国聚变研究从原理探索到大规模装置实验的基础；2020 年 12 月，自主设计建造的中国环流三号（HL-3）建成并实现首次放电，是国内规模最大、参数最高的先进托卡马克装置，也是 ITER 组织在中国的唯一卫星装置。
中国聚变能源有限公司由中核集团联合中石油、上海市、四川省等优势央国企和地方政府注资 150 亿元共同打造，是核聚变能未来产业的实施主体，正依托上海、成都“两地三区”布局推进中国环流四号研发，并牵头建设长三角高温超导技术创新联合体，补齐高温超导磁体工程化、产业化短板。
钟武律为中国环流三号项目总师、中核集团核工业西南物理研究院聚变科学所所长，长期从事磁约束核聚变物理研究与诊断研发，曾入选国家优秀青年科学基金，荣获中国青年科技奖。“燃烧等离子体”指的是氘氚燃料在等离子体中发生聚变反应，由聚变产生的 α 粒子（氦核）自持加热等离子体、维持上亿度高温并进入长期自维持、稳定可控的燃烧状态，这是全球聚变研究从“实验验证”迈向“工程验证”的关键科学门槛。
2026 年 8 月发布的《中国环流四号目标图像》显示，该平台将系统验证聚变复杂环境下 25 特斯拉（T）高温超导强场磁体可靠性，演示聚变堆全域智能控制，实现装置长时间稳态运行。高温超导材料可支撑更高磁场，有助于在更小装置体积内实现更高约束性能，从而缩短聚变堆体积与建设成本。

title: 国家发改委：积极支持大型汽车企业集团开展改革，以市场化、法制化方式推进企业间兼并重组
content:
感谢IT之家网友
9 月 12 日消息，工业和信息化部昨日（9 月 11 日）举行新闻发布会，介绍我国智能网联新能源汽车产业发展有关情况。
国家发展改革委产业发展司副司长邵稷出席发布会，他提到，新能源汽车在取得可喜成绩的同时，我们也认识到，当前产业技术路线仍在持续演进，未来还可能出现新的颠覆性技术，在产品质量安全、资源回收利用等方面还有不少提升空间。
为此，国家发展改革委将会同有关部门，把技术创新摆在更加突出的位置，持之以恒推动产业提质升级。
一是加强部门协同，持续支持企业加强技术研发应用。聚焦新型电子电气架构、全固态电池、汽车操作系统、智能驾驶等前沿领域，支持骨干企业联合产业上下游开展协同攻关，加快突破一批关系产业长远发展的共性技术、基础技术和前沿技术。配合工信部等部门稳步有序开展智能网联汽车准入试点等工作，积极支持行业中试平台和试验验证能力建设，推动创新成果加快应用。
二是强化标准引领，不断提升产品质量安全性能。今年 7 月实施的《电动汽车用动力蓄电池安全要求》等强制性标准，大幅提升了动力电池等安全要求。后续针对动力电池热失控、辅助驾驶安全事故等社会关注焦点，我们还将配合有关部门持续完善标准体系，鼓励行业骨干企业积极参与标准制修订工作，强化产品生产一致性监督检查，真正让消费者买得放心、用得安心。
三是推动组织创新，切实增强行业发展质效。
我们将积极支持大型企业集团开展改革，以市场化、法制化方式推进企业间兼并重组，支持骨干企业有效整合研发、生产等资源，避免在产品设计、技术研发等方面开展同质化竞争
。鼓励各类型企业深入挖掘自身特点，在不同细分市场深耕细作，形成差异化的竞争格局，不断促进产业从规模扩张向提质增效转变。
四是深化国际合作，推动实现更高水平的互利共赢。我们将坚持汽车领域对外开放，鼓励国内外企业在技术研发、标准制定、产业链协作等方面深化合作。支持外资企业继续深耕中国市场，共享我国完备产业链等发展优势，与中方合作伙伴面向全球市场合作开发新能源车型。支持我国车企学习国际企业先进经验，在更高起点上持续提升技术水平，将中国产品、中国技术带到全球。

title: 大众“史上最大”重组的代价：消息称裁员、关厂将烧掉 160 亿欧元
content:
感谢IT之家网友 不一样的体验 的线索投递！
IT之家 9 月 12 日消息，当地时间 10 日，据路透社援引知情人士消息称，大众汽车预计，上周敲定的重大重组协议将带来约 160 亿欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,246.92 亿元人民币）成本，主要用于裁员以及可能关闭部分工厂。
作为欧洲最大车企，大众汽车正推进公司历史上规模最大的重组。面对中国车企竞争、高额关税和产能过剩等压力，大众汽车直言，当前的处境就是一场“关乎生存”的竞争。
根据重组方案，大众汽车将为德国 4 座工厂寻找新的出路，这些工厂将在未来 10 年内陆续面临无车可产的局面。同时，公司计划在此前裁员方案基础上再减少约 5 万个岗位。
知情人士告诉路透社，逐步结束埃姆登和茨维考工厂的生产预计将分别耗资约 10 亿欧元（现汇率约合 77.93 亿元人民币），内卡苏尔姆和汉诺威工厂则预计分别产生约 20 亿欧元（现汇率约合 155.86 亿元人民币）成本。
此外，大众汽车计划预留约 100 亿欧元（现汇率约合 779.32 亿元人民币），用于承担全球最多裁减 6 万个岗位带来的费用。

title: 天龙三号遥二运载火箭完成总装、总测，预计今年第四季度择机复飞
content:
IT之家 9 月 12 日消息，据每日经济新闻报道，天兵科技介绍，公司正按照归零后形成的最新技术状态，稳步推进遥二相关准备工作。
“我们不会为了保成功而去降低火箭性能。”天兵科技火箭研发部副总经理、助理总设计师张建宏认为：“行业仍处在技术持续验证和快速迭代的阶段，机会窗口仍在，这个窗口不是等来的，要靠把设计、试验、验证和质量工作一项项做扎实来把握。”
据悉，目前遥二已经完成总装、总测，预计在 2026 年第四季度择机复飞，具体时间将结合火箭发射窗口综合确定。
天龙三号遥一运载火箭于 2026 年 4 月 3 日在东风商业航天创新试验区执行首飞试验任务。火箭飞行异常，飞行试验任务失利。
据IT之家此前报道，天兵科技昨日发布关于天龙三号遥一运载火箭飞行试验任务的归零情况说明。
官方表示，天龙三号遥一飞行失利原因定位为：飞行中排放的液氧被抽吸到火箭底部引起一级发动机涡轮废气在底部发生二次燃烧，使底部防热裙连接结构处产生烧蚀变形，导致发动机高温燃气进入一级尾舱，引起尾舱内起火，火箭飞行异常。
改进措施经过地面试验验证，可以满足飞行试验要求。经归零专家组质询评议，一致认为：问题定位准确、机理清楚、已完成故障复现、改进措施有效，并进行了举一反三，可以归零。

title: 特斯拉 FSD v15 将提升主动避险能力：更早的危险预测、更快的反应时间
content:
9 月 12 日消息，据外媒 Teslarati 今天（12 日）晚间报道，特斯拉计划在下一次 FSD 重大更新（v15）中加入一系列重要的安全和事故规避功能，进一步提升系统的主动避险能力。
特斯拉 AI 负责人阿肖克 · 埃卢斯瓦米借本周一起险些发生碰撞的事件，提前透露了 FSD v15 在安全方面的升级方向。
当时，一名车主的车辆为了避让从停车场驶出的另一辆车而主动转向。埃卢斯瓦米写道，自己为车主平安而感到欣慰，“FSD v15 将带来
更早的危险预测、更快的反应时间
，以及整体上显著提升的安全性和碰撞规避能力。”
v15 在特斯拉内部被视为一次幅度更大的架构升级，不仅神经网络规模明显扩大，预测与控制之间的联系也会更加紧密。
特斯拉开始在部分 Robotaxi 运营中测试早期版 v15 软件，同时向现有客户车辆推送 Automatic Collision Evasion（自动碰撞规避）等安全功能。即使驾驶员选择手动驾驶，系统
也能在必要时主动介入
综合IT之家此前报道，今年 4 月，特斯拉 CEO 马斯克就曾宣称，FSD V15 版本的安全性将远超人类水平，即便在完全无监督且复杂的场景中也是如此。
早在 2025 年 8 月，马斯克就谈到 FSD V14 版本的驾驶表现将优于人类司机，
而 V15 版本则有望实现比人类驾驶好 10 倍的水平

title: 算力词元贷加速全国推广，支持机房建设、GPU 服务器集群采购
content:
IT之家 9 月 12 日消息，据央视财经今日报道，今年服贸会首次推出“金融 + 科创”的联展模式，让金融机构联合他们所赋能的科创企业同台参展。展台上除了金融产品，还有智能机械臂、运载火箭模型、人形机器人等硬科技，背后是算力贷、算力保、投贷联动等新型金融工具的支持。
针对 AI 企业的“算力词元贷”自 8 月落地后，正加速向全国推广。服贸会上，多家银行发布相关产品。中国工商银行公司金融业务部副总经理胡贤文介绍，“算力基建贷”支持算力机房建设、GPU 服务器集群采购等新型算力基础设施建设，“算力研发贷”解决企业研发投入大、转化周期长的痛点。
中邮金融资产投资有限公司投资业务一部副总经理闫冉介绍，公司今年 3 月份正式成立后，已在新一代信息技术、人工智能等国家重点支持的领域投资了十几个项目，总投资金额已超 50 亿元。
数据显示，7 月末，科技型企业贷款余额 26.9 万亿元，同比增长 17.9%；今年前 7 个月，科技保险为科技活动提供风险保障金额达 7.2 万亿元，同比增长 55.8%。
IT之家注意到，今年以来有多家银行竞推“算力贷”金融产品。例如，今年 5 月，张家港农商银行成功为本地一家公司投放该市首笔 100 万元“算力贷”，该产品采用“基础授信 + 算力券增信”双维度规则，单户基础信用额度最高 1000 万元，配套算力券增信后，固定资产贷款最高可达 5000 万元。
今年 8 月，广东省首个词元经济专项金融产品“Token 贷”的推出引发热议，该产品以企业算力 Token 词元产出消耗、算力服务合约价值、算力业务产生的应收账款、Token 佣金结算量等作为核心授信依据，为企业提供授信额度。
由北京经开区创新推出的“亦企 Token（词元）贷”首批业务在区内落地，这也是全市范围内落地的首批 Token 算力贷。农业银行经开区分行、中信银行经开区支行、兴业银行经开区支行、北京银行经开区分行、民生银行亦庄支行、华夏银行北京自贸试验区高端产业片区支行为经开区多家人工智能产业链企业提供总金额近 20 亿元授信支持。

title: 谷歌完成对创企 Mechanize 的人才收购，旨在补齐自家 AI 编程短板
content:
9 月 12 日消息，据《商业内幕》今天（12 日）凌晨报道，谷歌完成了对旧金山 AI 编程初创企业 Mechanize 的人才收购。
Mechanize 联合创始人塔迈 · 贝西罗格鲁的 LinkedIn 资料显示，他自 8 月起加入了谷歌 DeepMind 部门，另有报道称，Mechanize 十多名工程师也一同转投 DeepMind。
交易财务条款现已公开，据信谷歌此前曾洽谈一笔价值 15 亿美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 100.88 亿元人民币）
的交易，以获得 Mechanize 的技术和人才。Mechanize 今年早些时候
曾以 5 亿美元
（现汇率约合 33.63 亿元人民币）
估值融资 910 万美元
（现汇率约合 6,120 万元人民币）
，目前由吉夫 · 阿萨迪担任 CEO。失去创始团队后，Mechanize 预计仍会继续运营其他业务。
这种交易通常被称为人才收购（acqui-hire）。对谷歌这样的科技巨头而言，这种方式可以
同时获得关键人才和技术
，又不必像正式并购那样接受美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）、英国竞争与市场管理局（CMA）等机构的反垄断审查。
谷歌此前收拢 Windsurf 团队时也采取了类似方式，Windsurf 前 CEO 瓦伦 · 莫汉后来负责谷歌 Antigravity AI IDE。此次加入谷歌的 Mechanize 员工主要从事中期训练，希望借此提升模型实力，在与 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的竞争中取得优势。
Mechanize 此前的技术和工程重点，就是
提升 AI 模型完成软件工程和编程任务的能力
。报道指出，这恰好是谷歌近期
部分模型表现不佳
的领域。除了创办 Mechanize，贝西罗格鲁还拥有 AI 模型测试经验，此前曾联合创立专门构建 AI 基准测试的 Epoch AI。
接下来，这笔人才收购能否帮助谷歌解决 Gemini Pro 模型延期的问题值得关注。如果谷歌继续受阻，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 则可以凭借 GPT-6 Astra、Claude Fable 等模型进一步扩大领先优势。

title: Li Auto replaces CATL cells with its own battery cells - electrive.com
content:
Li Auto is reducing its dependence on CATL and will increasingly rely on in-house developed battery cells in the future. The Li 6, intended for Europe, will also receive the new technology.
Li Auto is gradually switching its model range from CATL to in-house developed battery cells.
Image: CATL
The automaker is reducing its dependence on CATL and gradually transitioning its model range to in-house developed battery cells. The cells are manufactured by Sunwoda. The i6, which is set to be offered in Europe as the Li 6, will also receive the new battery technology.
As reported by
CarNewsChina
, the cells developed by Li Auto are already being used in the L8, L6, and i8 models. The rollout to additional series is expected to expand in the fourth quarter.
For the Mega Home electric van, Li Auto states that stocks of the previously used 5C ternary cells from CATL are almost depleted. New orders will therefore be fulfilled with its own 5C cells, with the first vehicles expected to follow in November.
The new i9 will initially still start with CATL cells and is set to switch to the in-house development as soon as sufficient production capacities are available. The 2026 model year of the i6 will also receive the new 5C battery as well as the similarly in-house developed Mach-Chip. Deliveries are expected to begin in early November.
Li Auto invests in Sunwoda EVB
At the beginning of September, the manufacturer announced an investment of 2.65 billion yuan (approx. $390 million USD) in Sunwoda EVB. Including existing indirect holdings, its stake will increase to 11.17 per cent. Li Auto will thus become the second-largest shareholder.
This collaboration has been in place since 2017
. Li Auto now defines the product specifications and develops cell materials, cell structure, and battery management systems itself, while Sunwoda manufactures the cells. This indicates that Li Auto is withdrawing from CATL as a battery supplier. As recently as April, Li Auto was one of the four largest customers of the Chinese cell manufacturer.
For the European market, this step is particularly relevant for the i6. Li Auto plans to present the model at the Paris Motor Show in October as the Li 6 for Europe and begin sales in the fourth quarter. Unlike in its home market of China – where Li Auto has grown with range-extender SUVs and continues to actively promote the technology – only battery-electric models are planned for Europe.

title: Carbon thermal batteries target cheaper power for US industry
content: GrafTech International, a major manufacturer of carbon and graphite products, and thermal energy storage company Antora Energy are teaming up to develop carbon-based materials for thermal batteries that can store electricity as heat. The companies will develop and supply the materials at GrafTech’s St. Marys facility in Pennsylvania, where eight bake furnaces have been restarted as part of the collaboration.The key difference from conventional batteries is how Antora stores energy. Its thermal batteries convert low-cost electricity into heat and store it inside insulated blocks of solid carbon. The stored heat can later be delivered as industrial heat or converted back into electricity.This makes the system suited to facilities that need large amounts of energy around the clock. Antora says its factory-built modules can serve chemical plants, food producers, steelmakers, data centers and the grid.Carbon stores industrial heatThe carbon blocks and insulation used in the batteries are made by heating lower-purity carbon feedstocks, including petroleum coke and coal tar pitch, in high-temperature furnaces.The approach could create a new market for US carbon materials and industrial byproducts while giving Antora a domestic source for components used in its thermal batteries.GrafTech is expected to use a significant portion of the bake furnace capacity at its St. Marys facility for the collaboration. Eight furnaces have already been restarted, and the companies have hired new workers while planning to add about a dozen more across plant operations, machining and maintenance.“St. Marys has been an important part of GrafTech’s manufacturing footprint since we acquired the facility in 2010, and we are proud to partner with Antora to leverage the facility and our nearly 140 years of experience in carbon and synthetic graphite-based solutions,” said Timothy Flanagan, CEO and president of GrafTech International.The partnership also gives Antora access to carbon materials without relying on supply-constrained critical minerals used by many conventional battery technologies.Thermal batteries target industryAntora’s system is designed to store electricity when it is inexpensive and deliver energy later as heat or electricity. This could be useful for industrial operations where heat is a major part of energy demand.The company says its factory-built modules can be deployed across different applications without the multi-year construction timelines associated with some large energy projects.The collaboration follows Antora’s $550 million Series C funding round announced in July. In May, the company announced the commissioning of Project Big Stone in South Dakota, which is already delivering round-the-clock energy to POET, a major US biofuel producer.For GrafTech, the deal provides another use for its carbon and graphite manufacturing capabilities, while Antora gains a domestic source of materials as it works to scale its thermal battery technology.“By partnering with GrafTech to source carbon-based materials from their St. Marys facility, Antora is strengthening our domestic supply chain,” said Andrew Ponec, co-founder and CEO of Antora Energy.The two companies have signed a memorandum of understanding and intend to negotiate definitive agreements for the collaboration. The final agreements remain subject to negotiated terms and conditions.

title: China mysterious WZ-X drone spotted in clearest view yet
content: New images are circulating that appear to show China’s latest American B-2 “Spirit” looking stealth drone, the “WZ-X.” Snapped at an unknown location and date, the images appear to show some interesting features of the aircraft.These new images come only a few months after other tantalizing images of the drone were released back in August this year. Those particular images showed the drone from the rear, revealing information about its landing gear, rear rudder setup, etc. The new images confirm some other important features, like its overall shape. From the images seen, it has what appears to be a “serrated trailing edge,” meaning the back edge of the wing isn’t a simple straight line. Rather, it is more of a zig-zag, almost sawtooth pattern, much like the B-2 “Spirit.” On stealth aircraft, designers try to align edges at specific angles so radar energy reflects away from the transmitter rather than straight back at it. The jagged rear edge can also help conceal things like control surfaces and exhaust features from radar.WZ-X spotted again in the airThis feature alone reinforces the belief that this new drone is, indeed, stealth-capable. Analysts believe drones like this could be used to operate deep inside “contested airspace” much like stealth aircraft do today.For what purpose is not known, but likely it would collect important data and images before returning. That would make it conceptually closer to the role of something like the US RQ-170/RQ-180 family than a conventional MQ-9 “Reaper.” The latter isn’t particularly stealthy, but something like this would be designed specifically to survive where a Reaper probably couldn’t.The enormous flying-wing shape also makes sense for reconnaissance missions. A flying wing offers lots of fuel capacity, long endurance, room for sensors, and, critically, a relatively low radar cross-section. While not obvious from images, analysts believe the drone would also come with synthetic-aperture radar, electronic-intelligence receivers, infrared/optical sensors, or communications-intelligence equipment aboard. However, what exact electronics and sensor packages are onboard are just speculation at this point.Another interesting thing to note about the recent batch of images is that the drone was test-flown during daylight. That indicates that China is more than comfortable flying its new drone around during the day.Flown during the dayImportantly, people can more easily photograph it, meaning it might no longer be a super-rare prototype making occasional secret test flights. If true, this could indicate that the program could be moving toward a more mature flight-test phase.But there’s an important caveat here. The “WZ-X” isn’t an official designation, and the photos themselves haven’t been independently authenticated. So we know much more about what the aircraft looks like than about what it can actually do.If this truly is a planned “stealth” drone, bigger strategic significance is what China plans to use the drone for. For example, it could potentially scout ahead of Chinese bombers or missiles, locate ships, map air-defense radars, intercept communications and provide targeting information without risking a pilot.That’s why analysts care about it; it could be part of the sensor network that makes China’s long-range weapons much more useful, rather than simply being an exotic spy plane.

title: China's J-50 fighter could fly itself if pilots pass out in combat
content: Chinese military aircraft researchers are exploring flight-control systems that could keep future fighters flying if pilots become incapacitated.The concept would give aircraft greater autonomy during combat. It could also help them navigate without satellite signals and coordinate with unmanned wingmen.Researchers at the Shenyang Aircraft Design & Research Institute outlined the approach in a recent study. The institute is linked to the development of China’s next-generation aircraft, including the aircraft commonly known as the J-50.The paper does not name the J-50 or confirm that it will receive the proposed systems. Instead, it offers a rare look at the engineering direction China is considering for future combat aircraft.Flight control moves upThe researchers describe a shift from conventional flight control toward what they call “cognitive manoeuvrability.” Modern flight-control systems already handle much of the work involved in keeping fighters stable. Future systems could take on a larger role in managing aircraft behavior during combat.Software could translate broad tactical instructions into flight commands. The aircraft would also monitor its own condition and available performance.That could become particularly useful when pilots face extreme workloads. The system could assume control if a pilot becomes unable to fly.The researchers still want strict limits around autonomous control. They argue that conventional systems should remain responsible for the most safety-critical functions.“The functional positioning of the flight control system is undergoing a fundamental restructuring,” Zhang Dong and his colleagues wrote. They envision intelligent software operating farther from the aircraft’s core control loops. That software could help optimize trajectories and coordinate aircraft.The architecture reflects a major problem with autonomous flight. Data-driven systems can be difficult to verify across every possible situation.Fighters could navigate without GPSThe paper also addresses operations in environments where satellite navigation becomes unavailable. Military forces increasingly treat GPS denial as a serious battlefield problem. A fighter operating under heavy jamming could need an independent way to establish its position.The researchers propose combining several navigation techniques. Quantum inertial navigation could work alongside visual references and terrain-based positioning.Geomagnetic navigation also appears in the proposed architecture. Multiple sensors could help prevent one disrupted system from compromising the aircraft’s navigation. The study does not claim that China has already deployed quantum navigation on a fighter. It presents the technology as an area requiring further engineering work.Drone formations could reorganizeThe researchers also envision crewed fighters working with autonomous wingmen during combat. Unmanned aircraft could receive different assignments during a mission. The drone formation could then redistribute those responsibilities if one aircraft becomes unavailable.A dynamic “virtual leader” could replace a lost command aircraft. That would allow the remaining platforms to continue operating without relying on one permanent leader.The concept could eventually link several classes of aircraft into one combat network. China’s J-36 and J-50 are both candidates for its next-generation fighter force, though neither aircraft is confirmed to use these systems.The researchers recommend extensive simulation and flight testing before intelligent software handles more sensitive functions. They also suggest using lower-cost uncrewed aircraft during early trials.The paper was published in the peer-reviewed journal Aircraft Design in August.

title: Google signs long-term deal for 50% of Finland’s Loviisa nuclear power
content: Google has signed a long-term power purchase agreement with Finnish energy company Fortum that will secure electricity from the Loviisa nuclear power plant through the middle of the century, providing financial support for the facility’s planned lifetime extension.The agreement covers up to 50% of Loviisa’s capacity and comes as Google prepares to invest €13 billion ($15 billion) in data centers and supporting infrastructure in Finland during 2027 and 2028.The power purchase agreement will begin in 2028 at a reduced capacity before covering 50% of the plant’s output from 2030 through 2049.Google backs Loviisa’s life extensionLoviisa consists of two VVER-440 pressurized water reactors. Unit 1 began commercial operation in 1977, followed by Unit 2 in 1981. The plant currently supplies more than 10% of Finland’s electricity.In 2023, the Finnish government extended Fortum’s operating licenses for both reactors through the end of 2050. Fortum is now undertaking an investment program of about €1 billion to extend the plant’s operating life. The company said around 80% of the projects required for the extension, representing approximately €700 million, still lack investment decisions.According to World Nuclear News, the agreement with Google is intended to provide a predictable revenue stream that can support those investments. The deal also supports additional generating capacity at Loviisa. A 38 MWe capacity increase is already underway and is expected to be completed in 2028, while the agreement is expected to enable another 10 MWe increase.Fortum said keeping the reactors operating for the coming decades would help maintain fossil-free electricity generation while supporting the resilience of Finland’s electricity grid.Data center demand meets nuclear powerThe agreement comes as Google expands its Finnish infrastructure, including its data center in Hamina. Google said maintaining Loviisa’s nuclear generation would help preserve access to reliable and affordable electricity for Finnish households, businesses and industry. The company also said it would work with Fortum to explore potential opportunities for new nuclear reactors at Loviisa.The two companies have separately signed a memorandum of understanding covering potential cooperation on new nuclear power, renewable generation and electricity-system flexibility.That collaboration highlights a growing challenge for technology companies: expanding data centers and AI services require large amounts of reliable electricity, while companies are increasingly seeking low-carbon sources that can provide power around the clock.Google and Fortum are also exploring flexible power solutions. As part of that effort, Fortum has agreed with Google to optimize a 94 MW battery storage system planned for Google’s data center in Kajaani.The companies are additionally examining potential business models for new nuclear generation and whether Fortum-owned sites with grid connections could support future Google data centers.Fortum has previously said that new nuclear projects would require strong customer demand secured through long-term power purchase agreements, strategic partners, appropriate financing and risk-sharing arrangements.The latest agreement therefore goes beyond securing electricity for Google. It could help provide the long-term commercial certainty needed to keep Finland’s existing nuclear capacity operating while the country considers how to build additional low-carbon generation for rising electricity demand.

title: Laser-made optical isolator cuts reflected light 95% on silicon chips
content: A new optical chip technology from Kyocera and Tohoku University could help solve a growing problem in high-speed data centers by cutting back-reflected light by about 95 percent.The technology integrates an optical isolator directly onto a silicon photonics chip using laser annealing, a process that heats only a targeted area instead of exposing the entire chip to high temperatures.That matters because optical isolators prevent light from traveling back toward the laser source. Reflected light can interfere with the laser and degrade the performance of optical communication systems.As AI workloads push data centers to move increasing amounts of information, silicon photonics is being developed to provide faster and more energy-efficient connections. The technology uses light rather than electrical signals to transmit and process data.Laser heating solves integrationOptical isolators commonly rely on magneto-optical garnet, a crystalline material that needs to be heated to around 600 degrees Celsius or higher to develop the properties needed to suppress reflected light.Heating an entire silicon photonics chip to that temperature, however, can damage its electrodes, wiring, and other components. Kyocera and Tohoku University addressed the problem by directing a near-infrared laser only at the section where the isolator is being formed.The laser was focused on an area measuring roughly 700 by 700 micrometers. This localized heating crystallized the magneto-optical garnet without exposing the surrounding silicon photonics circuitry to the same thermal load.The approach could make it easier to integrate optical isolators with compact optical circuits and Co-Packaged Optics, or CPO. CPO places optical and electronic components within the same semiconductor package, reducing signal paths and potentially lowering signal losses and power consumption.For optical links, keeping light moving in the intended direction becomes increasingly important as systems become smaller and more tightly integrated. A directly fabricated isolator could therefore remove a key integration hurdle for compact photonic circuits used in future high-speed networks.Chip blocks optical interferenceThe researchers fabricated an optical isolator on a silicon waveguide and tested how well it could distinguish between light traveling forward and light reflected backward.The device achieved an isolation ratio of 13.6 decibels in the optical communication wavelength range. According to the researchers, this corresponded to an approximately 95% reduction in back-reflected light.Electron microscopy also showed that the laser-treated magneto-optical garnet had crystallized properly over the silicon waveguide, supporting the operation demonstrated in the experiment.The result builds on earlier work by Kyocera and Tohoku University to develop optical isolators that can be integrated directly onto optical circuits.The companies now aim to improve the technology by reducing optical losses, increasing efficiency, and making the process more suitable for mass production.If those improvements are achieved, directly integrated optical isolators could become useful in future high-density optical systems, particularly as data centers adopt more silicon photonics and CPO to handle growing AI-related workloads.The research was published in IEEE Access.
